rationale: A prompt becomes labelled HTML/CSS/JS sections and 'the model genuinely determines the resulting artifact', parsed into three mutable source strings shown in an iframe and packaged as a ZIP. Mutation penalized: no evidence for AI in-place iteration on an existing page ('no project database or version store is present'), so revision semantics are unproven.

svg-infographic 'computes a layout, writes structured SVG, lints the source before rendering, and exports a 2x PNG', with the SVG as editable authority and a deterministic validation contract (containment, connectors, CJK). Mutation scored 4 only: the skill can be re-run to revise SVG source, but direct in-place edit of an existing infographic is not evidenced; semantic correctness still needs human/agent review ('no evidence for in-place AI mutation').

A creative agent maps template/prompt to canvas objects preserved through canvas saving services and SQLite/Supabase adapters, with reusable templates and migration-tracked metadata ('Template records and migration history make campaign structures reusable'). Mutation scored 4: agent tooling adds/manipulates canvas objects but no explicit in-place AI editing of existing work is evidenced; live collaborative deployment was not exercised, capping delivery.

With Resolve Studio the MCP 'inspects and mutates the open native project' via the scripting API (media pools, timelines, markers, LUTs, render jobs), and without it materializes FCPXML/EDL/marker/LUT/mix artifacts; mutating workflows return dry-run plans and require confirmation. AI proposes creative edits but deterministic engines (beat grid, color, loudness) own facts and may flag 'needs_human', so authority and human-loop are gated at 7.

A short prompt or source pack becomes a brief, evidence-aware narrative and visual contract routed to editable PPTX, native HTML or PDF, with visual QA covering contrast, typography, crop integrity and topology. Mutation scored 4: routing produces distinct artifact authorities per format, but no direct in-place AI revision of an existing deck is evidenced in the dossier; benchmark depth is proven for the HTML route only.

Design is an optional stage where the user-confirmed brief outranks generated visual references; canvas refreshes 'update text in place and preserve user-arranged layout', so AI does mutate the editable board. Authority is capped because 'visual concepts remain communication assets' decided by the human brief, and delivery is a handoff (proto-plan executable file) feeding an implementation stage rather than the final product.

The editable block graph is 'the same object across visual authoring, conversational modification, execution, deployment and monitoring', persisted alongside deployment, execution and collaboration records, and 'execution interprets the graph rather than prompting from a screenshot'. Conversational/visual/code construction means AI mutates the persistent graph directly, and errors/deploy versions/reverts reach real consumers; human authorship of workflows keeps authority at 7.

The extension deterministically reads computed signals and normalizes them into DESIGN.md/SKILL.md generators with 'no AI model during generation' involved in the product; it 'does not edit the source website or become a canvas'. As a bridge it rates 1 on authority and mutation per rule 6, and delivery is an intermediate governance artifact for another agent rather than a shipped result.

Current Bolt turns prompts, files, templates, Figma frames or repositories into a JavaScript application and iterates through chat, rendered-element Select, Code View and GitHub; the historical MIT tree proves streamed file/shell actions writing project source. Human still chooses platform/model, presses explicit Publish/Update and owns Git merges, so human_loop is 8 rather than 10; closed storage/diff semantics penalize nothing further at this evidence ceiling.

OpenRouter creates or revises one complete HTML page stored as latestCode in MongoDB with deployment metadata; 'later prompts include current code and replace latestCode after a successful parse', which is whole-document regeneration-with-context rather than fine-grained in-place editing (mutation 6). Artifact is durable but the snapshot has 'no durable historical version collection', and delivery stops at code export/deployment tracking.

The agent reconstructs vectors by measuring silhouette/color, constructing paths and rendering back to pixels, and 'iterates on vector geometry rather than painting over the preview', with svg_audit rejecting embedded rasters — direct mutation of the SVG authority. Delivery is 6 because the skill produces exportable SVG evidence of high similarity on specific assets, not a bounded general guarantee.

Typed React Flow nodes and ordered edges determine how generation jobs compose and provider services execute the graph; the human authors the workflow and AI only executes nodes, so authority and mutation are low (no evidence AI edits the graph). Project save/sanitize keeps the graph durable and generator outputs deliver media, but node-canvas remains 'a graph authoring product, not a count for every provider adapter'.

The library lets an external agent assemble a traceable engineering analysis from domain data, calculation and integration skills, but 'Python examples and third-party solvers perform deterministic computation' and the library 'does not own a common geometry model or project database'. AI authors analysis by composition rather than by direct iteration on a persistent design artifact (no evidence for mutation), so authority/artifact stay low.

One agent skill produces prototypes, browser decks, editable PowerPoint, motion, infographics and critique with format-specific renderers; 'the advisor generates at least three materially different directions, then waits for a choice', so AI authors the content but human choice is a first-class gate. Mutation is 6: review sheets and critique reports guide refinement, but direct in-place editing of an existing deck is not detailed in the dossier.

The canvas exposes structured block/project state to an agent and 'the editor applies those operations to the same block graph a human selects and moves', so AI directly mutates the persistent graph via typed operations. Delivery is capped at 5 because this is 'a working AI visual-editor starter' rather than a shipped product, with no evidence of a fuller user loop beyond the forkable demo.

A native macOS workflow canvas where SwiftData persists the graph and Coordinators traverse edges to craft typed handoffs; the human authors the canvas and provider services make live LLM/MCP calls, so AI executes rather than authors the design (no evidence AI edits the graph). The product is 'closer to a local agent IDE than a hosted no-code SaaS' with no shared deployment, capping delivery at 5.

Canvas context is visible to the LangGraph agent and generated media 'returns as manipulable canvas elements rather than a detached gallery', with explicit inspect-canvas and manipulate-canvas tools mutating the composition. Supabase migrations separate project, canvas, chat, thumbs and screenshots into durable clocks; delivery is 6 because no paid provider job was run to prove end-to-end media delivery.

A PRD-gated multi-agent builder where a structured prdAgentAction/generateApp token gates initial generation, then LUI/GUI/code edits mutate the generated app and AI inspection triggers repair; delivery covers hosted release, packages, custom domains and source ZIP. Human gates (PRD confirmation, explicit publish) hold human_loop at 7; the closed generator core prevents rating authority/mutation above 8.

AI patch editing is real: the server adds a SEARCH/REPLACE contract to Gemini and 'AI and manual work converge on one source map' via the same writeFile/HMR path as Monaco. The professor defines governance, locked source, model and rubric and the student drives the session (authority 5, human_loop 4), while submission records persist final files, grading and prompts but are 'not editable project versions' (delivery 6).

A product description is divided into brief, tokens, components, pages and review commands; figma-init writes a design brief the user reviews, then Figma Plugin API execution 'materializes those decisions in the active file' as native variables and nodes. The reviewer agent inspects rather than accepting command completion, so AI authorship and mutation of the persistent Figma artifact are strong while the human brief gate and host OAuth keep human_loop at 6.

The bridge hosts figma_write, which runs bounded JavaScript 'to create or change editable nodes' in the native Figma graph, plus read/token tools, so the host coding agent directly mutates the persistent Figma document (mutation 9). Authority is 6 because the product supplies the transport/operation layer while the hosted agent authors the actual design; Figma owns persistence and delivery, so the bridge's own delivery is 6.

AI-authored fictional worlds persist as PostgreSQL universes, entities and relationships, with agent services creating additional lore/quests through application and MCP routes while the React Flow graph is an exploration projection. Authority is high because AI authors the model content, but mutation is 6 (agents append/create content; in-place restructuring of existing entities is not explicit) and delivery is 6 (a working app surface, not a publish pipeline).

A project manager coordinates an architect and operator so 'one agent' does not inspect, mutate and approve its own work; the operator builds Webflow DOM/classes/styles in small MCP chunks and the architect approves or records corrections, with a mandatory session handoff and explicit user approval gate before host mutation. AI agents author and directly mutate the Webflow implementation, but the mandatory human approval and separated duties hold human_loop at 5.

An agent writes a time-addressable HTML/CSS motion composition that is linted, inspected, browser-previewed and rendered deterministically to MP4; 'source correction -> re-render' is the iteration loop, so AI authors and revises the persistent HTML project. Delivery is 7: MP4 is a delivery projection while versioning remains ordinary Git/filesystem rather than an evidenced hosted design graph.

Human-authored workflow graphs move through optimistic revision-aware editing into immutable versions executed by a registered graph engine, with recovery, traces and multiple delivery surfaces (portal, API, webhook, schedule, MCP). AI executes inside nodes rather than authoring or directly editing the graph (no evidence of AI mutation), so authority 4 / mutation 3; the durable versioned artifact and delivery breadth carry the score.

Deterministic extraction of computed styles and interactions with no AI model called during extraction; normalization feeds generators for DESIGN.md, tokens, preview and coverage, and 'the tool does not write back to the source website'. As a deterministic bridge it scores 1 on authority and mutation (rule 6), delivering an evidence bundle for later agents rather than a shipped design result.

Several workers mutate isolated Git-worktree copies of a real project under leases, render them as live alternatives, and 'commit variant' applies the selected worker delta to the user's working tree; fresh runs materialize static or Vite projects with shared node_modules. Durable variant manifests and a private tree store persist exact tree refs, while the human picks the winner and owns Git/PR/publish, keeping authority and human_loop at 8/7.

The agent proposes a todo plan for confirmation, then generates structured Specs feeding flows, UI screens and a prototype in one managed project; 'later visual choices remain connected to a product model rather than a single prompt' and iterative agent plus direct refinement is the loop. Handoff to Figma, GitHub, HTML or ZIP is explicit multi-authority materialization, with no evidence of continuous three-way sync keeping mutation at 7.

A skill-routed agent workflow where 'the agent can propose and transform RTL' while synthesis, simulation and acceptance tooling remain the numerical authority, and Partition-Opt-Merge recombines focused edits before verification; workspace files carry RTL and verification outputs between stages. Delivery is 6 because verification/synthesis/physical-design ambitions are partly unpublished ('does not support claiming a complete public RTL-to-GDS implementation').

A Copilot CLI canvas where agent-facing actions load/update a per-canvas artifact rendered via loopback server, source edits rerender views and a color picker maps back into the displayed markdown before re-running lint/contrast — AI/agent directly mutates the working design-system artifact. Authority is 5 because it inspects and corrects an existing design document rather than authoring it from intent, and saving back to the repository is an explicit later action (delivery 5).

Claude Code orchestrates a filesystem-governed production line over brand guidelines, tokens, CSS, HTML/SVG/PPTX and organized asset directories; Gemini and MiniMax scripts generate or analyze media and token validators/asset checks 'return defects to the workflow'. Mutation is 6: validation feedback loops drive corrections, but direct in-place AI editing of existing assets is not detailed; durable, reopenable filesystem artifacts and real asset deliverables carry the higher dimensions.

AI turns a short business interview into a complete Next.js project under site/ ('the agent builds source under site/'), so generation is the authoring axis. Revisions are applied to the existing generated project ('the user reviews the actual page, asks for revisions'), the durable source tree is the artifact, and delivery closes with an optional Vercel deployment plus user-retained source. Penalized slightly on human_loop because four intake rounds plus plan approval and deployment authorization are deliberate human checkpoints.

The SKILL.md lets an agent create a DESIGN.md from a brief or repository scan and its scripts scaffold, lint/diff and preview the design document, giving the agent real authorship of a structured YAML-frontmatter artifact. Mutation is capped because 'there is no hosted editor or automatic write-back' and dmd.py only lints/diffs/exports while files and Git own recovery. Delivery reaches materialized HTML preview and exported CSS/token JSON but not a shipped design product.

An in-product assistant can draft and run a workflow while the user inspects 'what the model sees,' edits the graph and tests before publication, so AI co-authors the workflow design rather than wholly owning it. The workflow.json schema is a durable, structured graph contract backed by versions, evaluations and traces, and delivery spans run API, MCP, email and web widgets. Mutation of existing workflows by AI is only weakly evidenced (drafting is primary), so mutation is scored 5.

A vision model infers typography, color, spacing and radii from a screenshot into an approximate DESIGN.md ('URL -> browser screenshot -> vision-provider inference -> approximate DESIGN.md'), so AI authors the reconstructed design system. Mutation is one-shot: 'user correction of the file' is manual and the document only becomes authority after review, with files/Git providing persistence. Delivery stops at a previewed design document and does not reach a shipped product.

Reframe compiles brief/HTML/blueprint into an INode SceneGraph and the embedded agent and reframe_edit tool directly mutate that persistent graph with audit auto-fix, making AI a primary author and editor of the design. The .reframe project layers project.json, scene JSON, ops.jsonl history, components and brands as durable structured artifacts. Penalized for partial operation-history replay, best-effort non-atomic saves and a CLI whose documented commands are not implemented; delivery covers ten export routes including HTML, React and bundle.

Hemy reads project context and routes fashion operations such as sketch-to-render, render-to-technical-flat and fabric/color replacement, so AI generates and edits renders from references. The shared canvas library tags and versions assets, but evidence is architecture-level and inputs are JPEG/PNG, so the artifact is a versioned image library rather than a parametric model and internal schema/version graph are closed. Delivery reaches technical flats and commerce imagery, while tech-pack automation remains unshipped future.

The skills route domain reasoning and run deterministic Python calculators, generating BIM templates and fabrication specs, but 'the package is not a unified visual editor and does not persist a native model itself,' so AI shapes guidance rather than owning the design. No evidence of AI editing an existing persistent design model; outputs are handed to the user's chosen CAD/BIM authoring tool. Delivery is limited to templates/specs that feed downstream tools, and the human operates the authoring environment.

Multi-provider model output streams into the same vector scene humans edit (stream-parser.ts), so AI generates directly into the durable project that persists through project-manager.ts with layers, symbols and multi-page structure. Streamed scene mutations plus direct node edits and full undo/redo make AI a co-editor of the persistent artifact rather than a one-shot generator. JSX/SVG/HTML/PNG exports are deliverable but are independent materializations with no round-trip back into the project.

The canvas is a human-authored graph-authoring interface over an event-driven runtime; no evidence that AI authors or mutates the workflow graph, and code generation is only a downstream projection ('emit a summary and Python representation'). The serialized graph models plus SQLite WAL event store and checkpoints are durable structured artifacts. Delivery compiles authored graphs into a working runtime, but authorship and iteration remain manual, so authority and mutation are 3.

Four role-separated agents move a brief through discovery, concepts, high-fidelity screens and implementation with product design using Figma as native authority and an executor receiving bundles for architecture/backend/frontend, so AI authors the design and code. Figma graphs, design-system knowledge and memory directories are durable structured artifacts, and the pipeline reaches executable implementation. Human checkpoints separate design approval from construction, which is why human_loop is 5.

Concurrent generation agents execute document and node operations against the .op JSON AST, and the canvas synchronizer keeps the Skia projection in sync with the document store, so AI both authors and iterates the persistent design artifact with Git-backed diff/recovery. Mutation is strong because agent tools and parsers update the shared graph rather than returning disconnected mockups. Delivery spans many framework exporters (React, HTML, Vue, Svelte, Flutter, SwiftUI, Compose, React Native), with fidelity noted as target-specific.

Aura is a LiteGraph canvas where the human authors the workflow; the backend only reconstructs and executes the drawn dependency graph, and no evidence shows AI writing or editing the graph itself. The serialized graph JSON is a durable structured artifact with named file persistence, but there are no users, versions or run ledger, and the API connector is an explicit timed mock with a silent Gemini-to-mock fallback. Delivery executes workflows but is transitional, so authority and mutation score 3 and 2.

Dealer and palette scripts generate candidate mocks across aesthetic axes while preserving user-pinned taste, and a build agent turns an approved mock into committed repository source, so AI generates candidates but the human gates each of four stages (research, plan, mock sign-off, build). Repository files and Git remain authoritative durable artifacts. Mutation is moderate because the visual critic and detector review renders rather than directly patching existing source, and browser pixels are evidence only.

Autodesigner 2.0 generates multi-screen projects and modifies existing selections by native object id, returning add/modify/delete commands ('createDesignFromText... selectedNodeIds'), so AI directly mutates the hosted prototype graph. The prototype is a durable structured artifact (screens, native objects, interactions, brand kits) though autosave is not version history and themes are materialized patches rather than live token bindings. Delivery is deliberately plural and lossy: static/PDF/SVG and one-component React/CSS forks, but no whole-project runnable export.

FigML does not call a model on the user's behalf; it deterministically exports selected Figma frames to XML and the user manually carries that XML to a chosen assistant, so the plugin itself has near-zero design authority and no mutation of existing work. The XML is a durable grounding intermediate and Figma remains the design authority with the repository becoming a separate implementation authority and no round-trip promised. Delivery relies on the external assistant for code, so the tool covers only a conversion fragment (bridge per rule 6).

AI proposes source/template actions and writes prose from approved results, and 'analysts own SQL and AI writes prose from approved results,' with AiSourceApplyService persisting and transactionally applying actions only past an explicit apply gate; the MCP surface creates/updates reports and can deliver to Sheets/Looker/chat. Persistent TypeORM entities for marts, reports, schedules and run history are durable structured artifacts, though no user-facing branch/commit history is established. Authority is tempered because the SQL/connector definition remains the numerical authority.

The skills execute real multi-step transformations inside the Penpot plugin API — code-to-design-system, Figma migration, system-bound screen design — with a self-critique loop against a score threshold, so AI authors and mutates native Penpot objects. Penpot remains the authoritative editable artifact and every mutation runs in its environment, with recovery depending on the host file and history. Human approval gates (direction card approval) keep human_loop at 5, and delivery is design objects plus screenshots/audits inside Penpot rather than a shipped application.

The first prompt routes through planner/generator/explainer into React source and later prompts call modifier.js, which 'sends that code and the requested change to Gemini 2.5 Flash,' so the model directly edits the current code authority rather than regenerating from scratch. currentCode is the shared input to editor, preview and next modification, with a sandboxed iframe preview. versionStore.js and storage.js persist generated/modified/rollback states to sessions_data.json, so versions survive process restart and delivery is exportable React source plus live preview.

The skill profiles reference sites, captures a moodboard and shot plan, generates assets and 'builds the implementation,' so AI authors the website from explicit direction that itself becomes repository artifacts before code generation. The site source plus retained design artifacts are authoritative and durable. Mutation is scored 6 because iteration is evidenced through screenshot gates and an anti-slop linter comparing built source to decisions rather than a documented direct-edit loop, and delivery closes to a built site with route-level design-system checks.

Design Ruler is a measurement-first verification tool: it returns computed rectangles as JSON, captures screenshots and tints the reference for pixel-offset visibility, but 'never writes application code or decides aesthetic correctness' and the repository remains authoritative, so it has no design authority and no artifact mutation. Outputs are evidence reports rather than durable design artifacts. It covers a check fragment of the loop with an external agent performing source fixes, so this is bridge/tooling at 2.8.

Agentation records human intent as structured annotations, placements and rearrangement proposals ('proposal geometry, not target-source AST nodes') and the external repository remains authoritative, so the tool neither authors nor mutates the design. Its feedback artifact — annotations, sessions, events in SQLite/localStorage — is durable and structured, which is the strongest dimension. Delivery is an intent/context primitive: an external coding agent must perform the actual edits, so the loop covers only a fragment.

An MCP-connected agent creates and modifies UI artboards as HTML where 'HTML/CSS is both what the agent writes and what the canvas renders,' so AI authors and directly mutates the live canvas via MCP/WebSocket operations with in-session undo/redo. Artboards and the .uicanvas workspace are portable, editable artifacts, though no durable multi-user or version-history service is documented. Delivery is saved workspaces or copied HTML rather than a full published pipeline.

The bridge gives an MCP-capable agent broad native write tools — createSection, appendChild, node property assignment, remove, bulk text replacement and override propagation — so an AI coding agent directly mutates the authoritative open Figma document, which is a durable structured artifact owned by Figma. Design authority rests with the external agent using the tools, so authority is 7 rather than higher. Delivery is a control path into the host document with no own store, transaction wrapper or version graph, and recovery falls back to Figma.

Kin3o generates Lottie/dotLottie JSON from prompt, tokens and motion personality, maps emotions to timing/easing constraints and validates with auto-fix, so AI authors the motion design. The refine command 'reads the existing artifact and writes a versioned successor rather than overwriting it by default,' giving strong mutation of the Git-friendly diffable Lottie artifact. Delivery closes with marketplace publish or MP4/WebM/GIF render, with the browser preview treated as evidence.

Azure OpenAI produces structured typed nodes and edges that are auto-laid-out and merged into the existing DiagramData scene, so AI authors editable structured diagram fragments that round-trip through JSON and persist in a Supabase JSONB row. Mutation is capped because 'there is no AI patch protocol for existing elements; subsequent correction is primarily direct manipulation,' and only fifty in-memory history snapshots survive, reset on reload. Delivery is the authored scene and JSON import/export rather than a full published loop.

Built-in skills write ordinary workspace files (HTML/SVG/PPTX) from briefs and the workspace file remains authoritative, with canvasVersions implementing named snapshots/restore and editorReconcile arbitrating agent filesystem updates against local edits, so AI authors and co-edits durable files. Ephemeral widgets are correctly separated from durable workspace artifacts, with model-facing vocabulary generated from the same designSystem constants the renderer defines. Delivery reaches previewable, versioned and rollback-able HTML documents and deck files, with medium human involvement in correction and rollback.

Architecture, file writing, QA and deployment are LangGraph steps where the backend writes model-returned files into the React workspace and 'failed checks route back to the developer node,' so AI authors the app and iterates on its own files through a QA loop. Workspace files remain the shared authority and the event stream only explains state. Delivery closes with a local preview or final deployment URL, giving a full intent-to-deployed loop.

The skills orchestrate code-generated KiCad boards through placement, routing, ERC/DRC and fabrication checks, but the design generation is deterministic Python emitting .kicad_sch and driving pcbnew, so AI authorship is tooling-directed rather than model-authored. KiCad files are diffable, regenerable and checkable, and the workflow iterates routing/verification as separate gates. Delivery reaches fabrication/order preparation and release files, which is substantial, but authority and mutation stay low per rule 6 for deterministic converter workflows.

The editor turns a bounded-box selection plus instruction into a scoped subprocess source edit (codex-edit.js), so a coding agent directly revises the existing slide HTML, and manual direct editing writes the same source so paths do not diverge. HTML slides are the durable, hash-fingerprinted edit authority. The two-pass design gate with a Proceed receipt blocks PDF/PNG/PPTX/Figma export on stale or un-reviewed source, so human review is a hard checkpoint (human_loop 5) and delivery is gated but complete.

The model fills a bounded content schema (eyebrow, headline, description, CTA, three features) and a deterministic renderer owns layout and export, so AI authors the copy/content while layout is fixed and 'arbitrary layout editing and durable projects are outside the current product.' No edit/iteration loop on an existing artifact is evidenced and invalid model output falls back to a local deterministic draft, so mutation is 2. Delivery is a reproducible standalone HTML document from the same SiteDraft fields.

AgentGo generates an HTML deck from a topic and the agent mode patches a selected DOM element via natural language with tag/text/styles/CSS path attached to the instruction, so AI authors and directly mutates the persistent original HTML. Named saves and restores are backend-connected with an e2e version-restore test, and preview/export always use the agent's original HTML rather than the GrapesJS editor model, keeping the durable authority stable. Delivery covers preview, PDF/PPTX and version restore, with PPTX flagged as a lossy conversion projection.

AI Planner interprets an NL edit request and the Applier generates Python that mutates live PowerPoint COM objects and calls presentation.Save(), so AI authors in-place changes to the user's existing deck ("execute generated COM mutations"). The native PowerPoint document remains the durable editable authority. No application-level transaction or undo journal and ambiguous shape targeting mean partial executions and retries still need human verification, so human_loop and delivery are slightly discounted.

A model proposes typed engineering actions validated with Pydantic schemas, and a Fusion add-in executes them into the native parametric document ("validated FusionAction -> local add-in -> sketch/feature mutation in Fusion document"). The action vocabulary is deliberately limited (boxes, cylinders, holes, extrudes, fillets, materials), so it is not full design authorship. The dossier gives little evidence on the human loop or a complete shipped design result, so those dimensions are scored low.

AI generation is a single GPT-4o mini request that replaces the editor's one Mermaid string; it "does not pass current source for targeted revision," so mutation of existing work is minimal (whole-state replacement). The only persistent state is a single local-storage key, so artifact is a lean editor state rather than a managed project. PNG/SVG exports are rendered derivatives that deliver but do not export the editable source.

Built-in assistants create presentations, documents, spreadsheets and web artifacts in a workspace where "HTML changes can move between rendered and code views without leaving the workspace," so agents author persistent workspace files. AionUi itself orchestrates previews while OfficeCLI executes native mutation, so the full artifact mutation loop partly depends on a separate product. Delivery to final native Office output is therefore assessed as orchestrated rather than self-contained.

The model receives the description and current document and returns a complete HTML page that becomes current website state, so AI is the author and can iterate on existing work. Persistence is a file-locked pickle store of per-user sessions with a chat-shaped version trail and restore, which is durable but lacks database-level concurrency or migration semantics. Publish points a share route at the same session artifact rather than a deployment build.

The PPT generation contract moves from style/outline to asset plan, page HTML, per-page review and PPTX export, so agents author the presentation while retaining page HTML as a re-editable intermediate. A visual workbench lets the user select, resize and regenerate slide elements, which is human-in-the-loop element editing rather than full AI iteration. The exported .pptx is the native delivery artifact and an editable deck example is released.

OfficeCLI is the mutation engine: PowerPoint handlers resolve selectors and manipulate native text, fills, tables, charts and animations inside real Open XML parts with an AtomicPackageWriter, so it directly edits the persistent .pptx rather than regenerating it. Authoring authority is exercised by the agents that drive it, and the Morph skill adds design policy on top, so the tool itself is not the design author. The .pptx remains the authority and reopens in ordinary Office software.

First-party architecture describes generating one or three website alternatives from a URL or captured page that are then editable via AI chat and visual editors, with React/Tailwind export. Evidence is architecture-level: the hosted editor internals, revision model and selection protocol are unexplored, so mutation and artifact mechanics are credited from claims and slightly penalized. Delivery to exported code and hosted pages is documented but the code export is a materialization boundary.

Stage-specific director skills drive research through script, assets, timeline and composition while "project manifests, scripts, timelines, assets, checkpoints and decision logs jointly form production authority," so AI authors and mutates a persistent filesystem project. Backlot and delivery-promise gates pause for human approval and block bad renders, matching the review/steer loop. The MP4 is the final delivery projection but all intermediate state is recoverable and auditable.

Framelink is deliberately read-only toward Figma: two tools obtain simplified Figma data and download images, with "no node-creation or mutation tools" and no reverse sync, so it is a design-to-code bridge rather than a design author. The downstream repo becomes the artifact but Framelink does not edit or persist any design state itself. It runs automatically, but it delivers only context, not a shipped design result.

HeroUI's MCP servers and skills extract component docs, source and theme variables so coding agents build UI constrained by the design system; the code packages remain authoritative and nothing is mutated by the product itself. It is agent-facing knowledge infrastructure of a design system, not a system that generates or edits design artifacts. Automatic to query, but it delivers only reference data and an isolated agent surface.

An agent authors typed semantic JSON against a defined skill contract and renderers produce interactive HTML, PNG, SVG, WebM and share-card assets from that IR, so AI authors the model that defines the diagrams. Delta artifacts make change reviewable, but direct iterative mutation of an existing authored model is not strongly evidenced. The structured IR is durable and the delivery contract distinguishes semantic validity from rendered usability.

Pix runs a closed visual correction loop: it implements repository source from Figma reference data, then uses runtime screenshots and computed styles to diagnose differences and correct source repeatedly ("source correction -> repeat"). This is direct AI mutation of the persistent repository artifact, which becomes runtime authority. It remains an instruction package without its own metric engine or comparison history, so delivery is a converged implementation rather than a measured end-to-end product.

Noir.dev persists current project code plus autosaved numbered version snapshots with revert and comparison, and WebContainer projects that code into a preview environment, so generation happens against recoverable project state. AI-authored generation replaces the code artifact rather than surgically editing it, and revert requires the caller to re-apply the version to the current project, which slightly weakens mutation and delivery claims. Deployment and export services consume chosen states.

The B.L.A.Z.E agent discovers installed Blender capabilities and executes natural-language edits against the native scene, with screenshots fed back as visual state, so AI both authors and mutates the canonical Blender scene. Blender scenes and saved .blend files remain the durable authority while WebRTC is only a projection surface. Render and blend-file endpoints deliver the outputs.

Agent skills normalize a captured Figma component into Component Markdown as the durable source of truth, then render selected contract sections back into Figma as annotation frames, so AI synthesizes documentation artifacts. The Figma render is a projection and "edits made only to those frames are not a reverse update," so AI mutation of the design graph is limited to creation of new frames. It delivers documentation rather than a design itself.

The model proposes a typed BuildPlan spanning data, state, behavior, automation and visual pages, and only a validated plan is applied by BuildPlanApplier into durable records, so AI authors and directly mutates the managed application. The GrapesJS canvas is one view of a larger managed project and page revisions preserve visual changes. The validation gate implies human review before mutation, keeping human_loop moderate.

The skill decomposes a working prototype into screens and states, maps elements to the target design system, and writes native frames, instances and annotated flows into Figma through MCP, so AI authors a native Figma design from an implemented prototype. It materializes a new Figma graph rather than mutating an existing one, and the source prototype and Figma remain two authorities with only traceability, not merge. Figma owns persistence after materialization.

The bridge streams live open Figma files to AI clients and exposes a bounded set of native write tools (geometry, text, fills, auto-layout, grouping), so an AI can directly mutate the persistent Figma document, with the native file remaining canonical. The write surface is intentionally smaller than the read surface and lacks transactions, so complete design delivery is limited and the bridge itself does not author the design. Human guards such as delete-confirmation flags keep human_loop moderate.

The agent reads the typed node/edge graph and 'returns graph mutations rather than a diagram screenshot', so AI authors structural architecture changes and can generate a separate spec. The graph is the working artifact: React Flow rendering, Liveblocks presence and autosaved canvas JSON. Mutation of the persistent canvas is evidenced by durable task execution; the spec may lag graph edits and must be regenerated, capping delivery to graph + spec documents. Tutorial-associated repository with no license is noted but does not change the score.

The product performs corrections (text replacement, annotations, redlines, signatures, page ops, OCR) on existing PDFs, so AI is an editor rather than a design author (authority 4). Mutation is excellent and versioned: 'every successful change' routes to a new file in a private version stack and the MCP wrapper 'always writes a new output path, preserving the same non-destructive boundary'. Artifact is the PDF version stack; delivery covers corrected/converted PDF outputs.

GenerativeUI accepts model-written Prefab Python and executes it in a Pyodide sandbox, so AI authors interactive UI within a bounded component vocabulary. Mutation is moderate: generated code is re-executed/streamed and CallTool actions mutate app state, but the authoring authority stays in host-persisted Python ('the embedding MCP server REST application or file project must persist authoritative Python'). The versioned PrefabApp JSON envelope and typed components form a durable structured artifact; delivery reaches a rendered interactive UI with action transport.

An agent conversation generates media whose tools 'calculate placement and add results to the canvas rather than leaving them only in the chat transcript', so AI authors and directly mutates the creative canvas. Canvas and chat state are separate durable SQLite records, making the canvas a strong structured artifact that reopens without replaying the conversation. A human edits the canvas directly and drives the conversation, so human_loop is mid; delivery is the populated local desktop canvas/export surface.

JavaScript source (.fluid.js) is the canonical model and 'visual tools and agents do not edit an opaque duplicate: both work by changing .fluid.js', so agents have solid authoring and direct mutation of the persistent model, with modeling history rollback. The source-plus-feature-history is a durable structured artifact; STEP import/export provides an engineering delivery boundary. Human click-tools and agent edits coexist, keeping human_loop at 6.

The pipeline crawls a live site and classifies computed/interaction evidence ('it does not treat every captured CSS value as a durable rule'), so AI analyzes and extracts a design system rather than authoring new design. It 'does not mutate the sampled website' and Git remains versioning, so mutation is minimal. The produced DESIGN.md, structured tokens, agent instructions, preview and pixel-level proof are durable structured outputs that govern later agent work but do not round-trip back, capping artifact/delivery.

Quilter performs the core PCB design work — searching placement and routing within engineer-supplied physics constraints and generating 'hundreds of alternatives in parallel' — so AI authors candidate layouts. The engineer fixes outline, pre-places connectors and reviews/adjusts candidates, and the hosted result is a candidate rather than a mutated authoritative artifact, so mutation stays moderate. Projects return in native format for DRC/fabrication in the user's EDA tool; the private RL implementation is unverified but the evidenced architecture supports the scores.

AI ranks visual directions from a curated deterministic catalog and produces a first-viewport implementation; 'model output cannot silently invent the catalog identities', so its authoring is bounded but real. Mutation is moderate: the workflow 'first viewport -> inspect and revise' implies iteration but the revision mechanism is not detailed, and previews are candidates rather than versions. The selected DESIGN.md and application source persist as durable artifacts; delivery covers the DESIGN.md handoff contract plus first-viewport implementation.

AI tools operate inside the same editing/color/Fusion project (CineFocus, face tools) and remain adjustable via native controls, with the saved Resolve project authoritative. The human chooses focal subjects, adjusts parameters and keyframes, so authority and automation are low while the native project is a strong durable artifact. AI mutation is limited to parameterized transforms rather than iterative repair; delivery is high as a professional render/publish platform.

Pinned source shows MCP commands read/create/edit/inspect/critique over native Figma nodes with schema-first batches tagged `flaude:dslId`, idempotent upserts and read-back drift classification. Claude via MCP authors and repairs the editable Figma node graph, making this a strong co-editing loop. Hosted server-side schema generation is unverifiable from the open revision but not needed for the core loop.

AI routes propose or repair the editable workflow node graph, and deployment materializes provider-native command/skill files; SQLite retains local project state. Human inspection of sessions precedes automation, so the loop still leans on manual review. The visual graph is a design surface over filesystem authorities rather than a universal runtime, capping delivery.

Agent tool results add/update screen nodes in `useProjectState` while the canvas renders existing screens without flattening them, and the design-agent contract supports a continuing correction path. Human move/select/edit rounds steer the loop. Small codebase and active-transition lifecycle, but the shared screen-node state is a genuine editable multi-screen artifact.

agent.py persists outline/storyboard and generates section-level Manim source, while the critic scopes repairs to line/function/section and re-rendering gives a reproducible path to video. Existing files are loaded on later runs, so artifacts remain inspectable and replaceable. The interaction model is scripted (edit prompts/JSON and rerun), lowering human_loop.

Convey is a runtime-intent relay: the overlay packages visual intent plus element/runtime evidence for a coding agent that edits the actual repository, and reload verifies the result; overlay state itself is temporary. It does not author the design or persist a visual artifact, so authority/mutation/artifact are low. The loop does close intent to verified source change, giving a moderate delivery.

Agent tools create typed design/slides/video artifacts mounted through an artifact panel with a dedicated HTML runtime where the user can continue editing. Session-bound storage and local exports keep this a workbench rather than a portable cross-instance design graph, so artifact and delivery are capped. Design is a first-class editable mode, not universal design authority.

Six skills write generated `.uxm`/`.md`/`.rendered.md` files under the user's `fluxwing/` directory while bundled templates stay read-only, keeping artifacts git-diffable across conversational revision; a validator gates translation to React. The conversational agent authors the low-to-hi-fi design files. Human review precedes translation, so automation is partial.

Prompt and style produce four previews; the user selects one before editable desktop/mobile Figma designs and a linked Dora site project are materialized, with credits separating preview from conversion. AI authors the site design, but public evidence does not establish AI iteration on the established design or Figma-to-project synchronization, so mutation semantics are penalized. Closed implementation and publishable website delivery.

The form schema is the authoring contract and `create` deterministically materializes a runnable agent directory (generated Python, FastAPI, clients, docs); there is no AI generation or iteration. It is a deterministic design-code materializer, so authority and mutation are minimal. Generates a durable, executable filesystem project with a working run path.

The skill runs a staged pipeline from repository discovery to a checked-in `DESIGN.md` source of truth, then tokens/themes/components and Storybook, with quality gates and a readiness handoff. An AI agent executes the design-system build over the user's repository, mutating real project files. Human steers phases and gates; the skill owns the process, not cloud versions.

The MCP contract exposes node discovery, execution and saving/updating workflows with recoverable versions and URL handoff for inspection/correction on the Comfy Cloud canvas; the local server drives a live ComfyUI via `comfy-cli`. As a bridge, it does not author designs itself (an external agent does), so authority is low while saved graphs are a strong durable artifact. Execution and delivery are verifiable.

WhipUI is a routing/context layer: it writes `PROJECT-DNA.md` and fingerprints, routes requests toward installed design intelligence/Figma MCP/Playwright, and coordinates bounded repair iterations, while repository code remains implementation authority. It neither authors nor fully persists the design itself, so authority/mutation/artifact score low. The loop closes to agent-implemented source changes.

PPTX is parsed into a typed scene graph that a conversational planner changes via reviewable ActionPlans; the executor applies, validation/review requests corrections, and a preview-plus-diff with undo precedes PPTX writing. Sessions are process-local rather than durable projects, penalizing artifact longevity. The AI mutates the actual slide artifact through a strong reviewable loop.

First-party alpha docs confirm build and edit verbs against the visible Comfy UI graph from an in-app chat, with the saved graph remaining the artifact authority. Implementation, planning and history semantics are unknown at architecture level, so mutation depth is penalized. Distinct co-located interaction model with strong artifact backing but no explicit publish delivery.

An agent skill interviews the user and a deterministic builder emits a W3C-shaped token ZIP; the Figma plugin performs conflict analysis then creates/synchronizes native collections, modes, variables and styles, with alias ordering and destructive replacement gated by human confirmation. The design-system mutation is real but batch/export-import rather than live co-editing, lowering human_loop.

GPT-4o generates a strict agent configuration the user inspects and edits, stored in localStorage with JSON import/export, then converted into live OpenAI Realtime agents with external tools. The artifact is a portable spec, not synchronized project storage or version history, and AI iteration on existing configs is limited. Fidelity gaps in conversion cap human_loop and artifact.

Agents (Saga/Freya/Mimir) write product briefs, UX scenarios, page specs, design-system work and assets into named `design-artifacts/` subtrees, with signoff separating intent changes. AI authors a staged design-development chain, but external tools retain their own native graphs and no single automatic round-trip is claimed. Delivery is an implementation/delivery package rather than a published artifact.

Gemini turns floor-plan images and briefs into validated structured room/object data, and the copilot translates natural language into add/update/delete operations over the SQL-persisted 3D object model, with failed interpretation preserving the graph. Generation candidates and the editable scene graph are distinct authorities, giving a strong shared-authority loop. No merge/branch model or lossless reconstruction is established, capping delivery.

`frontend-design` routes work, `add-ui` mutates source, and `critique`/`audit` produce evidence for the next pass while existing source/component/token choices take precedence. An agent executes the design refinements directly in the repository, yielding deployable source. The loop relies on agent-driven passes with human review rather than an end-to-end automatic pipeline.

OpenAI returns a bounded pages/sections JSON stored in relational Website/Page records, rendered live, and chat edits update current sections with immutable SiteVersion snapshots. The nucleus is genuinely AI-authored, editable and versioned, but restore, publishing, auth and billing are explicitly unfinished, capping delivery. Deterministic fallback and snapshotting show real artifact discipline.

LLM proposals are normalized into structured nodes/edges that pass deterministic pin/schema repair before joining the MongoDB-stored project graph, and the user can directly move/edit with autosave. Probabilistic reasoning never directly becomes the stored artifact, so the graph stays inspectable. Hackathon-stage workspace; no electrical-rule correctness or branchable history established.

The hosted MCP resolves a design system (semantic tokens, components, review rules) and the agent writes ordinary repository UI then corrects it against accessibility/visual review rules; the open registry pins component JSON and CSS token layers. Application source is runtime authority with no bidirectional canvas. Hosted MCP implementation is closed, so review execution is unverifiable.

The skill demands at least six distinct SVG concepts, writes each to its own file for comparison, and refinement proceeds from the explicitly chosen source, leaving the filesystem as the candidate graph. The winning SVG stays editable in vector tools and scripts derive PNG/mockup deliverables. No embedded model or database; the host agent authors files.

Figma variables are streamed into running clients as CSS custom properties for visual validation, and only a human-controlled CSS export promotes them to repository source; the plugin can write missing WEB custom-property syntax back into the Figma file. It is a candidate-promotion/validation bridge where AI participates rather than owns, so authority is low. Plugin/server source is closed, penalizing evidence for authority and iteration.

The human UI and local MCP bridge share one document schema, command system and semantic query layer, so agent edits commit to SQLite through the same invariants as direct editing, with undo/redo and scene-first documents. The agent authors and mutates a persistent editable scene document plus disk assets. V1 constraints and browser-backed capture limits mark active-transition maturity.

The adapter exposes CRUD over the same FPT/ShotGrid entities artists see and carries review decisions back into that graph via skills, using a pinned `fpt` CLI for transport. It is an agent-facing adapter that mutates a managed production graph rather than creating design media. Authority stays low because the design/coordination work is performed by the connected agent.

converter.py deterministically parses a web-oriented DESIGN.md and emits a presentation-oriented DESIGN.md with safe zones and provenance; there is no deck generation, canvas or render loop. It is deterministic design-code translation with the translated constraint document as the durable artifact. Human invokes the CLI; delivery is only an intermediate file for a later image/slide agent.

The canonical project is structured JSON whose screen bodies are executable Tailwind HTML; geminiService sends the current project plus existing screens for whole-project generation, new screens or targeted refinement, and canvas/preview/refinement converge on the same screen records. Undo/redo and localStorage persistence exist, but server-side branches do not. HTML ZIP export preserves editable source for delivery.

Hugo Chat proposes a site as structured Markdown that the open kit renders through a pinned block schema and reusable Hugo blocks; users then make direct source edits and deploy portably. AI authors the Markdown site, but the hosted generator's prompts, orchestration and revision store are not public, so AI iteration semantics are penalized. Strong artifact portability and deployment delivery.

Claude Agent SDK edits room source/JSON files directly in the project directory with screenshot-verified hot reload, so AI authorship and mutation of a durable artifact are source-pinned ('claude_agent.py', 'CLAUDE.md'). Human plan/build modes and direct canvas edits keep the loop collaborative. Delivery is the live browser scene plus durable project files rather than a hosted publish.

Calino generates raster candidates from selected frames/quality tier and fills frames or builds variant grids in Figma (DALL-E 2/3, GPT-Image-1), giving AI real authorship of image content. Mutation is weak: the AI never edits existing imagery, reinsertion from the 30-image paid history is a new canvas mutation, and history sits outside Figma version history. Delivery is a usable in-Figma fill; fill serialization and batch recovery are undisclosed and penalized.

Streaming generate routes produce complete multi-file React/Next/Astro projects and the agent route exposes correction tools over current project material, showing direct AI authorship and mutation of persistent files (MongoDB Project model, workspace undo/redo). GitHub deployment and hosted deploy branch from accepted project source, closing delivery. Bounded in-memory undo is not a complete server-side archive, a minor artifact caveat.

Gemini creates typed hero/service/product/FAQ/SEO values from a validated business brief into Supabase records, evidencing real AI authorship of site content bounded by the wizard. Mutation is scoped: editor actions update one section/theme/brand color without replacing the whole site, and regeneration is confined to that scope. Publish, JSON roundtrip and static HTML+data ZIP close delivery; AI does not freely iterate across the whole artifact.

Design Mode delegates open-ended visual instructions to the coding-agent runtime while ast-editor performs guarded atomic JSX mutations resolved by stable data-caret-id attributes, so AI edits persistent React source directly ('ai-edit-handler.ts', 'ast-editor.ts'). The .caret design layer and Git are the durable recovery layer, and sync materializes reviewed changes into application source. Delivery is live in-editor preview plus application-source writeback; dynamic JSX falls back to scoped agent editing.

Every Playground is a sessionId-addressed internal Git repository and an authorized agent clones, commits and pushes to change the existing artifact rather than regenerating it; chat, Code tab and visual text edit also alter files. Authority is strong across p2c/l2c/f2c/import ingress, and publish/one-way GitHub push/version history cover delivery. Multi-writer merge semantics and history-to-commit mapping are undisclosed, a bounded artifact caveat.

A multi-agent orchestrator (planner/research/writing/quality/slide-design/image stages) produces structured slides that enter a database-backed editor store, giving AI primary authorship of deliverable content. Mutation is moderate: generation is a pipeline and iteration happens in the human SlideEditor, with no strong evidence the AI re-edits slides already in the store. PPTX/PDF/text export closes delivery.

Vextra MCP is a read-only design-file bridge: it parses local Figma/Sketch/Vextra/SVG files and renders node PNG/SVG images for external agents, with three inspection tools and no write tool. Authority and mutation are therefore 1; the artifact is the host file plus cached/derivative renders. It delivers visual grounding for implementation or checking, not a shipped design result.

The hosted generation record binds brief → preview → HTML and React TSX exports, evidencing AI authorship of a full page/UI from a brief. Mutation is one-shot: no first-party evidence of editing existing output or source round-trip, so mutation is 3. Exported source is a takeaway deliverable; native layer editing, project recovery and collaboration are unverified and penalized.

Inngest conversation tools list/read/create/update/rename/delete Convex file records, so AI directly mutates the persistent project file graph, with CodeMirror as the human direct-edit surface and WebContainer as the preview projection. GitHub import/export is an explicit sync boundary with the Convex project authoritative until remote success. No in-product snapshot/restore ledger exists, a minor artifact caveat.

The pipeline (outline → visual system → page renders → correction) writes project.json, Design Files and numbered page images to disk, and deckVersions keeps immutable project-local snapshots with restore, evidencing AI authorship and mutation of a durable per-slide render artifact. Chat/mark/direct deck operations plus presenter view and PDF/image-backed PPTX export close the loop. Visual-quality claims were treated as product claims, not evidence.

AKO is a deterministic rules-based pipeline (Perceptor/Planner matrices, Pillow mockups) that calls no model, so 'AI authorship' is governed template selection rather than learned design; it still produces icons, theme JSON and PNG assets. Mockup approval gates production and reviewers can demand revision, giving limited iteration, while the output directory is the durable store. Human inspection is a required interactive step, capping human_loop.

The agent in Figma Design creates and edits native layers using the file's real components, tokens and variables, with parallel prompts, chat undo and host-file version history — AI is the direct author and mutator of the shared design file. Humans select, prompt and review on the canvas, so the loop is collaborative though highly automated. Internal transaction/concurrency semantics are undisclosed, penalized only as unknown rather than demonstrated defects.

Deckestra routes new-deck/template-fill/beautification/native-enhancement jobs through deterministic layout with a layout-trace gate, so decks are produced by scripted geometry rather than learned design, capping authority. It delivers editable .pptx with narration/animation preserved, and privacy/provenance gates govern releases. Free-form AI iteration on an existing deck is not evidenced, so mutation is capped.

The metric plan is the single source of truth and the design route parses bounded, schema-validated model operations before applying them, so AI can mutate real plan geometry but only under fixed constraints, with a deterministic basic planner otherwise. Human top-view/block editing drives the plan while Blender compiles it into a walkable 3D result with concept JSON/SVG exports. Authority is deliberately subordinate to deterministic invariants.

QoQo generates structured discovery material (personas, journeys, IA, interview prompts) from a brief, which is clear AI authorship of content drafts. Outputs are copied into Figma as sticky notes with no durable two-way sync, so AI mutation of a shared artifact is absent and Figma becomes the collaborative authority afterward. History schema and exact generation parameters are undisclosed, penalizing artifact and delivery.

Agents mutate real local folders or per-conversation Git worktrees with file/command/browser tools, while plans/diffs/screenshots are review evidence rather than implementation authority — strong AI authorship and mutation across the 2.0/IDE/CLI/SDK/API family. Humans review artifacts, comment on milestones and integrate worktrees, so the loop is review-heavy but not manual. Delivery is the intended Git state and managed-environment export; internal harness planning is closed.

The FreeCAD component reads current documents, applies named property/object edits and re-reads state and views after mutation, so AI directly mutates the persistent parametric FCStd document via object-level tools. Screenshots are feedback while .FCStd retains parametric identity, and STEP/STL/OBJ/DXF/PDF are export outputs. FEM requires an installed solver and valid setup, keeping some human intervention in the loop.

An external coding agent (Codex) reads the repository contract and edits the React/data source directly, while ProductImageEditor saves preview adjustments back into TSX source, so AI and human edits converge on the same artifact with Git as recovery. Audit reports arrive as validated, checkpoint-restorable patches the user applies or ignores. Delivery is print-specific (compressed preview PDF and high-quality print path); no in-app embedded model call exists.

The CLI turns a natural-language request into a .yaml typed-node graph that is both design and executable program, giving AI authorship of the core artifact. Mutation of an existing diagram is human web-editor refinement, not an AI loop; runtime instantiation and GraphQL/MCP edges expose the graph. Delivery is the running multi-agent system, with users required to review topology and runtime permissions before --and-run.

Kanvas is a governed coordination board: agents may propose work, start approved cards and submit for review in the .canvas JSON, but only humans approve or mark review complete — so AI mutates a persistent coordination artifact rather than a designed artifact and holds low authority. Dependency edges auto-block/unblock and Git versions the board. Execution stays in agent CLIs, so delivery is coordinated work, not a designed product.

DesignCanvas separates the tldraw spatial snapshot from a compiled project graph; image-job results (URL, asset ID, seed) are written back to generation cards and can seed downstream iterations, evidencing AI-produced assets with lineage. Mutation is bounded to card results and iteration; SQLite stores give two optimistic version clocks for one local app. Delivery is generated image assets; there is no multi-user merge protocol.

Decibel is a design-memory and governance layer: fsStore persists principles/decisions/progress and figmaStore reads tokens/components, so it does not author the design itself — authority is low. Agent tools upsert, log and append into the durable rationale store, which is its real artifact. It strengthens design agents across conversations but delivers no design output of its own, capping delivery.

BuildGraph's copilot exposes read-only tools over a deterministic model-facts/calculation-trace view and cannot invent dimensions, loads or sizes — deliberately subordinate, so authority and mutation are low. The event-sourced project (layout events folded into topology, compliance and cost) is a strong durable artifact with replay/undo and SSE collaboration. Delivery covers design reports and BOQ CSV, but the AI contributes explanation rather than creation.

Browser Design Mode sends a runtime target packet plus screenshot and the Agent edits repository files with hot reload, while Canvases are agent-authored durable .canvas.tsx with .canvas.data.json state — both surfaces show direct AI authorship and mutation of persistent artifacts. Humans review diffs and explicitly commit/apply worktrees; Canvas publishing is a read-only snapshot. Target return stops before file/range identity, so source grounding is heuristic.

Penpot AI Kit routes skills into suggest-only audits, review-gated operations and small approved auto-fixes, and meaningful writes require a preview image/summary checkpoint before the Penpot graph mutates — AI performs real native design work under human gates. Penpot's file remains authoritative and editable, with reports and DESIGN.md as downstream evidence artifacts. The review gating keeps human_loop at a medium level.

The model emits a validated game configuration bound to known Canvas/WebGL templates, so AI authorship is real but confined to a bounded runtime vocabulary. GameVersion snapshots give an explicit correction/restore history around the playable artifact, though iteration is largely human-editor driven, capping mutation. Delivery is strong: a playable browser game plus published launch pages with leaderboards and reviews.

Montevive Penpot MCP is intentionally read-only: it fetches a Penpot file, validates it against committed schemas and exposes a normalized object tree with screenshots/exports, with no write tool, so authority and mutation are 1. The tree-plus-image evidence contract is a real deliverable for design-to-code grounding. It is a separate read-only bridge, not native artifact authoring; delivery is the evidence contract rather than a design result.

Onlook instruments JSX with durable data-oid source identities and both human visual operations and AI chat write-code actions persist back into the project codebase, so AI and human co-edit the same authoritative source with operation-level undo/redo and branching. The sandboxed live preview runs the actual project and deployment is advertised. Non-Next.js/Tailwind support is unfinished, bounding the source-mapping scope.

The official AI Copilot extension performs completion, edit and text-to-image actions that write into the current Markdown document with editor undo for recovery, so AI mutates the durable local file directly ('extension-ai-copilot'). Markdown remains the authority while preview and diagram blocks are projections. It is a powerful editor extension rather than a standalone design agent, so delivery is the authored document rather than a published artifact.

CAD-GPT writes design logic, parameters and OpenSCAD/CadQuery source from a requirement, so the editable generation logic — not an opaque mesh — is the AI-produced artifact, and humans can inspect and edit parameters/source before re-rendering. Mutation is moderate because iteration happens on human-edited parameters/source rather than an AI re-write loop. Rendered meshes are projections; the preserved paper implementation with incomplete refactor caps delivery.

web-to-design-md extracts DOM/CSS evidence into a DESIGN.md plus a token-based HTML preview for human visual review — an analysis/handoff skill that does not author a design or mutate the source site, so authority is low. The coupled DESIGN.md + preview is a durable, inspectable artifact built from the same tokens. It owns the evidence and design-system handoff, not the downstream site's source, capping delivery.

EDA Agent models a plan→snapshot→checkpoint→review→placement/routing autonomy cycle over KiCad/EasyEDA/Altium backends, so AI performs bounded design operations on the native EDA project files with checkpoints for reversibility. The canonical artifact remains the host project's native files, with a portable operation and review layer on top. Fabrication-oriented exports close delivery; visual/rule review and solver setup keep humans in the loop.

The agent operates one isolated headless Blender scene via a socket service, turning chat/voice/M365 intent directly into persistent .blend edits ('the .blend scene is canonical; web, activity and voice are alternate control transports'). scene_manager.py saves/restores per-VM state so the same scene survives transport changes and idle resumes, evidencing durable mutation and artifact. Human drives by prompting and reviewing viewport evidence, so human_loop is moderate rather than end-to-end autonomous.

Superinterface is an embeddable-assistant open core, not a design surface: 'the host controls theme placement and supplied client components' and a model can request UI only through the integrator's handlers and component vocabulary. Server persistence covers Workspace/Assistant/Thread/Tool records but the designed artifact lives in the host product, so authority and mutation are low; delivery is the embedded interaction surface rather than a shipped design result.

Design mode turns a brief into an agent-created HTML artifact run by design-runtime.js, and the DesignInspectorPanel lets the user 'select elements, edit properties directly and ask the agent to revise the same work' — a closed edit–revise loop on a persistent artifact. Rust artifact commands own filesystem/session persistence ('the editable HTML/runtime artifact is the working authority; screenshots are previews'). Human still inspects and edits elements in the tool, so human_loop is moderate.

Commands create numbered Markdown architecture artifacts from templates and diagrams via Mermaid/PlantUML, and hooks warn on stale dependent artifacts, so the agent generates and updates a governed filesystem graph ('Git and the artifact tree are authoritative'). Delivery is documentation/diagram artifacts gated by a human review workflow rather than a shipped product, and the human runs the commands and reviews states, keeping this AI-enhanced.

QBIC translates Cursor model reasoning through an MCP server and WebSocket hub into native Figma node operations ('rectangle and text creation ... batch text replacement ... connectors'), so the AI creates and edits the persistent Figma document ('The Figma document remains authoritative'). It is counted as an external agent bridge and the pinned implementation proves the Figma example only, so delivery covers a bridge/demo rather than a full intent-to-ship loop.

Gemini-based generation/edit operations feed canvas items with position/scale/stacking state that the user keeps arranging ('uploaded and generated media become canvas items ... the user can continue arranging the composition'). The model's outputs enter the same state container as manual uploads, so AI does not own a separate project graph; no durable server-side project/history model is evidenced at the pinned hackathon-era snapshot, penalizing artifact and delivery.

The agent reconstructs a flat slide screenshot through layout_plan.json and a semantic SVG into an editable PPTX plus QA report; the SVG is 'a materialization bridge rather than the final product' and the PPTX is the user-editable delivery. Optional LibreOffice/Inkscape rendering closes a compare-and-correct loop, but reconstruction is largely a one-shot regenerate from the source screenshot rather than sustained mutation of a persistent artifact.

The Illustrator skill layer exposes typed vector semantics and artwork tools that 'can update text and path points and apply translation, scale or rotation' directly against the native Illustrator document, with opaque DOM refs valid only per bridge session — direct mutation of a durable structured artifact. It is an agent-control bridge (delivery ends at native save/export), and it requires the adobepy/CEP bridge session, so intent-to-shipped-result coverage is partial.

A lightweight server joins a shared drawing board with Firebase storage and local ComfyUI generation (including inpainting) so 'generated proposals return to the same spatial board' as editable raster inputs. The human leads the drawing and composition and there is no parametric building model ('outputs should not be described as BIM or CAD authority'); it is a working prototype with machine-specific setup rather than a maintained hosted service, penalizing delivery and human_loop.

The model generates implementation markup streamed into the local conversation ('accumulates that response into the local conversation instead of writing a repository or provider-hosted project'), so the artifact is browser-held HTML and suffers a one-shot creation pattern with no editing of existing work; export-code is 'a materialization step rather than continued editing of the same artifact'. No durable project store or version graph is present at the inspected commit, penalizing artifact and mutation.

Five agent roles (Consultant/Researcher/Planner/Designer/Reviewer) pass explicit artifacts and produce one source SVG per slide with stable semantic IDs; natural-language edits 'resolve through a slide manifest, target the relevant SVG content and save the previous source under slides/history/ before regeneration', evidencing direct iteration on a persistent editable artifact. Reviewer scores and routes failures back to roles, and PPTX/HTML are exports from the SVG project, giving strong coverage of intent to deliverable.

Next.js routes upload assets to RunningHub workflows and store task/session records in Supabase with webhook reconciliation, so the workspaces are job orchestrators over provider workflows with persisted histories and canvases. AI generates media outputs (campaigns, retouches, resizes, video) but each surface is a separate artifact loop over provider jobs rather than direct AI iteration on one persistent design artifact; the private provider workflows behind each app ID are not proven.

The plugin inspects selected image pixels and 'writes that decision into the layer name that Figma later uses during ordinary export'; the visual composition is never regenerated, so the AI supplies a small naming mutation inside Figma's authoritative graph. It is a narrow delivery fragment ('an auditable proposal that needs human review'), with no source repo or documented batch/review behavior, so authority, delivery and human_loop are all low.

ives packages Design as contextual judgment skills whose decisive workflow runs four critique lenses to 'identify specific issues and coordinate changes with implementation-oriented skills', but 'it does not own a renderer or a proprietary canvas; the host project's source remains authoritative' (operated reasoning and review system). It steers but does not author or persist the designed artifact, keeping authority, artifact and delivery low.

This is a deterministic preparation layer: OCIO validates and converts between named color spaces and OIIO builds tiled mipmapped textures, recording 'a semantic transform rather than applying an unnamed visual adjustment'.
