Delivery is shared collaboration material rather than a shipped/externally exported result.

Eleven orchestrated agents materialize the full solution-design pack (pain points->architecture, KPIs, roadmap, exec story, app spec) from accepted workshop evidence, so AI authors the designed artifact ('delegated solution design with review gates'). Regeneration 'advances the artifact instead of overwriting history' via ArtifactVersion records, giving real mutation of persistent work. Artifact is strongly persistent: Prisma projects, agent runs, artifacts and versions. Human gates (facilitator edits/accepts cards, review of stages) keep the loop hands-on. Delivery is concrete via Markdown, DOCX and PPTX renderers.

The text prompt becomes a complete editable vector illustration through an explicit raster->trace pipeline ('the final SVG is the delivered authority'), so AI authors the visual artifact directly. Mutation is one-shot: the pipeline regenerates from scratch and 'AI output is one-shot; cannot touch the existing artifact afterwards' — no iterative edit of a prior SVG. Artifact is a durable editable SVG file, though 'a traced region may be editable geometry without knowing that it is a wheel, label or reusable icon' (no semantic component model). Verification is agent-judged with no fidelity threshold; delivery of the final SVG is the product's complete export.

Gemini generates the whole site from business idea/category/style inside a Laravel controller, making AI the author of the generated site. Mutation is minimal: the controller 'creates or retrieves generated-site records' with no branching revision graph or refinement loop evident. Artifact is a durable database envelope (GeneratedWebsite) but 'does not expose a branching revision graph'. Human supplies the form intent and sees a preview; no deep editing loop. Delivery ends at the retained generated preview — deployment/export beyond the app is not evidenced.

This is an EMC/signal-integrity review system: it parses KiCad artifacts, cross-references the BOM and 'applies preflight constraints' — it analyzes rather than creates design, so authority is low. It does not change the board ('Native KiCad files remain authority'), making mutation ~2. Artifact is review/correction evidence: shared findings, reports and simulation queues ('reports and queues are review/correction evidence'). The loop runs analyzers and queues deeper simulations with limited human intervention, and delivery is findings/simulation evidence rather than a shipped design.

dcc-cua is a Computer Use runtime/CLI bridge supplying the exact-window observation/action/verification boundary — infrastructure rather than a design author ('Design relevance is not generic mouse automation'). Authority is low because the product defines how agents act, not what is designed. Mutation is moderate: fresh observation-bound actions do change target-application state, with 'a new screenshot or semantic observation is required after a mutation'. Artifact is transient evidence (screenshots/observations), not a persistent design artifact. Host policies constrain the loop. Delivery is a runtime capability, not a designed/shipped result.

Behavr is a simulated-user usability-testing workspace: it extracts a prototype flow and runs AI users through it to produce metrics, heatmaps and findings — it evaluates design rather than creating it ('a Design-evidence system rather than a native authoring tool'). Mutation is absent: 'agents do not rewrite that file' and no writeback API to Figma is established. Artifact is a durable study (traces, metrics, heatmaps, findings) with several disclosed evidence levels. The run is largely automatic once the user supplies a Figma URL and task, but internals (parser, schema, sampling) are undisclosed and delivery is analytical findings, not a shipped design change.

Adly generates multiple static/video ad variants plus copy from a reusable brand profile, so AI directly authors campaign design assets. It 'supports refinement and approval' and landing pages 'can be edited before saving to a durable public link', evidencing real mutation of the campaign artifact. The artifact is a managed campaign package with release state, though no public schema establishes native asset/approval/scheduler structure (architecture-level ceiling, so artifact not higher). Human editing and approval gates bound release authority. Delivery is strong: schedule/publish to connected channels and durable public links.

Reicon is a governed icon system: the agent 'searches the canonical catalog, previews a result, generates framework code and applies a selected icon rather than asking a model to redraw it' — the agent selects and materializes existing approved assets, so it does not create the design itself. Mutation is moderate: applying an icon changes the host artifact and generated code can be traced to the catalog entry. Artifact is durable (`data/icon-data.json` catalog authority plus generated code). The loop is largely agent-driven selection/application. Delivery is framework code/plugin/figma materialization across hosts, a real integration result rather than a full design deliverable.

CapCut's AI edition is 'one entry into a much larger project': chat can create a draft, and AI operations cover script/media generation, captions, background/object manipulation and image editing — AI meaningfully authors and edits within the media project. The artifact is a strong persistent editable media project across online/desktop/mobile ('continue as editable project state'). Mutation is real but scoped: 'public marketing does not establish that a single autonomous agent can mutate every property'. Human does the bulk of editing with AI assistance. Delivery is concrete: export is the flattened, shareable video result.

ClaraVerse crews divide work and can produce interactive artifacts (images, charts, games, apps) in a retained creation surface, so AI agents author generated artifacts (authority moderate-high). Workflows can 'update' produced artifacts, giving some mutation, but the dossier mostly evidences generation plus repeatable automation rather than direct iterative editing of an existing artifact. Artifacts are durably retained ('not making chat the only place where work survives'); persistence and self-hosting are evidenced. Human review is built into crew orchestration ('a person reviews intermediate results'), so the loop is not end-to-end automatic. Delivery is in-workspace artifacts/workflows rather than a shipped/exported result.

Deliberately read-mostly: the server parses native KiCad artifacts and provides discovery, BOM, netlist, DRC, pattern recognition, validation, export and thumbnail evidence 'without claiming to be the authoring authority'. Authority and mutation are both near-minimal ('must let the user or another authoring tool change the native project'). Artifact is durable evidence — DRC history and exported renders — rather than a design artifact. The loop runs bounded subprocess analysis with explicit path/execution constraints, then hands off to the user. Delivery is analysis reports/evidence, not a designed artifact.

The toolkit turns screenshots into targetable regions, inventories and coordinates so text-oriented agents can repair UI/graphic/diagram artifacts; for UI restoration 'repository HTML/CSS/SVG remains authoritative' and the agent edits it, so AI performs real restoration/mutation of existing artifacts. For graphic restoration an editable SVG becomes the deliverable, evidencing AI-authored visual output. Coordinates 'are not treated as pixel-exact' and verification is a second pass, so authority/fidelity claims are bounded. Artifacts are the authoritative source files plus pixel-diff/HTML-shot evidence. The loop is agent-driven with explicit re-verification after generation or interaction. Delivery is restored/reconstructed artifacts for coding agents.

Gemini streams HTML/CSS, Tailwind, React or Vue component source and the workspace 'resubmits the current source when the user requests a refinement', so AI authors the component and iteration feeds the existing source back in (mutation is real but refinement is regenerate-from-current-source rather than surgical edit). Artifact is durable after explicitly saving: the library persists prompt, framework, source and refinements in MongoDB ('durable ownership begins only when the user saves'). Human requests refinements and performs the save; otherwise generation is streamed. Delivery spans four runtime targets plus a saved personal library.

This is a project-local operating system for agents: an AGENTS.md contract, static scaffold, style-guide extraction and component/page skills guide agents that prepare a site in source files and then transfer it into Webflow — AI builds the site following the scaffold (authority moderate; the template orchestrates rather than solely designing). Mutation is real but governed: agents edit local source and 'the agent is not allowed to blur local experimentation with a successful host mutation' — Webflow transfer is an explicit delivery step. Artifact is durable local source, design-system notes and a page log. Delivery is a concrete transfer into Webflow as the host authority.

The builder asks an OpenAI-compatible client for component source and stores it under a project, making AI the component author. Mutation is limited: generation creates a new record and a preview is created 'from a selected generation' — iteration means generating new generations rather than editing an existing artifact in place. Artifact is strongly durable: SQLite migrations make projects, generations and compiled previews 'independently recoverable and exportable', with compilation results or failures recorded. Human selects generations and triggers previews. Delivery is compiled React HTML with runtime and Tailwind styles — an exportable build rather than a full shipped product.

Mowgli expands a living specification into moodboard alternatives, then a full screen/flow canvas and interactive React prototype, making the AI the author of whole-product UI. Targeted chat edits 'operate on a selected button card or section' while global prompts rework a page or product, evidencing direct mutation of the persistent canvas. Artifact is strong: living specification, version history and branching keep experiments reversible. Human chooses directions, remixes attributes and steers edits, so the loop is co-editing rather than fully automatic (AI-first). Delivery is concrete: editable Figma file, React/Tailwind reference code or an agent-ready bundle, with the caveat that React output is 'structurally flat and assumption-free'.

TechDraw sends a constrained React Flow JSON schema plus icon vocabulary so the model creates an architecture graph — AI authors the diagram. Mutation is real but narrow: the context-menu path sends the selected node plus a change request and 'copies title, content and icon from the first returned node onto the original ID', while 'geometry, edges and all unselected nodes remain under human control'. Artifact is a persisted local project in IndexedDB, but 'there is no durable revision table' and source contradicts the claimed autosave. Human controls geometry/edges and must press Save. Delivery is PNG/SVG export plus IndexedDB snapshots — not a shipped product.

The bridge exposes Python and SKILL operations for reading and mutating real Cadence objects, so an external coding agent performs schematic creation, connectivity inspection and parameter edits through it — the bridge is the control plane while 'Cadence owns design truth'. Authority is bounded because the product is infrastructure that enables agent authorship; mutation is high and evidenced (schematic editor, ops, GDS export). Artifact is the authoritative Cadence library/cell/view, durable but owned by Virtuoso rather than the product. The loop is agent-driven through persistent sessions with licensed/EAD environment constraints. Delivery is DRC/LVS/simulation/GDS evidence and export, requiring external validation.

Claude Design is an agent-first design workspace: 'Claude creates a working first version' on a canvas and the user corrects it via chat, inline comments, direct edits and Claude-created adjustment sliders, making the AI the author of the hosted design. Mutation is strong and documented: corrections address selected canvas elements, direct edits touch visible elements, and 'Claude can apply that change across the larger design'. The artifact is a persistent hosted project with saved directions, organization design systems (extracted, published, governed) and shared review states; internal schemas are closed so artifact/versioning gets a modest penalty. The human mostly reviews/steers with several correction channels, though direct edit is a manual channel. Delivery is extensive: ZIP, standalone HTML, PDF, PPTX, partner destinations and Claude Code handoff.

Windsurf's historical loop had Cascade and the human operating on the same local codebase: Integrated Browser captures rich DOM/CSS/geometry element packets, 'Cascade searches the repository and edits project files in Code mode', so the AI directly authors and mutates the real source artifact. Mutation is strong (direct file edits, repair of side effects, worktree isolation, checkpoints), though the runtime packet stops before source identity ('rich runtime grounding followed by heuristic source search'). Artifact is the strongest dimension: local source tree and Git are the durable center ('Workspace files are the product artifact and implementation authority'). Human reviews diffs, reloads and merges worktrees, keeping the loop co-editing. Delivery includes App Deploys (Netlify previews), source commits and exported builds.

Naaviq is a visual editor where humans author an agent as an executable graph (React Flow) that compiles into a LangGraph StateGraph; the AI agents execute across chat/WhatsApp/voice but the graph design itself is human-authored in the editor, so authority is moderate-low. Mutation is versioning on save ('edit the graph, save a new graph version, test through chat or voice, then inspect the trace on the same topology') rather than AI-driven editing of the graph. Artifact is durable: PostgreSQL agent records hold graph configuration and versions with a checkpointer. Human authors the graph and tests; delivery is channel binding rather than source export.

The AI App Builder runs against the live relational model and 'an AI session gets an isolated, short-lived container in which it can build an application', so the AI authors a deployed interface/workflow grounded in real data (authority high). Mutation is moderate: building happens in a sandbox and publishing moves the app to a long-lived container; the workflow engine runs AI steps on record changes, but the open core does not evidence ongoing AI editing of the same app artifact. Artifact is strong: live PostgreSQL tables/views as directly editable authority plus the served app; sandbox mechanics are architecture-level, not source-inspected. Human edits tables and publishes. Delivery is concrete: a published app in a serving container.

AI DESIGN SPACE aggregates text/image/video models into a production project; generation history is grouped into project folders and dedicated image/video editing modes (mask inpainting, sketch-to-render, background removal, upscaling, video assembly) operate on canvas objects, so AI authors generated media and edits existing canvas/media (mutation real, covering edits to persistent objects). Artifact is durable: project folders, infinite canvas objects, media resource library and generation history, though the canvas schema/revision model are not exposed (architecture-level). Human organizes, comments and exports. Delivery is PNG/PDF/media export plus CRM task handoff.

Four bounded agents turn a concise requirement into execable build123d geometry via typed intermediates (Spec Planner -> Geometric Architect -> Python Coder), so AI authors the CAD construction source from intent. Mutation is real: a repair stage 'responds to execution and QA failures' and brief/plan caches let a fresh coding/repair attempt rerun without discarding upstream decisions. Artifact is durable: cached `cad_brief.json`, `architect_plan.json`, execable Python as construction authority, with STEP/STL/GLB as derivatives. The run is largely automatic (manual reruns for repair). Delivery is concrete printable geometry (STEP/STL/GLB) subject to domain validation.

Gemini produces exactly three typed files (HTML/CSS/JS) from a prompt, so AI authors the mini-site. Mutation is minimal: generation is one-shot and 'the user can edit each one' manually — the AI does not re-iterate or touch the artifact afterwards. Artifact is weak: the files are React state impersonating a file tree ('no project store or history exists, so download is the only durable recovery boundary'). Human edits code in textareas and triggers export. Delivery is a ZIP export that materializes real files, closing the loop to a downloadable site.

The Design subsystem can author a DESIGN.md, build or polish an interface and deliver critiques, so AI authors design briefs and implements/polishes UI from them. Mutation is real: 'critique-loop can convert findings into tracked work and re-run the same review until it converges', a repeatable correction loop against the implementation. Artifact is durable repository artifacts (USERS.md, DESIGN.md) as contracts the critics evaluate against. The loop is skill-invoked with user initiation, so it is not end-to-end automatic. Delivery is findings routed into tracked work plus built/polished interfaces — a repeatable review loop rather than a single shipped deliverable.

Hot Design is a visual designer over the running app: a designer (or an external agent via Uno Platform App MCP) selects real UI elements, changes layout and properties, and 'adopted changes are reflected in underlying XAML', so AI makes real visual changes that converge into the source — strong authority and mutation. The artifact is the canonical XAML application project source, durable under version control, while runtime selection IDs are transient. Human review/acceptance and rebuilding from clean source are required, so the loop is co-editing (AI-first). Delivery is a rebuilt cross-platform .NET app; the Studio/MCP layer is architecture-level, so atomic rollback and source-mapping internals remain unproven.

The Drawer renders executable plotting code that recreates a reference figure from the user's data, so AI authors the figure design. The Reviewer returns a score and revision checklist while the preserve list accumulates across iterations, evidencing direct iterative mutation of the editable Python script that is 'the durable authority'. Camera-ready PDF closes the loop to a publication deliverable; the loop is measured and automatic but the user supplies data and steers, so human_loop is not a 10.

The pipeline generates storyboards, media and the assembled film through provider adapters, so AI performs the creative production. 'Changing an upstream stage invalidates dependent outputs' plus versioned artifacts and explicit regeneration tasks show direct mutation of persistent project state. React Flow is only a control projection while 'artifact snapshots remain the durable production record', and FFmpeg materializes final.mp4 for delivery; review can create regeneration tasks, so the loop closes with human critique.

Ten specialist agents handle research, strategy, visual direction, motion, content and implementation, but the pipeline is 'directed by a human' with a required human-direction stage between debate and build, so authority is high but not maximal. Agents fix issues after parallel critique and 'repository files preserve their decisions', evidencing mutation of shared filesystem artifacts including design-state.md and DESIGN.md. 'Design-state.md is the process memory' makes the durable artifact strong; Direct mode pausing at handoffs keeps human intervention hands-on; handoff and verification evidence connect decisions to source delivery.

A local Qwen model generates the three fenced code blocks that become the site, so AI authors the HTML/CSS/JS. However the dossier states 'No correction loop, saved history or recovery path is present', so mutation is one-shot at 2. The three layers persist only in React state until a ZIP export writes index.html/style.css/script.js, so artifact is moderate and delivery reaches an exportable site; no iteration loop means the user prompt-and-export flow is the whole human role.

Multiple agents propose and critique a narrative, but slides are curated from indexed decks and the dossier calls it 'a curation workspace rather than a general presentation generator', so AI authorship is partial. The native PPTX merger preserves source formatting but AI does not directly edit existing slides, capping mutation at 3. The workflow state and resulting PowerPoint are durable editable artifacts and the merged PPTX is a real deliverable; human outline editing and slide selection keep the loop highly manual.

As a transport bridge (local HTTP server to a Figma plugin) it does not itself create design; authority stays with the external agent, so authority is 2 per the bridge rule. The read-write API lets an agent 'create frames text components and instances' and bind properties, so mutation of the native Figma graph is enabled but performed by the agent, not the bridge. Artifact is strong because value is bound to live Figma variables (spacing/lg survives) and 'Native Figma graph' is the product's authority; version history in the host is the recovery mechanism and 'Production-ready remains contingent on code-side verification', limiting delivery.

The skill 'reads and summarizes the host artifact; it does not itself publish a page or own component revisions', so it does not author the design itself (authority 3) and never mutates the host Artifact (mutation 2). Its output is a durable, inspectable '<page-type>-page-guidelines.md' that serves as a governance input, which is a solid structured artifact but only an isolated guidance fragment on the delivery dimension. The workflow runs automatically once invoked, giving a mid human_loop score.

AI 'creates or extends the dataset' including text, colors, booleans and variant choices, but application is explicitly 'not model-driven free-form editing' — deterministic bindings place accepted values, so AI authorship is content-level rather than visual design. The plugin mutates native Figma structures via repeated-structure scans and an ordering rule, and AI can revise datasets through column-scoped instructions. The typed dataset is a durable managed artifact with account-backed teams, and the output is a populated native Figma prototype; humans configure assignments and run the apply, keeping the loop hands-on.

The AI returns structured JSON recommendations 'that the user can apply' while the user tunes chart settings and picks presets, so the AI advises rather than authors the figure. Recommendations 'do not mutate the figure until applied', but origin_driver.py can drive Origin and save .opju for later refinement, evidencing a gated mutation loop. The editable Origin project, data and recipe 'carry working authority' and export covers SVG/PDF/raster, giving strong artifact and delivery; the user-driven apply-and-tune workflow keeps human_loop low.

Self-Review is a cross-domain agent audit that compares intent, deliverable, method and progress; it does not create design, so authority is 2. It 'never silently edits the artifact it evaluates', making mutation 1. The findings report is a durable 'decision artifact' but delivery is only an isolated audit fragment; the audit runs builds and inspections automatically once invoked, which supports human_loop.

The plugin combines AI image generation with background removal, upscaling and tracing, so AI performs creative generation and image transformation. Tracing claims 'host-native vector layers' while other branches leave rasters, showing a real editable-output path. Evidence is thin: 'the creator does not disclose model providers, prompt or input-image transport, vectorization algorithm... or whether the vector path preserves colors and holes', so artifact and delivery are capped by missing evidence; the user invokes operations in a plugin surface.

Groq returns structured landing content that the template graph materializes, so the model authors the content and structure of the page within templates. Field and section corrections update the persisted object, evidencing iteration on the structured artifact; however the object lives in localStorage with 'no shared server-side project/version authority', capping artifact at 5. The export builds a complete Next.js ZIP from the same components as the preview, closing the loop to a deployable result.

Agents materialize 'a governed, executable Proteus artifact' from MCP-exposed component metadata and tokens, so the agent authors the UI document within a governed design-system vocabulary. Proteus's designer exposes the tree/property model for direct manipulation and visual regression review guards changes, evidencing an iteration loop over the persisted artifact. The JSON UI spec validated against a public schema is a strong durable artifact, and the loop reaches Figma-connected, rendered Axiom components; design review/Chromatic implies human guarding.

The model is asked for a constrained landing-page specification, and 'The JSON graph owns the visible design', so AI authors the design within a bounded vocabulary. 'Subsequent instructions replace the structured configuration; they do not mutate exported HTML or repository files', capping mutation at regenerating whole configs. The JSON graph lives in session state with 'no durable project store, direct node inspector, version lineage or code export', limiting artifact and delivery to preview; the user iterates through prompts.

The creative agent 'plans and executes multi-step work' across Firefly and Creative Cloud hosts, so AI authors generated assets and creative edits at scale. 'The agent does not erase host-native documents' — it coordinates operations over Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign and Premiere authorities, showing mutation of persistent host documents. Those host-native documents and Firefly Projects are durable editable artifacts; human review and direct host editing are retained but public evidence stops short of internal planning graphs and cross-app transactionality, and beta surfaces make delivery solid rather than fully proven.

Claude Code authors scripts, a video specification, narration and Remotion composition source using the toolkit vocabulary, so AI creates the video design. 'A failed visual does not require regenerating the whole film; the user or agent can replace one asset, change timing or patch the composition', evidencing direct targeted mutation of the project files. 'The project directory is the edit model' with repository files as recoverable authority and Git version history, and FFmpeg/Remotion render final.mp4; frame/audio review keeps a human checkpoint in the loop.

The png2svg skill asks the agent to express measured logo geometry in compact SVG paths, so the agent performs the reconstruction, though tightly constrained by measurement templates and conventions. 'Examples and tests compare the rendered vector with the supplied logo', evidencing a verification-and-correction loop over the SVG. The SVG is the durable structured artifact and the delivery; the skill runs as an agent task with human review, and scope is limited to geometric logos.

The contract describes AI generating 'an initial structure and design' from a brief and then changes to layout, palette, typography and content, so AI authors the site. Release notes expose project-level ops such as new-page generation, block cloning and global CSS, evidencing mutation of a managed site graph. 'The site project is the durable boundary' and publication can target Mobirise hosting with a connected domain plus full source export, giving strong artifact and delivery; the private mutation protocol and persistence schema are unknown, so mutation is held at 7, and users refine in chat or builder controls.

AI or offline planning produces a typed Processing graph that must pass schema and algorithm validation, so AI authors the geoprocessing model. Direct graph editing is protected by dirty-state tracking, Undo/Redo and crash recovery, and execution uses immutable snapshots with a result ledger, evidencing a careful mutation loop with undo checks. Bounded versioned JSON is the native format with .model3 and Python export, a durable structured artifact; proposals 'remain inert until the user explicitly chooses to apply', making human approval part of the loop.

As Figma's official interface for external agents, the server provides a bidirectional protocol but 'external clients invoke MCP' — the server does not author the design itself, so authority is 3 per the bridge rule. Write skills execute bounded Figma Plugin API code for 'frames, components, variables, auto-layout and canvas updates' under explicit permissions, so it enables mutation rather than performing it. 'Figma files and their native nodes are authoritative', a durable artifact the interface addresses; the hosted implementation is closed so internal mechanics are unknown, slightly capping mutation, delivery and human_loop.

d2c-build reads a Figma URL, suggests reusable components and 'generates source within those conventions', so the AI authors the frontend implementation from the design. 'Pixel diff and structural visual judgment guide iteration on repository source', and d2c-audit finds hardcoded values and bypasses, evidencing a correction loop over persistent project files. The repository and its design-tokens.json contract are the durable authority, and output is production frontend source across frameworks; the loop is grounded by rendered screenshot comparison with human review.

Codex is the external runtime that generates page concepts and revisions, with the product seen as the project structure and review surfaces it gives that runtime, so AI authors the concepts. 'A user annotates a region on an existing image before asking for a revision' and each page retains multiple concept images with an active version switch, evidencing targeted mutation of existing images with versioning. The filesystem 'pages.json' index and per-page files are durable structured artifacts guarded by the main process, with ZIP export and local Git as deliverables; user annotation and slice selection make the loop hands-on.

The pipeline agents author successive brief, outline and public deck objects validated as JSON, so AI creates the deck structure and content from scattered sources. The pipeline is resumable and 'later agents consume bounded evidence rather than the original pile of files', evidencing iteration over the JSON handoffs rather than one-shot output. The canonical artifact package is explicitly separated from the renderer by rendering-contract.md, a durable structured contract; final HTML comes from an external renderer, so the repository delivers render-handoff packages rather than owning a visual editor.

Gemini planner, generator and explainer roles produce the React source placed into the session, so AI authors the UI code within schema constraints. The browser editor 'changes current source' with a rollback sequence and live preview, evidencing a complete creation-correction-selection loop over the current code. However 'Restarting the server loses that graph' — the session is in-memory with no durable database identity, capping artifact at 4; there is only preview delivery and no export path, so delivery is low.

The Brandkit skill generates palette, logo and typography candidates that feed mockups, packaging, decks and brandbooks, so AI performs the brand creative generation. 'Regenerates only outputs affected by a later change' and 'repairs only a failing deliverable' show dependency-aware targeted mutation. The working authority is 'a compound local project: approval state plus editable SVG/HTML/PPTX sources and their exports', a strong durable artifact; approval is part of the artifact since 'Silence or a successful generation is explicitly not approval', keeping human review looped in, and the website skill closes delivery with preview and deployment.

Agentic AI expands moodboard and concept candidates in a fashion collection workflow, so AI generates the creative candidates while 'Designers decide which direction becomes CAD or a technical pack'. Mutation is weakly evidenced: 'current evidence establishes an operating professional workflow but not how much data transfers automatically between modules', so mutation is capped. The collection workflow links moodboards, prints, CADs and tech packs into a durable product chain and delivers toward suppliers and campaign assets; the public data model and CAD/tech-pack schemas are not public, capping artifact and human_loop (designer promotion remains essential).

The AI plugin streams structured slide commands, validates layouts and placeholders, creates a theme and slides, so AI authors the presentation structure and theme. It uses Asc.Editor.callCommand to 'mutate the live native presentation' and companions add charts, images and placeholder text through the same editor API, evidencing direct mutation of the persistent document. 'The durable artifact remains the office document handled by the mature editor' with native save and export, a strong artifact and delivery; ordinary editor correction after generation keeps a human edit loop.

OpenRouter creates the structured plan and 'model output governs layout and component decisions', so AI owns the design decisions even though generator.ts emits deterministically. Complete agent responses are appended to React state and a selected version 'replaces current code' with no localStorage or database, so mutation is whole-config replacement and the artifact is session-only. LivePreview maps the surface into an iframe document but is 'not source-equivalent production bundling', limiting delivery to a preview; the user selects versions and evaluates previews.

The runtime distils tutorials and reference artifacts into executable skill libraries, then the agent retrieves, composes and invokes domain MCP servers to produce web files, editable PPTX and Blender scene state — AI turns learned references into complete designed artifacts ('human-created examples become addressable operational memory'). Mutation scored 6: the runtime operates real tools and the generated project is authoritative, but the dossier does not evidence a direct iteration loop editing an existing artifact. Artifact 7 for editable PPTX/files/scene state; delivery 7 since tasks resolve into exportable web, PPTX and scene outputs.

Packaged Claude Code agents turn prose into a TypeScript component plus Storybook stories, tests and accessibility treatment ('component-generator' agent), with skills for visual regression analysis in Git history context and mockup/visual analysis — AI authors components directly in the repository. Mutation 7: agents edit the persistent filesystem source. Artifact 7 as components/stories/tests remain filesystem authority. Delivery 6: output is source components in a repo without a published/working UI result beyond the component graph.

The React Flow builder stores nodes and edges in Convex and the chat route compiles them into a traversed flow — the human authors the agent topology while AI (Gemini/API nodes) only executes at runtime, so authority is 4. Mutation 3: AI does not edit the saved graph; the graph is human-edited. Artifact 7 for the persistent Convex node/edge records and typed settings. Delivery 5: publication is 'a flag and hosted interface rather than deployment of a new service,' and loop nodes/user-approval remain incomplete.

The agent reconstructs diagrams/screenshots as editable SVG by separating measured pixel evidence, semantic interpretation and primitive selection ('extracted contours are measurement evidence, not automatically the final answer') — AI performs the reconstruction design. Mutation 8: element-preview gates let the agent 'repair arrows, panels and text without regenerating the whole figure,' directly editing the existing SVG. Artifact 8: SVG is the durable authority with a fusion-map schema and evidence trail. Human_loop 7 as OCR/semantic correctness depends on tool availability and review; delivery 7 as the result is an editable, render-tested SVG.

Text, images or sketches generate editable layers on an infinite canvas and an app-prototype mode is conversation-led — AI turns raw input into the complete designed artifact and proposes page/transition task lists. Mutation 8: users select content and request conversational changes that alter layers and interactions in place. Artifact 8: persistent project with reusable private components and AI-generated interaction rules. Delivery 8: exports to Figma, Axure, HTML, images, a generated PRD and MCP prototype code — a broad closed-to-handoff loop.

An architectural brief is turned into a constrained JSON graph description parsed into editable node/edge objects on a canvas — AI authors the graph structure from the brief. Mutation 5: generation is a one-shot brief-to-graph path with validation/fallback between model output and canvas; no evidence the AI later edits the materialized graph. Artifact 7: the editable graph is the working authority. Delivery 6: result is a system-diagram visual; no deployment or repository features ('does not establish collaborative versioning or production infrastructure').

Design Mode captures a live DOM selection as grounded visual evidence that coding agents implement against, and agents produce concrete implementations — AI does the implementation work from user intent. Mutation 8: agents edit files across multiple Git worktrees, with explicit candidate comparison and promotion via merge (promotion 'does not silently overwrite the main project'). Artifact 6: the design artifact is an evidence bundle (DOM, screenshot, context) rather than an editable design canvas; code/Git retain final authority. Delivery 8: parallel candidates are promoted into the main project in Git.

First-party pages describe AI generating a multi-screen mobile app project with shared theme, platform patterns and follow-up chat refinement of layout/color/features while maintaining the screen set — AI authors screens from one application description. Mutation 7: conversational refinement changes the generated screen set. Artifact penalized to 6: it is an editable HTML/Tailwind component project, but no implementation or project schema is public, so persistence/versioning/component identity are unknown. Delivery 8: standalone HTML project ZIP plus high-resolution images are produced.

Skills convert Figma variables, text styles and tokens into design-tokens.json/QML singletons and generate Qt Quick Controls 2 components, with platform-aware UI constraints — AI performs the design-to-QML conversion and generation. Mutation 6: the conversion 'creates a new source authority' with no bidirectional binding back to Figma, so existing-QML iteration is limited. Artifact 7: QML source, token JSON and generated controls are durable artifacts. Delivery 7: build/profiler/test skills project the source through the Qt runtime and reports.

A hardware-design skill suite where specialist modules contribute parametric CAD source, electronics/PCB, simulation and FEA to one physical-system design via typed handoffs — AI performs the domain design/generation work per skill. Mutation 6: CAD source and exported solids own geometry and modules operate on domain files, but the handoff protocol integrates authorities rather than showing AI directly revising one persistent artifact. Artifact 7: CAD source, exported solids, domain files and a design-score schema are durable. Delivery 7: the pipeline extends to manufacturing preparation and printer handoff.

The Streamlit app captures a brief and calls a LangChain Gemini chain that returns a complete three-part HTML/CSS/JS frontend displayed separately and rendered live — AI generates the full frontend artifact from intent. Mutation 3: output is one-shot; 'no durable project or version database is present' and there is no path for AI to edit an existing result. Artifact 6: parts are inspectable and downloadable but session-owned. Delivery 6: a downloadable website and in-app live render are produced.

The chat route calls an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and parses a structured JSON response into editable project files with a constructed live preview — AI generates the website project from a prompt. Mutation 6: Version snapshots exist and a restore route writes a selected snapshot back into current project state, but evidence is snapshot-level replace rather than fine-grained AI editing. Artifact 7: current files, chat and Version records persist in Mongo. Delivery 7: preview plus source workspace and versionable project state.

Ten role prompts implement UI work as a sequence of owned decisions where 'the execution agent changes repository code' then a verification agent captures breakpoints and compares against the specification — AI performs the design implementation from specs. Mutation 7: the execution agent directly edits repository code. Artifact 6: code is the authoritative artifact with design-system files and status.md as coordination records rather than a visual artifact. Delivery 6: implemented UI in a repository with screenshot verification; it is 'primarily a method/prompt release rather than a new visual runtime.'

A prompt or referenced website is turned into multiple complete UI directions run as live React/Tailwind prototypes with a distilled design.md — AI authors the directions and the executable project. Mutation 7: selected elements can be edited inline with the running result updating in place and directions can be promoted; AI-driven revision is evidenced but appears prompt/inline-driven. Artifact 8: self-contained local project, design.md, measured handoff and Figma export are durable. Delivery 8: live prototypes plus Figma materialization and handoff artifacts, though reverse sync from edited Figma is not proven.

Nyno is a local-first workflow engine whose React Flow canvas serializes to a .nyno YAML document that the runtime executes — the human composes the workflow; AI executes nodes, so design-authoring authority is 5. Mutation 4: the YAML round-trip is reversible ('the file is both portable source and saved visual authority'), but AI does not mutate the workflow itself. Artifact 8: the versioned YAML is a durable, portable structured artifact with position-ordered edges. Delivery 6: workflows run through HTTP routes with task state; no evidence of deployment or managed hosting.

The nature-figure skill classifies chart families and establishes typography, semantic color and panel purpose before plotting, and paper2ppt extends papers into presentations — AI authors publication figures under journal-grounded rules. Mutation 6: Figure QA reviews source rules and rendered composition against the authored Matplotlib/R source, implying revision, but direct iterative editing of an existing figure is only lightly evidenced. Artifact 7: Matplotlib/R source plus source data is the reproducible authority with text-preserving SVG. Delivery 7: publication-ready SVG/PNG figures and editable presentations.

A methodology layer for Claude Code requiring three distinct directions before convergence — AI generates options, spec, critique and QA content, but authority is 6 because the visual artifact itself is delegated to Figma/code prototypes ('the product's own authority is the decision trail and required gates'). Mutation 6: durable outputs (spec, QA report, handoff) are authored and revised through the gate sequence. Artifact 6: decision-trail files are durable but not a visual design artifact. Delivery 6: engineering handoff and pre-shipping verification materials.

Giselle is a typed workflow-design platform where the designer edits a typed workspace structure directly and AI executes generative nodes — human composes the graph, so authority is 5. Mutation 4: debounced persistence 'protects the newest graph' from human edits, but AI is not shown mutating the workspace structure. Artifact 8: typed workspace model with schema version is a durable, structured authoritative graph. Delivery 7: published apps resolve via an authenticated run route into tasks through the same runtime — a closed loop to runnable apps.

A catalogue plus ordered workflow builder where workflows are persisted lists of agent IDs with conditional steps — the human constructs the workflow while AI agents execute steps at run time, so authority is 4. Mutation 3: workflows are human-edited; the runner only splices chosen agent IDs at execution; AI does not modify the workflow artifact. Artifact 6: workflow records persist in Supabase with fork support. Delivery 5: runs produce bounded localStorage traces rather than shared server history or deployed results.

AI component creation submits a brief through OpenRouter and returns component code stored as a named Mongo record, with react-live preview of the source — AI generates the component from intent. Mutation 5: the component record is 'current authority; there is no separate historical revision model,' and generation creates new components rather than revising existing ones. Artifact 7: durable component records with name, code, props and publication metadata. Delivery 8: admins write the approved component into the library index and build/publish the npm package — a full release path.

The workflow rebuilds slide screenshots, diagrams and scanned pages as native editable PowerPoint text boxes, shapes, tables and charts — AI performs the reconstruction into semantic presentation objects. Mutation 6: spec locks and OOXML validation frame the reconstruction; revision of the output is supported but not deeply evidenced as an AI loop. Artifact 8: the .pptx is the working artifact with native editable objects, plus pptx_spec_lock.md and validation tooling. Delivery 7: a native, editable, validated PPTX deliverable.

Canvoss is deliberately infrastructure ('the library is agent-controllable, but it is not a hosted design service'), so authority is 5: it provides the mechanism by which an agent could author a design rather than itself turning intent into a complete artifact. Mutation 7: agents emit the same EditorOp operations as direct manipulation, applied deterministically to the LayoutDocument so AI turns are 'inspectable, replayable and rejectable.' Artifact 7: a serializable layout-node tree, though there is no durable project store — hosts must persist LayoutDocument. Delivery 6: renders to HTML and Playwright-captured export, but no hosted delivery or persistence.

The course sample models a project as named source files where the model loop offers structured file-manager and string-replacement tools applied in the browser — AI generates UI files from a prompt. Mutation 8: tools apply mutations to the persistent file graph directly, and the loop is 'prompt → tool mutation → source inspection → live projection → another prompt.' Artifact 7: the virtual filesystem persists as project data in Prisma and is editable. Delivery 6: live JSX preview projection and registered projects, scoped to an educational sample rather than a published product pipeline.

Prompt, Figma, GitHub and template starts all converge into a code-backed project with frontend, backend, auth and deployment state — AI generates and extends the full-stack product ('subsequent prompts can add behavior pages and Supabase-backed data'). Mutation 8: Interaction Mode binds a natural-language request to the element selected in the running preview so 'the agent is revising a specific code-backed object rather than producing an untracked replacement image.' Artifact 8: the live project and connected source repository are authoritative. Delivery 8: GitHub ZIP or deployment; patch format and version semantics are not public, so capped at 8.

The skill defines routes from language, measurements and photos to a print-ready model, building geometry from a frozen/hashed job contract or a five-role file-contract path — AI performs the model construction from inputs. Mutation 5: the deterministic route builds geometry once from a frozen contract and revision happens by rerunning the command; direct AI editing of an existing model is not evidenced. Artifact 7: contracts, Python/model source, kernel results, measurement reports and receipts are durable. Delivery 7: export files and print-engineering handoff reach a print-ready result, though physical printing stays separately gated.

The builder calls OpenAI from the browser and keeps the resulting JSX as session state rendered in a preview — AI generates the component from a prompt. Mutation 4: generation is ephemeral until an explicit save ('it becomes a retained variant only when the user saves it'), and the gallery only reprojects/copies saved source; no AI revision of saved variants. Artifact 6: saved prompt/source/title are persisted to Firebase, but pre-save output is volatile session state. Delivery 6: a copyable gallery on a live Vercel product.

Tessra packages agent design as a visual composition of persona, model, memory, skills and runbook over a typed AgentDraft, then exports a versioned agent directory — the human composes the design while AI does not author the agent itself, so authority is 4. Mutation 3: the canvas edits the draft and export promotes it; AI mutation of the artifact is not evidenced. Artifact 7: the downloadable package (agent.json, SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, workflow.json, skill Markdown) is a durable, runtime-ready artifact. Delivery 6: a handoff package is produced, but deployment or observing a live run is not proven.

A voice or text request becomes editable build123d code and geometry shown in a Three.js CAD window, then sliced toward a 3D printer — AI generates the CAD program from request language. Mutation 7: 'code keeps the model revisable' and the build123d program/model is the correction authority, implying AI-editable persistent source. Artifact 7: build123d code and model with STL/slicing as delivery projections. Delivery 7: the route reaches printer-ready sliced output, though the physical print remains an external step.

This is a verification product: agents compare an existing SimpleCORE wireframe board against the running application and write handover/parity files — it does not create or change the design, so authority and mutation are 2. Artifact 5: handover and parity files durably preserve audit state ('the remaining-work list is the progress authority'). Human_loop 5: fresh agents can inspect clusters across multi-session audits, but decisions are parked and judgment lenses remain human-driven. Delivery 3: the output is audit findings for projects that must already have a board, not a shipped result.

AI turns a text brief or ARK-vision-described upload directly into fenced React code promoted to editable canvas state, so authority is high. Mutation is limited because the dossier shows one-shot generation with human-side code edits, not an AI repair/iteration loop over the existing artifact. Artifact is editable React source in session state only ('no durable project or version store is claimed'); delivery is a working esbuild-bundled iframe preview with no export/publish loop.

PageGen turns text, screenshots, templates or files into React/Tailwind/shadcn pages and keeps generated code editable beside a live responsive preview, so AI is the author. The preview consumes the current editor buffer ('a manual edit is immediately reflected without another model generation') but AI re-editing of the existing artifact is not clearly evidenced, penalizing mutation. Artifact is the editable code buffer with share/publish/screenshot export, though account-level persistence was not verified so delivery is scored from the public surface only.

A single provider interface drives generation and the builder joins editing, generation and version selection around the current project, so AI authors the app. Schema stores projects, files, versions and parent-version references with list/compare/restore, giving real mutation and durable artifact evidence. Sandpack runtime plus a packaging export route deliver working source; human_loop is mid-range because users edit and steer versions around the AI-generated state.

This is an instruction/example package that routes Figma/code/token inputs and produces spec, token JSON and CSS/Tailwind handoff reports; it is a design-to-code bridge, so authority is scored low per the bridge rule. Mutation is absent ('accuracy depends on the agent's access to the cited sources and subsequent human review'); recommended outputs are 'proposed local governance artifacts', not edits to the design itself. Artifact and delivery reflect real documentation/handoff outputs, capped by the fact that it is not an extraction runtime.

Agents compose pyATS/ACI MCP tools to discover network facts and materialize editable Draw.io topology documents, so the AI generates a coordination artifact rather than a designed UI surface. Mutation and artifact are solid: 'the Draw.io document is a durable, editable coordination artifact generated from it' and users can keep editing the XML in the bundled host. Delivery is bounded to network reasoning/topology output, and human oversight remains necessary for operational decisions.

Gemini returns a structured JSON contract (JSX plus supporting schema/hooks) that is mounted as a virtual project in Sandpack, so AI authors the component from prompt. Mutation is limited to regeneration and human Monaco edits; the dossier does not show an AI loop editing the accepted bundle. Persistence is user-linked generation history via Prisma/Clerk with code/ZIP export, giving durable but sequential checkpoints rather than a rich version graph.

AI proposes ecommerce-landing structure inside the project's typed Layout schema and a separate service handles image generation, so AI is authoring within constrained fields. Mutation stays moderate because the accepted layout graph is edited through structured fields by humans, and the snapshot is 'browser-state driven' with no durable projects or version graph, capping artifact and human_loop. Export to React or Shopify source is a real delivery, though exported source only becomes authoritative in the destination system.

Six agent skills turn design intent into self-contained HTML/wireframe/prototype/diagram artifacts, with the HTML file as artifact authority and browser rendering as evidence, so AI-with-agent does the creating. Mutation is decent because HTML source stays editable and revisable, but the package is a skill set that depends on an agent harness and human steering, limiting authority and human_loop. Delivery is self-contained browser artifacts with recommended (not embedded) sharing tooling.

A coding agent generates source, the system renders it to pixels, and 'a pixel comparison becomes correction evidence for another pass', so AI is the author and iteratively mutates the generated source toward a Figma target. Artifact is the generated application source and rendered output with source export or MCP integration into an existing codebase. Scores are capped slightly by the closed early-access evidence: thresholds, patch-selection limits and MCP authorization are undisclosed.

Humans author the XYFlow workflow graph while AI agents execute workflow nodes in a durable distributed runner, so design authority is split and scored mid-range. Mutation and artifact are evidenced by versioned encrypted workflow copies that can be restored, executed via Hatchet, and published through Redis/Socket.IO. Human_loop is constrained by tool-approval events, and delivery covers running workflows plus export/import rather than a shipped design result.

Claude follows staged skills to write build123d source and produce STEP, STL and colored 3MF, making AI the author of parametric CAD. Mutation is strong because 'a later dimensional change edits a constant and reruns QA' on the canonical script, i.e. AI-revisable persistent source. Human_loop is capped because the project explicitly records that geometric QA missed a kinematic collision caught by a person in the slicer; manufacturing deliverables complete the loop.

An orchestrator plus specialist agents create wireframes and hi-fi deliverables under explicit review gates, with filesystem artifacts and a three-tier memory as authoritative, so AI contributes substantially but does not own the decisions. Mutation is evidenced by later agents advancing work only after review gates while artifacts persist across sessions. Human_loop is low because every gate requires human review, and delivery ends at design-workspace artifacts inside an editor rather than a shipped product.

Gemini streams boltAction file tags that are parsed and mounted into a WebContainer workbench, so AI authors the whole app; an automatic repair loop parses terminal/build errors and 'parsed file fixes are written back into the workbench', giving real AI mutation. Artifact is strong: server-side SQLite saves files, dependencies and runtime state transactionally, with Monaco editing the same file map. Delivery reaches a running app and saved checkpoints; human_loop is capped by the bounded, memory-limited auto-fix and explicit Save step.

Model providers generate or patch one complete HTML document, with 'bounded SEARCH/REPLACE operations instead of losing the whole artifact on every turn', so AI authors and edits the persistent artifact. Artifact is the current document plus session update history with element-targeted edits, but no server persistence is claimed, capping that dimension. Delivery is real: standalone HTML or ZIP packages with local image assets derived from the same source authority.

HOZO extracts patterns/tokens from an existing site or design data into an enterprise design system and then 'AI composes compliant components and pages from natural-language requests', so AI is the author under governed constraints. Mutation is evidenced by system updates that propagate into previously generated UI and bidirectional conversion between code and the cloud design artifact, though the scope of 'bidirectional' is explicitly limited. Human reviews in both professional surfaces and delivery to HTML/React enterprise sites are documented.

The agent compiles a structured JSON workspace into native PowerPoint via pptxgenjs using full-deck composition grammars, so AI does the deck authoring. The JSON workspace 'remains the revision authority' but manual edits in the exported PPTX cannot flow back, limiting mutation. Artifact is durable (JSON workspace, rendered images, PPTX) and delivery is complete native decks with three-layer QA (geometric, visual, placeholder checks).

As a historical family, Automator is deterministic while Magician is genuinely generative (icons/images/copy/layer renames) and Genius never shipped past preview, so AI authority is partial. All products directly mutate the native Figma document ('Actions create/update native nodes, styles and file metadata'), giving strong mutation and an 8 for artifact since the Figma document is durable, editable state. Delivery is bounded to in-Figma utilities; the closed cores leave model, persistence and run-atomicity semantics unproven, penalizing the unverified dimensions.

Gemini image generation produces the mockup from uploaded logo/material plus a prompt, so AI is the author of the result. Mutation is minimal because 'editing means regeneration, not layer mutation' (no layer graph, mask history or parameter ledger), and the output image is the only durable artifact with no saved project or version restore. Delivery is a PNG download, making this a candidate-generation loop rather than a persistent-editable design tool.

A provider cascade (Gemini then OpenRouter) generates and runs targeted edits, with the current HTML sent on each edit and successful edits replacing both local state and stored generated_html, so AI authors and mutates the persistent artifact. Durable Supabase HTML rows are the authority, and fallback provenance stays visible ('fallback: true' with a Demo Mode banner). Delivery is a real ZIP of HTML plus a Vite project, but 'Publish' is UI-only and no version table exists, capping human_loop and delivery.

The hosted service generates HTML drafts from curated repository context as asynchronous jobs, making AI the author of the design draft. The draft graph is durable and branchable ('iterate-design-draft --mode branch' creates separate nodes; per-draft versions with revert that snapshots first), giving strong artifact and mutation. Human_loop and delivery are moderate: users review/branch on the hosted canvas and the coding agent implements only after approval, so there is no automatic canvas-to-source round-trip.

AI drives a gated design-to-code pipeline from Figma/Canva/InDesign or conversation through a build spec and token lock to tested application code, so AI is the author of the implementation. Mutation is evidenced by up to five visual-diff iterations comparing the running app against the design, with tests written before component implementation. Human_loop is gated (design reviews, pipeline gates), and delivery ends in repository source plus a final build report.

The AI path asks Gemini for a complete inline HTML document and streams it into the editor and iframe, so AI authors the page. Mutation is weak because 'no source path connects the AI-generated HTML into this graph' — the drag-and-drop designer is a separate surface and there is no convergent AI correction of existing work. Artifact is the streamed HTML plus a designer graph, but delivery is capped at historical status with no maintained live service, and the public implementation history ends in 2024.

OVHcloud-hosted models make and revise one complete HTML document, with prompt refinement requesting replacement documents and manual editor changes promoted back into the conversation, so AI authors and can revise. Mutation is capped because the result is 'a linear sequence with no branch, diff or explicit restore command'. Artifact is only the localStorage chat transcript for one-browser continuity, and delivery is a server-side write or browser download rather than a hosted deployment record.

The Claude Agent SDK starts with the project directory as its working directory and a bounded tool set, so AI both writes and mutates the Expo/React Native source directly. The filesystem is the durable artifact ('source files remain ordinary local files, so an external editor and the agent operate on the same authority'), giving top-tier artifact. Delivery is strong: phone preview via Expo QR and EAS build/submission handoff to the App Store or Google Play, with the user reviewing steered work.

A Claude Code environment designs printable 3D objects from natural language, writing numbered versioned .scad revisions rendered to PNG for visual correction, so AI authors and iterates on persistent source. Mutation and artifact are evidenced by retained earlier source variants and an export skill that converts the selected revision to STL with non-manifold validation. Human_loop is mid-range because the user compares previews and steers refinement, and delivery is a validated STL production handoff.

A curated component registry is the starting authority and AI proposes variants that 'does not silently overwrite the registry component', so AI is an assistant rather than author — a candidate-and-promotion workflow. Mutation is scored low because AI output is a proposed variant that must be manually promoted, and the kit is browser-local governance with ZIP packaging. Human_loop is constrained by registry curation and manual promotion; delivery is packaged component source rather than a deployed product.

This is an interactive policy lab for deciding what an AI agent may execute — a governance/decision-design workspace, not a design generator, so authority and mutation are low (AI does not create design work). Policy selection and execution are 'deterministic and browser-local' with audit events, giving a modest artifact. It is explicitly a prototype with no external agent action, durable audit database or organizational service, capping human_loop and delivery.

AGENTS.md routes visible feature requests through a repository-local design operating system and the agent classifies the job, selects a posture and reports applied constraints, so AI designs under local governance. The repository contract is authoritative and durable (tokens, taxonomy, presets, component anatomy, review checks) with drift-auditable verification scripts, giving solid artifact and mutation. Delivery is design-system-governed application code rather than a published product, and human review/verification keeps human_loop mid-range.

One Codex skill designs, builds and refines frontend experiences by writing ordinary application and design-system source, so the agent authors and corrects real code. Mutation is evidenced by browser-based visual QA and a design-audit script after which 'the agent corrects the source'. Artifact is ordinary durable source in the consuming repository; delivery is the refined code within the repo rather than a shipped deploy, and human review keeps the loop partially manual.

Tempo is a local-first AI software factory where Chat and background Agents do real work in isolated Git worktrees and Canvas edits return as source annotations with guarded, merge-aware, reversible file writes ('optimistic source transaction over local files'), so AI authors and mutates the actual codebase. The branch-scoped Git repository and committed storyboard source are the durable artifact. Human_loop is strong with Plan Mode and PR review before merge, and delivery ends in commit/push/PR-to-production; closed internals slightly cap authority/artifact evidence.

Four skills (consultant, brand-system, PDF, PPT) materialize upstream storyboard and identity decisions into either pixel-controlled PDF via Playwright or native pptxgenjs decks, so the agent does the deck authoring. The storyboard, brand-brief.md and identity.js are durable cross-renderer inputs, but there is no feedback path from rendered output back into them, capping mutation. Delivery is strong: two real artifact forms (fixed PDF and editable native PPTX graph).

Agent bridge that authors interactive-audio structure directly in the native Wwise graph: skills build containers, create events and 'configure_rtpc_curve.py authors interactive behavior', so the AI turns intent into design structure (authority 6). Mutation is high because skills create/edit events and curves in the persistent Wwise project, not one-shot output. The native Wwise project, Work Units and save paths are a durable structured artifact (artifact 8). Loop is agent-driven with human setup/review (human_loop 6) and SoundBank generation plus ProjectInfo reconciliation deliver engine-ready assets (delivery 7).

MCP server lets an agent create components, wire parameters, change values and group objects in the authoritative Grasshopper parametric document, i.e. AI performs design mutations on the native graph (mutation 7). The Grasshopper document 'stays authoritative' and is a durable editable artifact backed by up to 20 snapshots (artifact 8). The user must place the Cordyceps component and supervise snapshot discipline (human_loop 6); delivery materializes via Rhino bake/layers/render (delivery 6). Authority is 6 because the AI operates within the user's existing engineering document rather than owning the full design task.

AI generates a complete single-JSX React site from type/name/theme and runs it in a WebContainer, so the AI authors the artifact (authority 7). Recreation sends existingCode with a new instruction but 'replaces the stored code' in an overwrite with no version ledger, so mutation is regeneration-with-context rather than direct editing (mutation 5). The Mongo Website.Code field is durable and re-editable but a single string (artifact 6). Loop is largely automatic after user selection (human_loop 7) and delivers a runnable preview (delivery 7).

Core CAD skill produces STEP from prose or image requests, so AI turns intent into editable CAD geometry (authority 7); 'CAD source creates or edits geometry' supports direct modification (mutation 6). Parametric source and STEP preserve editable geometry while meshes/G-code are derived (artifact 7). Multiple stage contracts with review and 'cautious printer handoff' require human gates (human_loop 5), but the chain reaches real slicer G-code, fabrication checks and a dry-run-first printer handoff (delivery 7).

Hosted engine performs placement and routing under board constraints, i.e. AI does the core board design work (authority 7). Optimization generates candidate board states that can be resumed, edited and protected, with manual protection respected by later runs (mutation 7). Revisioned board states and browser-edited elements form a structured, reviewable surface (artifact 7). Cooper assistant flags/fixes but 'the user confirms before routing proceeds' (human_loop 6); the chosen revision downloads back to the user's native EDA tool (delivery 7). Internal optimizer/graph implementation is closed and penalized only indirectly.

Gemini creates the first UML/ER model through a strict JSON gate, so AI authors the initial diagram (authority 6). It is 'one-shot delegation rather than an agent loop' — the model does not operate the canvas and later changes are manual or fresh regeneration (mutation 3). The Java object graph plus portable JSON round-trip is a durable, editable semantic artifact (artifact 7). Human editing in the JavaFX editor is central (human_loop 5), while deterministic generators materialize the same reviewed model into language files and SQL DDL (delivery 8).

Bolt-derived chat-driven generation produces site source, so AI authors the application (authority 7). Users can reopen projects and 'continue chat-driven source changes' against persisted files (mutation 7). Backend ProjectVersion snapshots plus persisted project files make the artifact durable and versioned (artifact 8). Chat + WebContainer preview make the loop near-automatic with version recovery (human_loop 7); deployment-oriented surfaces and preview cover delivery, though deployment semantics are not fully evidenced (delivery 7).

The agent moves logical content to editable .drawio XML, i.e. AI produces the diagram artifact from content (authority 6). Skills support build-up views, PR diffs and validation on the same XML, enabling agent iteration over existing diagrams (mutation 6). The .drawio file is authoritative and remains editable in diagrams.net, a durable structured filesystem artifact (artifact 7). Validation tooling makes the loop agent-driven with review evidence (human_loop 6); delivery is the editable diagram plus visual review evidence rather than a hosted canvas product (delivery 6).

Skill turns flow/sequence/class/ER/architecture descriptions into editable SVG or ASCII, so AI authors the diagram (authority 6). The render-audit pass runs 'as the file is authored' and supports redaction, but iteration-on-existing evidence is thinner (mutation 5). SVG remains readable by people and agents — a durable editable artifact (artifact 7). Agent-driven with an explicit audit pass (human_loop 6); the SVG itself is the deliverable product (delivery 6).

Agent produces versioned SKiDL, electrical-rule reports and KiCad-compatible netlists from a circuit request, so AI performs the pre-engineering design (authority 6). Versioned SKiDL implies iteration, but evidence of direct AI re-editing is limited (mutation 5). SKiDL source and netlist are durable, editable, versioned artifacts (artifact 7). Explicit human handoff and approval gates for PCB DRC/EMC/safety make intervention substantial (human_loop 5); delivery reaches a KiCad-compatible netlist and handoff packet, stopping before production approval by design (delivery 6).

A visual-decision-verification workspace: the assistant lists diagrams, follows nodes and queries the CodeGraph to explain flows, but the diagrams themselves are human-maintained; the AI proposes drift diffs without auto-applying (authority 4, mutation 3). The .blueprint workspace binding Mermaid source, navigation and code references is durable and structured (artifact 7). The agent automates traversal and explanation but 'the user must decide which authority to promote' (human_loop 5); delivery is verification/proposals rather than a shipped design artifact (delivery 4).

Chat-driven Cursor workspace turns a design brief into a working schematic/PCB: the agent selects parts and 'mutates a live KiCad project through IPC', so AI performs the board design directly (authority 6, mutation 7). Native .kicad_sch/.kicad_pcb files remain authoritative and durable (artifact 8). The loop is chat-driven but hard-coded Windows paths and WSL requirements make it a personal architecture requiring hands-on setup (human_loop 5); ERC/DRC CLI verification delivers a checked board design (delivery 6).

Prompt/screenshot-driven UI generator that emits rendered design, HTML/CSS, SVG and Figma layers, so AI authors the full UI from intent (authority 8). Iteration on an existing design is not evidenced — exports look one-shot and version lineage/round-trip semantics are undocumented, so mutation is penalized (mutation 4). Saved hosted designs plus HTML/SVG/Figma materializations are durable, though token/Auto Layout semantics are not preserved across export paths (artifact 6). Generation loop is prompt-driven and hosted (human_loop 7); HTML/CSS and Figma paths deliver production-usable output (delivery 7).

Historical full app builder: describe an app and Spark generates a TypeScript/React app (authority 9). Iteration is deep — prompt, Fix All, visual target edits on rendered elements, theme tokens, code-tree/Codespace edits and Restore all revise the persistent artifact (mutation 9). Workbench versions, two-way repository main sync and Codespace provide durable structured state (artifact 8). The loop is largely automatic with human review of previews and explicit publishing (human_loop 8); publishing deploys to Azure Container Apps with managed data and URL, closing intent to a deployed result (delivery 9). Sunsetting does not change the score per the standard; source reconciliation internals are closed but well evidenced at the edges.

Unified agent bridge operating Blender and Unreal in one session; the AI can operate both native scene graphs via the server, add-on and Unreal plugin (authority 5, mutation 6).
