This is a socket bridge: the Python MCP server translates tool calls and the add-on executes Blender Python against the live scene, so the product itself does not author designs (authority low per bridge rule). The .blend scene graph and Blender operators stay authoritative and remain a durable, editable structured artifact, and export tools materialize scenes to project formats, but there is no closed loop to a shipped result beyond exports.

Specialized researchers and composer agents turn repository research into durable architecture/database/workflow documentation including C4 and Mermaid source written into the filesystem (workflow.rs, architecture_editor.rs). A dedicated outlet fixer directly reviews and revises generated content rather than treating model text as valid, evidencing iteration on the persistent artifact; the filesystem remains the authority and delivers documentation output.

SYNTHESISUI audits an existing repository and compiles owned contract files (tokens, components, motion, usage laws) that coding agents must obey, with measured conformance and human rule decisions on gaps; it is a design-code bridge/governance product rather than an authoring canvas. AI does not directly mutate application source and delivers a governance loop rather than a shipped artifact, with extraction implementation and contract grammar undisclosed.

A client-only creative DAG where Gemini executes model nodes and deterministic utilities handle transforms; node/edge state lives in localStorage and connections stay editable so users can branch, replace or rerun steps (types.ts, App.tsx). AI generates node content within a user-arranged graph and regeneration replaces step output rather than deeply refactoring an artifact; there is no server version history or publication path for this early browser-only implementation.

The editor-era AI paths mutated the native hosted design file: AI Layout promoted inferred auto-layout to native structure on an explicit save boundary, AI Reduplication wrote native duplicates using a stale organization-scoped index, and AI Design Systems separated recognition candidates from human-promoted libraries. The durable artifact is a rich hosted design document with version history, collaboration and libraries; the later generator produced screens with Figma/code exports, but handoff broke at per-screen Project ZIPs and the read-only MCP server, keeping human acceptance central.

AGENTS.md instructs a coding agent to interpret incremental requests and continuously update one current Mermaid document, with templates for system/diagram conventions; 'the agent revises the existing file rather than producing disconnected images', and the user can edit Markdown directly with Git as the authority. AI authors and iterates a durable, editable diagram source, but there is no runtime, database, canvas or publish loop — the product is the protocol plus templates.

A Claude Code starter that turns the agent into a role-separated design-and-development team (business analysis, UX, UI, design review, accessibility, dev, copy, testing) advancing through a declared pipeline; generated application source is the artifact authority and docs/todo.md plus docs/lessons.md preserve project memory across sessions. The agent writes and revises the application source through iterative review agents, but execution depends on the host model and human-steered runs.

A portable skill plus Vite/Tailwind scaffold where an external agent (Claude Code/Cursor/Copilot etc.) mutates normal project files under guardrails defined in SKILL.md, with files owning the design and a browser preview as evidence. The publishing workflow blocks release on unresolved placeholders/metadata and routes the same project to GitHub Pages, Cloudflare, Netlify or Vercel, giving a gated closed delivery loop; the authoring intelligence is external, so authority and mutation stay in the AI-enhanced band.

Two model passes (feature decomposition, bounded component retrieval, JSON tree) generate a UI prototype and the plugin materializes native editable Figma frames, text, auto-layout and SVG nodes via the Figma Plugin API (plugin.js, server.js). Once materialized, Figma is authoritative and there is no node-to-JSON synchronization or post-creation AI editing path, so mutation is one-shot; the durable native Figma document is a strong artifact and the output is a deliverable visual prototype.

An npm CLI migration runtime whose init/audit/migrate/update commands scaffold durable .ai/ context, audits and migration plans (MASTER_PROMPT.md, component_registry.md) and direct a coding agent through source reconstruction and quality checks. The CLI scaffolds rather than executing UI changes, so AI authorship and mutation come from the host model executing against the persisted .ai/ state, and output delivery is reports plus shipped code.

A hosted managed app-project graph where the Horizons agent turns ideas into rendered interfaces plus text content, accounts, databases, payments, analytics and deployment; users ask the agent to change appearance/behavior, edit content directly, or use a code editor, with version history as a product contract. Design is end-to-end product delivery with publishing through the same product (domain/hosting), though export to React+Vite ZIP is explicitly one-way with no import back, keeping the provider-managed graph canonical.

A Go toolkit that converts structured circuit requests into reviewable architecture graphs and native KiCad source, with capability gates separating model suggestions from a deterministic registry and refusal receipts instead of guessing (ai_graph_design.go, creation-evidence.md). It writes project files with provenance and evidence records, producing durable KiCad artifacts, but creation is gated and scoped to supported circuit families rather than open-ended AI design.

A local-first browser 3D editor where human and agent operations share the same live scene, editor history and .skf project; the MCP bridge lets an agent read the scene, create/update objects, group, apply boolean cuts, and capture images (sketchforge-mcp-server.mjs, SKF_PROJECT_FORMAT.md). Because the agent edits the persistent scene and history directly, mutation and artifact are strong, but the bridge is development-oriented and delivery stops at STL/OBJ/STEP interchange exports.

Superun's Figma assistant generates or modifies interface layouts through bounded operations (Kick Start, Style Transfer, Region Design, Smart Fill, element modification, template remix, frame redesign); results materialize into editable native Figma layers and components only at 'Import to Figma'. It modifies existing frames/regions and preserves structure in constrained ops like Smart Fill and Frame Redesign, producing durable native design files, though the closed implementation leaves model routing and synchronization undisclosed.

A local React project directory is authoritative: streamed model file blocks are written into the project (website_generator.py, image_to_website.py) and project_manager.py scaffolds Vite projects, exposes the file tree, and reads/writes individual files. Generation and correction share endpoints so fixes return to filesystem authority rather than a UI overlay; the durable artifact is the editable project, but delivery is a local preview server without a publish range in evidence.

A Stitch-style builder where one prompt becomes a planned multi-screen application via a persisted state machine (Project ANALYZING → streamed plan → structured sitemap → generated Page rows → COMPLETED) rendered as movable frames on a canvas; page/project rows survive refresh and can be resumed (schema.prisma, inngest/functions.ts). Adding a screen reads an existing page as a style anchor and leaves prior pages intact, evidencing mutation of the persistent project, and a deployed live surface exists.

The intended product is a D2-first chat editor where OpenAI proposes D2 code, D2 remains editable, and Kroki renders it, with downloads of .d2/SVG/PNG (route.ts, DiagramEditorMain.tsx, kroki-client.ts). The pinned commit is an incomplete assembly — the editor imports store/renderer modules that do not exist in the tree and there is no durable project persistence in the present files — so artifact and delivery are penalized as 'no evidence' for a runnable persistent artifact.

Hardware design is one managed project (firmware, diagram.json, .kicad_pcb) where the Sparky agent sees the whole project, proposes schematic/code diffs and can invoke a routed PCB workflow; the custom KiPCBEditor reads and writes native .kicad_pcb s-expressions with DRC constraint checks and a 3D viewer (KiPCBEditor.tsx, pcb-drc.ts, deeppcb-client.ts). AI iteration is diff-based on a durable native board file, and cloud routing results return to the same project, though it remains an active prototype without fabrication delivery evidence.

A repository-native brand production framework where SKILL.md routes deliverables (HTML, posters, infographics, dashboards, presentations, docs) through pipelines that bind templates, components, tokens and quality gates; files and Git own persistence and the checked-in example preserves prompt, HTML and rendered image. AI generates artifacts through the pipelines and they can be revised at deliverable-specific gates, but many deliverables remain contracts rather than tested implementations (active-transition), capping delivery.

This is a DCC bridge: agents first read bounded graph state and mutations are dispatched to Houdini's host thread with atomic chain builders producing native nodes, while rendering artifacts and project save semantics are separate responsibilities. The procedural node network remains the inspectable, durable, editable authority, but the product itself is the agent-facing adapter, so authority and mutation are kept low per the bridge rule and delivery stops at assets/pipeline jobs rather than a shipped result.

A packaged EditorPlugin/debugger bridge/sidecar loads 163 typed tools by domain and operates on the editor thread within Godot semantics, using the undo manager and restricting paths to res://; the Godot project and native scene/resource graph remain canonical. As a bridge product it does not author the game itself (authority/mutation capped), but it mutates a durable, editable scene graph and separates in-memory changes from explicit saves, with export and QA tools advancing saved state toward delivery.

A local-first knowledge workspace where diagrams are one durable content type beside Markdown notes, charts and canvas modes, with separate stores/database paths for article and canvas state (types/canvas.ts, stores/canvas.ts, db/canvases.ts). AI enters through content-specific tools where chart/canvas helpers convert requested visual content into supported structures, so AI generates and updates structured canvas documents that persist independently of inference turns; delivery is a local workspace with sync as transport rather than a publish loop.

A socket bridge that connects an external agent to a running Rhino document for NURBS/scene work, creating and modifying objects, layers, selection, viewport capture and Rhino Python execution; Rhino's native document, layer model and geometry kernel remain authoritative. The product is the MCP surface and host script rather than an authoring engine (authority low per bridge rule), while the persistent Rhino document is a durable editable artifact and screenshots serve as correction evidence.

A skill collection whose two operated Design surfaces — design-md-validator (DESIGN.md and token schema as testable authority) and ultimate-design-system-master (routing brand, UI patterns, Figma layout, critique, accessibility, translation, presentation into deliverables) — structure AI design work. AI produces validated Design Markdown, tokens, specs and review reports as durable files, but the product is an instruction/routing layer whose execution depends on the host model and human steering.

A coordination layer for taking one commerce experience across Figma, Webflow and Shopify: each host has its own MCP workspace, agent contract and handoff rules, with a registry deciding which specialist owns the next operation and templates persisting structured handoffs. The product coordinates rather than authors (Figma remains design-input authority, Webflow owns site structure, Shopify owns commerce), so authority is low and its own artifact is handoff/template files; specialists execute the actual mutations on external platforms.

A governed Copilot workspace where Markdown owns slides and a separate draw.io path materializes editable .drawio.svg diagram assets from JSON specifications so diagrams reopen without raster reconstruction; a slide-review skill runs browser overflow checks as encoded QA. The agent authors and iterates Markdown/deck content and editable diagram files, but the product is an agent-ready template system whose delivery is a rendered, reviewed deck rather than a hosted service.

An agent skill that validates a typed JSON specification before layout, constrains provider icon choice via bundled indexed assets, and materializes the spec into editable Excalidraw or draw.io outputs with separate serializers and a preview script. The agent selects components and relations under provider conventions but the product is a governed skill workflow rather than an authoring platform, and the durable artifact is the spec plus native editable diagram files.

A Figma-native agent engine (plugin + genable-mcp) documented as planning, writing, inspecting and visually checking the current native graph — frames, Auto Layout, vectors, components, variables, pages — where continued prompts inspect the result rather than restart from a flattened export. Mutation operates on the persistent editable Figma file, and native persistence/editability are well specified, though model orchestration and plugin-side safeguards are not commit-level verifiable from the closed plugin source.

An independently maintained MCP distribution that translates Superdesign's method into executable Claude Code tools and owns a filesystem iteration/gallery loop: it returns structured execution specs, the model writes HTML/SVG files under design_iterations/, and the gallery discovers and renders them for comparison. The server structures iteration and extraction rather than authoring the designs (authority low per bridge rule); the HTML/SVG files are the recoverable durable artifact and selected outcomes carry into repository history.

MCP skills let an agent author and mutate portable USD projects ('create_stage.py establishes the authority'; composition/material skills 'mutate native USD semantics'). Artifact is a durable structured USD stage/archive, but rendering and app-specific import remain host responsibilities and the AI that decides the design is external, so authority/delivery are capped.

Generation (Fal.ai) is one stage of a user-arranged React Flow node graph with storyboard and timeline stores; 'generation is one stage of a longer project rather than the whole artifact'. PostgreSQL persists workflows/nodes/edges/media durably, but AI does not edit existing media and the human composes the pipeline, so mutation and authority are low.

AI generates sitemaps, linked wireframes and style concepts directly into a structured hosted project ('AI rewrite can target text or a whole section'; component selection/swap mutate the project graph), with versioned custom-delta Site Builder and Yjs Publish artifacts. Human steers and polishes heavily (Design View is an '80% accelerator') and exports to Figma/Webflow/React/HTML or Publish deploy, fitting the AI-first bucket.

Gemini generation is project-contextual: 'generation.service.js builds the Gemini request from the project conversation and current code', and MongoDB persists messages, generated source and versions, enabling iteration on existing work. No documented side-by-side branching or deployment path beyond download/preview.

An agent-orchestration workflow that produces a diffable 'bundle of architecture evidence' (docs, decisions, diagrams) as source-controlled files; 'the filesystem is the durable handoff surface'. AI agents do the architecture work, but the repo 'does not prove recommendations match a live estate' or passed review, and revision semantics are only implied.

Content-aware auto/preset correction initializes a result, then 'a person can begin with an automatic correction and then tune the result'; outputs live in the ComfyUI workflow JSON which preserves parameters. The AI produces corrected images rather than editing a persistent artifact, and manual grading is required, so mutation and human_loop are low.

An agent network writes files directly into an E2B sandbox via 'typed terminal file-write and file-read tools' and a task finishes only when generated files exist; Fragment records persist file snapshots and live preview URLs as the durable handoff. Correction flows back through conversation with no element-to-file mapping, and the result is a running sandbox preview rather than a published deploy.

Gemini returns one component string that the browser injects into an isolated iframe; 'there is no persistence or versioning beyond browser state'. AI creates the component but output is one-shot and disposable, so mutation/artifact/delivery score at the floor.

A visual editor for humans to construct agent control graphs; workflows persist in a local JSON DB with version records and a generator produces runnable code. No AI generation or AI mutation of the graph is evidenced, so authority/mutation are low despite a durable editable artifact and runnable output.

An agent builds scenes in Blender through MCP tools with an explicit spatial reasoning layer; 'Blender's scene graph is authoritative' and the agent queries/mutates it directly while ASCII plans reduce spatial mistakes. Rendering remains for aesthetic correction, and the live scene plus exports are the working deliverable.

An installable skill distribution that extracts palettes and diffs images as 'coordination artifacts' so an agent's visual decision is reviewable; the design itself is done by the external agent/human elsewhere. It is visual-decision tooling, not a design-authoring product, so authority/mutation/delivery are low.

Closed-source multi-agent system where 'text and visual input are interpreted into CAD logic' executed in FreeCAD/CadQuery to yield editable parametric, manufacturable models; the engineering contract requires continuation after generation. Persistence, revision and mutation protocol are undisclosed ('does not publish a durable project schema'), so mutation/artifact are capped.

ChatGPT writes the HTML structure and Stable Horde supplies imagery, assembled server-side and pushed to GitHub for Vercel deployment; 'GitHub and Vercel are part of the ordinary-user delivery path'. The app has no local revision graph, so mutation and artifact rely on the external GitHub representation and are one-shot at generation time.

VibeBot returns structured JSON actions that 'target the current nodes and edges', so a conversational change mutates the existing visual automation, which a backend executes through 13 node types with status polling. Persistence 'is less developed than its execution path', so durable version history is not claimed.

Agent control (headless scripts and MCP) calls the same native modeling core as manual commands over exact BREP state; 'the .serp container — JSON scene plus binary BREP — is authoritative' with autosave/journal continuity. Humans and agents both edit a first-class editable model exportable to STEP/Rhino/mesh.

Agents plan SQL and charts against governed MDL/instructions/memory with a 'dry-plan boundary' (validation before execution), and charts assemble into dashboards deployable via Vercel/Cloudflare. Mutation of existing artifacts is less evidenced than generation and governed validation, while delivery to deployed dashboards is strong.

The durable artifact is 'an ordinary directory on disk'; the orchestrator applies a typed file-mutation stream constrained to the project root, with per-turn restore and snapshots, so chat/Monaco/preview are views over a persistent editable project. Browser runtime preview and archive delivery close the loop, without a hosted deploy path.

Gemini generation is mediated by a LangChain service and the chat model 'persists the conversation and generated state used for later turns'; preview executes current source and deployRouter creates a distinct published representation. Project/deployment records are durable, though direct AI editing of existing source beyond regeneration is not shown.

A hosted suite of five AI-assisted editors where 'multi-model assistance generates or revises project material' inside editable, collaboratively persisted projects; the repository is documentation only, so the runtime, persistence schema and provider adapters are unproven and 'it does not infer that all five editors share a common data model'.

A local broker/SDK control runtime where Python 'can select and style text, change layers or paths and request native save/export'; the open host document stays authoritative. It is infrastructure that enables an external AI to directly mutate Adobe documents, but it does not itself author design, so authority and human_loop are low.

The user edits an in-memory React Flow graph and the route 'does not persist the submitted graph or traverse its edges'; Supabase persists the deployed Eliza character config while several toolbox entries lack a backend op. The visual artifact is 'a deploy-time instruction surface, not yet a durable workflow authority'.

BAML module flows generate typed content into a structured 55-module, seven-phase-gated brand system, with Supabase persisting generation status and content across sessions and human edits kept first-class via update-module-content. Regeneration of existing module content is less evidenced than initial generation; PDF/HTML/Markdown export delivers the system.

A design-code bridge where Lightning converts Figma/Penpot structure to code, Smart Regenerate targets changed frames ('instead of blindly rebuilding the whole project') and Agent Mode modifies generated UI with natural language. The design authority remains the Figma graph, but AI mutation of the generated code project and repository merge are real; merge/conflict semantics are unproven product contracts.

An Electron desktop studio where model nodes are executable and 'pass upstream outputs into later generations', making one model result a branchable intermediate; workflows and files persist locally via IPC. Humans compose the graph and AI generates media content, so authority/mutation are moderate while local persistence is durable.

Typed 3ds Max skills let an agent create materials and bind bitmaps that 'mutate real host objects' while the live Max scene and saved native file stay authoritative; viewport captures and render stats are verification projections. Rendering previews and final outputs are produced, but the designing AI is external and import/export to downstream pipelines is host-side.

An installable skill collection whose formats/instructs/validators/helpers 'bind generation to inspectable artifact workflows' — PPTX/DOCX/XLSX/PDF/images retain native authorities. Skills enable and guide an external AI rather than being the author, and revision of documents is a capability rather than a documented product loop.

A LangChain agent streams HTML slides from governed Genie data; revised fragments are 'parsed and merged without losing deck-wide CSS and scripts' and save-points add snapshots/preview/restore around edits in persistent sessions. Decks export via a bundled PPTX emitter or Google Slides, closing the loop to real deliverables.

Gemini returns three delimited artifacts (HTML/CSS/JS) that the app previews, writes to disk and zips; 'the filesystem is a transient delivery stage and the inspected app has no saved project or version history'. The AI creates the site, but output is one-shot and non-persistent.

A visual environment where saved flows are durable JSON carrying component types, configuration and data dependencies; the agentic backend includes a flow-builder assistant as 'a control path into a durable flow'. Human composition dominates and AI assistance is a secondary loop, while API/playground/deployment surfaces deliver the saved design outside the editor.

A Figma plugin where a screen prompt yields 'editable Figma objects on the current canvas — frames, named layers, auto-layout, component structure, spacing and design tokens' directly in the native document. The generation service and node-construction/regeneration semantics are closed ('no live plugin acceptance run or source repository was available'), so mutation is capped at insertion-creation evidence.

Dispatcher streams agent-authored design concepts and code into per-domain canvas renderers ('each streams a design concept and code payload independently over SSE'), so AI is the author of the diagrams. Mutation is limited: 'Persistent message branching makes alternate runs inspectable but does not imply a universal merge model', and users 'edit suitable outputs' — no evidence AI directly revises the existing canvas. Canvas and chat stores persist structured code/graph sessions and PNG/SVG are delivery projections, giving durable artifacts and exportable delivery, but the loop still relies on user editing.

Eight personas generate design artifacts — 'Blueprompt produces app and agent blueprints; Clarity creates... wireframes'; Bliss 'turns the accepted direction into tokens and production interface code' — so AI contributes the design decisions. But the dossier is architecture-level: 'generated specifications and repository code are host-agent outputs, while the plugin defines how they should be sequenced and reviewed', with no independent runtime or persistent artifact service, so mutation and artifact are only partially evidenced. Human review gates and sequencing keep the loop hands-on; delivery reaches production interface code through the host agent.

The backend 'routes generate suggestions and apply edits' from a gaze-targeted element, and component code is model-generated with validation, so AI both authors and mutates the interface. Firestore 'defines projects, ordered sections, chat sessions' and the export packages components as a TypeScript project, giving persistent editable artifact and export delivery. The gaze-dwell and user-request loop still needs sustained human steering, so human_loop is moderate.

Canvas resources and steps 'become a workflow plan and then a skill package', so AI turns user-arranged canvas intent into executable, versioned skills. 'Users can inspect, interrupt, or rerun parts of the process' and canvas synchronization keeps collaborators aligned, evidencing AI-driven iteration on a persistent canvas/versioned-skill artifact. Delivery is explicit and plural: 'forked or published, exported for Claude Code, exposed through API or MCP, or wrapped in a workflow application', but intervention remains a designed runtime feature requiring user presence.

Hyperplane renders imported URL/HTML/MCP input into live design candidates and supports quick text/image corrections on the decision surface, so AI handles candidate preparation rather than free-form authoring. Promotion to Figma layers, HTML/CSS, PDF/PNG or a live link is one-way: 'Export creates a new authority suited to the next role' with no synchronized Figma-code round trip, capping mutation and artifact. Adoption is explicitly human ('Teams can place multiple alternatives side by side compare them and decide'), but delivery spans multiple export formats and a live link.

The agent 'emits a content graph and one HTML block per frame' from normalized source material, then records frames and encodes MP4, making AI the author of the video. 'Modify intent or HTML, preview, then adopt a new render' — corrections revise graph/frame sources and re-render, so AI can revise the persistent project (project.json, content-graph.json, frames/*.html) rather than pixels. The studio still requires user review and preview-adopt decisions; no pixel-level MP4 editing or immutable version graph is established.

The agent 'adapts a template, creates SVG-backed dashboard variants, pastes them into Figma and leaves comments open for client review', so AI authors the dashboard scenes in the native host. Two mutation paths are explicit — 'SVG paste for editable vectors and text, and Figma API/plugin/MCP operations' for native properties — with change-log guidance tracing revisions. Native Figma objects and comments become the shared durable authority; the skill still requires an authorized Figma session and computer/browser control, and no rollback or stable element identity is established.

The skill 'creates an image from intent' and 'carries a supplied image into a correction turn', so AI authors and revises texture source images. The product boundary is deliberately narrow: the generated image is 'creative source material, not a physically valid PBR material', with UV/baking/material binding left to the host DCC — an explicit handoff through an AssetDescriptor rather than a closed design-delivery loop. Artifact persistence is the image plus descriptor; delivery is the handoff step, so delivery is capped.

Archon is a 'workflow control plane for AI coding agents': humans author the visual DAG/YAML ('YAML is the reviewable source') and the plane coordinates isolated worktrees, gates and artifacts, so the design of the workflow is not AI-authored. Nodes execute agent work and mutate their own Git worktrees, giving some AI mutation, and persisted definitions/events/artifacts are durable. The product is domain-general with review gates; a Remotion workflow shows it can govern a visual deliverable, but delivery is still agent-mediation toward a repository rather than a shipped design artifact.

The Skill's generator 'produces material-separated Bifrost structural graphs and instanced finish details' for six architectural styles with seeded variation, so AI authors the house structure. Generation is capped, prototypes are reused by role and partial nodes are removed after errors — mutation is generation-time rather than a demonstrated direct-edit loop on an existing scene. The '.ma scene and Bifrost graph remain the artifact authority' (durable/editable), with the user selecting style/seed and a staged review orbit keeping the loop human-led; Arnold render provides the delivery projection.

A user 'can start from a prompt or manually add and connect more than forty node types', so AI can synthesize the architecture graph but humans are a first-class author too. Named snapshots and diffs govern change review rather than a demonstrated AI direct-edit loop on the graph, and the persistence backend/diff granularity are closed — mutation is weakly evidenced. The graph itself is durable, agent-readable architecture memory exposed over MCP, with Terraform/Docker/Kubernetes/n8n exports and session bundles giving broad delivery; generated IaC still requires review and drift is acknowledged.

YamlProcessor coordinates 'filter → query → tool → conclusion → YAML', so AI generates the structured slide-update representation from natural-language instructions and retrieved data. However 'its main executable path ends at generated YAML rather than writing a final .pptx' and 'the public snapshot does not include a main-path applier', so mutation touches an intermediate authority and delivery stops at a fragment (no native deck). Persistence is task-directory based with no version graph; the research release is not a user-ready editor, so human_loop and delivery are penalized.

Figma selection becomes 'structured context / edit intent -> workspace files -> rebuilt preview' with a system figma2code Skill directing Agent to 'write implementation code into the project', so AI authors the implementation. Mutation is hybrid and strong: 'supported style/text batch handlers can directly rewrite JS-family or HTML files and then ask Agent to validate', while general edits are delegated to Agent — all against the durable workspace file working tree. The user reviews Changes/Preview and confirms Spec, and deployment is a separate clock, so human_loop and delivery are moderate despite the closed-source boundary on the visual-to-source capture layer.

The skill instructs the agent to 'propose materially different directions and render them as HTML previews', and the confirmed direction in .picasso.md 'becomes a constraint on implementation' in repository source, so AI authors the visual direction and implementation. 'Screenshot iterations reconnect visual acceptance to repository source', evidencing an AI correction loop on the persistent Git-tracked files. The user chooses or mixes directions at the decision gate; preview alternatives are 'decision aids rather than durable branches', and acceptance requires checking actual browser output, keeping the loop human-confirmed.

This is a 'visual-verification adapter' that 'does not mutate the source game or scene' — authority and mutation are near-absent by design. Its durable output is a preserved .rdc capture converted into 'bounded machine-readable and human-reviewable evidence' (thumbnails, draw-call resources, Chrome traces), which is a genuine persistent artifact. Delivery covers verification evidence and review projections rather than a designed product, so it stays in the AI-adjacent bucket consistent with bridge/infrastructure scoring.

Fusion is a 'visual IDE and agent control plane over a running repository branch': Design-mode operations sync via 'Apply Visual Changes', Fast/Plan agents implement, and the local Builder MCP 'plan and implement UI directly into current project files' — AI is the primary author and mutator of the branch filesystem. The durable convergence target is code committed to Git and delivered through provider PRs to CI/deployment, giving the strongest artifact and delivery in this batch. Human review of diffs/PRs and Apply/Implement gates remain; hosted visual-to-source capture is closed, so the mutation planner itself is not source-verified.

The architect skill 'writes an architecture document', analysis critiques it and refinement decomposes components, so AI authors the design chain artifacts from templates. 'The workflow can regenerate or revise them through Copilot skills and review them through Git', evidencing AI-driven revision of repository Markdown files that are 'authoritative'. There is no visual database or bidirectional canvas, and the output feeds ticket preparation for implementation planning rather than shipping a product, keeping it in the AI-enhanced band.

The CAD agent 'asks for build123d Python, saves the script, executes it and requires an STL export'; execution errors are 'returned to the model for a corrected full script', so AI authors parametric geometry and directly iterates on the saved script. Timestamped source and mesh files persist in the project output, and the viewer receives an STL projection. The user inspects in Three.js, revises the prompt, slices the mesh and (optionally) submits a printer job, so the loop and physical delivery remain human-driven; no STEP/BREP path limits manufacturability evidence.

DeepSeek 'returns one complete HTML document' from a template plus structured user data, and the service 'can repair missing document wrappers', so AI authors the whole page. Mutation is weak: 'The inspected flow supports regeneration but no durable project or version store' — one-shot generation without editing an existing artifact. Preview and ZIP download provide a real deliverable, but the artifact is a generated bundle without durable project persistence, so artifact is capped.

The adapter treats the Unity project as a managed product graph where agent-driven 'Scene operations create GameObjects and change transforms through Unity Undo' and source writes use 'expected SHA-256 compare-and-swap and atomically replace content' — AI directly mutates the persistent project. Compilation, Play Mode, tests, captures and builds are 'connected but separately verified states', giving durable structured artifacts and build/capture delivery. The agent must reconnect to the same request ID after assembly reload and the user reviews, so the loop is not fully automatic.

The plugin 'sends actual Maya API work through the UI dispatcher' producing 'ordinary DAG, DG, Bifrost, material, animation and render structures visible to Maya users', so AI authors native scene content and directly mutates persistent Maya state. Project attachment, readiness and persistent jobs with cancellation/recovery by job identity distinguish it from one-shot scripts, and the scene is the durable authority. The user operates inside Maya and reviews staged work, and rendering/pipeline operations provide delivery projections rather than a self-contained shipped artifact.

The agent 'receives the current diagram and returns changes to an established XML canvas rather than replacing it with an image', so AI both authors and directly mutates the persisted draw.io XML. 'Generated or modified XML is loaded into the embedded draw.io runtime, where users retain ordinary object-level editing', evidencing a durable editable canvas with visible updates. The dossier notes review remains necessary ('They do not validate system semantics or guard every concurrent write'), and delivery is PNG/.drawio XML/Mermaid exports rather than a closed production loop.

OpenAIService 'receives both an instruction and current Mermaid for modification' and 'the response returns to the same editor used for direct keystrokes', so AI revises the same source string a person sees — direct mutation of the authoritative artifact. DiagramStorageService owns local project records and the editor joins library, preview and export, giving durable projects and SVG/PNG delivery. There is 'no collaborative branch model or semantic node graph beyond Mermaid syntax', and the user drives each instruction, so human_loop and delivery are moderate.

DCC LookDev 'relies on host adapters for mutations but owns the calibration and review contract' — the AI-authored output is a repeatable scene recipe, typed HDR recommendations and acceptance evidence, not the designed artifact itself. 'Native Maya, Blender, Houdini or Unreal scenes remain authoritative', so authority and mutation sit with the host workflows. The turntable setup is durable and portable, and its delivery is comparable review scenes/acceptance evidence rather than a shipped design.

Modeling calls 'are executed in FreeCAD's Python runtime, the dependency graph is recomputed and the staged document is accepted only when the requested invariants hold', so AI performs safe, validated mutation of the native .FCStd parametric document whose features remain authoritative. 'Failures leave the original bytes unchanged' and STEP/IGES/BREP/STL/OBJ are interchange outputs derived from that authority, evidencing durable structured artifact and validated delivery. The agent-driven session loop requires human review of staged results, so human_loop is moderate.

This is a 'visual authoring layer over the TFrameX multi-agent framework': the user composes agent/tool/pattern/trigger nodes into a graph and a flow translator converts it to TFrameX orchestration, so the AI system design is human-authored. 'Changing a node changes a durable runtime definition rather than only its appearance', and PostgreSQL/Alembic retain flows and runs with JSON import/export, giving persistent typed artifacts. Triggers turn a draft into executable automation, but JSON paths are 'not described as lossless code round-tripping' and the human composes the graph, keeping it AI-enhanced.

The add-on 'embeds the HTTP service, operation queue and monitoring panel inside Blender' to expose operations to orchestrating agents, so AI (via agents like PolyMCP) drives modeling/materials/animation mutations into the canonical running scene and saved '.blend'. Thread-safe queuing resolves agent concurrency into Blender's main-thread mutation model, evidencing real mutation of a durable artifact. The add-on 'owns safe access, not creative state', delivery is interchange/render operations, and the orchestration client is not the artifact authority, so authority and delivery are moderate.

Galileo 'turns... intent directly into UI screens': one prompt produces multiple generated screen variants, retry addresses failed screen_ids and theme changes regenerate a message's screens asynchronously — AI is the author of the variants. Refinement lineage ('based_on_screen_id') and partial retry are real, but 'no public contract exposes an immutable version graph, transactional rollback or a reverse binding', and theme edits are constrained regeneration rather than node-graph mutation, capping mutation. The hosted screen-lineage thread is durable and the only outward delivery is one-way HTML clipboard paste into Figma plus share pages, so delivery is a fragment relative to a closed loop.

Puter.js 'calls Puter AI for strict JSON containing HTML, CSS and JavaScript' to create a three-layer site, and the source 'makes this substitution visible' when a fixed fallback is used, so AI is the author with an explicit fallback boundary. Mutation is weak: saved projects support load/delete but there is 'no immutable revision chain' and regeneration is one-shot rather than direct edits to an existing artifact. MongoDB-backed saved bundles own recovery and the ZIP/preview give real delivery, so artifact and delivery are moderate.

Agents directly read and write the hosted design file via 21 MCP tools (create_artboard, write_html, update_styles, move/duplicate/delete nodes) with id-addressed mutation of persistent nodes ('update_styles', 'move_nodes' preserve ids). Artifact is a durable hosted node graph with real-time collaboration. Human still opens/selects the file and reviews changes, so loop is agent-assisted rather than fully end-to-end; delivery spans media exports, JSX projections and design-to-code handoff.

FlowSpect is a verifier that normalizes exported agent graphs into a typed IR and propagates taint, emitting terminal/JSON/SARIF findings; it 'never runs the agent' and does not author or mutate the workflow. The decision artifact is analysis output (node path + remediation), and delivery is a CI/security report rather than a shipped design. Score reflects the bridge/verification shape: high automation once rules are written, low authority and mutation.

AI generates candidate frames/options that the user must accept ('select / Looks good'), then AI-assisted erase/frame-restyle/rewrite edits refine the chosen canvas project. Artifact is a cloud-saved Designer project with OneDrive-backed assets, though 'some AI operations may flatten their selected region' and editability is not always vector-semantic. Human drives selection and refinement at every step, and output is delivered via download/share/Microsoft apps.

The model inspects a compact board summary and calls typed tools to 'draw native Excalidraw structures or patch existing elements by ID', with the client materializing events into the live Excalidraw scene — genuine AI-authored mutation of the visual. However the artifact is session/client state: 'the pinned source does not durably save boards... database insertion, snapshots and Excalidraw-room integration [are] incomplete', so persistence and delivery are penalized.

This is an MCP adapter that validates a ComfyUI workflow, submits it as an asynchronous job and retrieves artifacts; 'ComfyUI remains the execution authority' and the adapter 'does not invent a second hidden generation state'. It does not author or mutate the design graph, only enables iteration by re-submitting revised graphs. Artifact is the editable workflow JSON and job-attached outputs, delivered as retrieved media — a bridge, correctly scored low on authority/mutation.

The node-connected canvas is the continuing project artifact where 'an Agent can arrange nodes and choose among virtual try-on, detail-page composition, video and free-creation tools', with identity locks and reusable technique templates tying operations to the same graph. Human still prepares references and drives the graph; export produces delivery images, long pages or video. Node serialization and model routing are undisclosed (closed surface), capping evidence.

Groq authors a complete HTML document into a Mongo website record with title, owner, slug and conversation, and corrections replace `latestcode` only after 'another valid full-document response' — regeneration rather than surgical edit, so mutation is weak. Durable record and publication to a public slug URL deliver a deployed site; Monaco manual edits are not posted back, and no immutable version lineage exists.

A React Flow prototype where text-to-workflow generation can 'create the same graph shape from a prompt' and complete graph JSON is serialized to draft/published directories. The Realtime test path merely 'embeds the graph JSON in session instructions' with no interpreter, so publication is a state transition without runtime provisioning. Versioning/self-healing are roadmap claims not implemented in the pinned source.

The skill asks an agent to deliver a self-contained HTML document with an embedded diagram; the output is one-shot generation with no agent iteration on an existing artifact (only human drag/position stored in localStorage). The HTML file is authoritative for delivery and is a portable, usable document, but it is not a collaborative native graph service — lightweight source-authority projection only.

A tool-calling code agent mutates a reconstructed VirtualFileSystem during the streamed response — 'file creation, string replacement, rename, delete and Figma tools operate on that graph' — with a large design corpus supplying context. Authored projects persist messages and the serialized file graph on completion. Preview is sandboxed-iframe projection; direct manual edits are not shown crossing the server boundary until a save-producing workflow runs, and no hosted export step is evidenced.

Automated extraction supplies a starting screenplay breakdown but 'every result can be corrected or cleared', and the MCP server is deliberately read-only so agents can never rewrite the editorial source — AI initiates, humans own edits, and mutation is not AI-driven. The `.scriptbreak` JSON project is a strong durable artifact (scenes, characters, bibles, schedules, timeline), and scoped prompt packs/schedules/export queries provide delivery.

Gemini planner/generator/explainer roles produce source that is validated against a component registry and retried on unsupported components, so AI authors and iterates on the code in-browser. But 'persistence ends with the browser session because no durable project store is connected' and export/hosted delivery 'remain outside this repository' — the artifact is disposable session state and delivery is only an iframe preview.

Drag-and-Swap is a visual composition tool for trading agents: humans build the node graph (stored per-wallet in local storage) and the runtime 'traverses downstream blocks from triggers' to execute real swap actions. No generative AI authors or mutates the design — AI is the composed agent runtime, so authority and mutation are near-tooling level. Artifact is durable per-wallet graph state; delivery is live execution in the browser.

In-editor Flowpilot 'can start from a prompt, source code or screenshot, or refine the current canvas', with a parser round trip preserved so 'a round trip must preserve relationships and editable semantics' and one repair turn on failed DSL. The canvas and OpenFlow DSL are two editors over one persistent graph in IndexedDB with snapshots. Human review is light (agents repair parse failures automatically), and exports span JSON/SVG/PNG/PDF/video/Mermaid/PlantUML; the MCP path is deliberately narrower.

CICADA generates build123d-oriented CAD code, executes it through the kernel and runs a visual-feedback loop where QA modules 'compare those renders with the refined design goal and issue corrections' — AI-authored geometry with direct source repair. Source code preserves editable construction intent, but the dossier explicitly bounds it as 'an operable research framework, not a PDM system... or production release workflow', capping delivery.

Seko moves from idea to structured story, visual assets, storyboard and timeline with subjects/scenes as 'reusable project entities' rather than regenerating each shot; image edits apply back to selected storyboard frames and every modification instruction enters generation history. It is 'a managed project graph with candidate history and promotion, not a one-shot media endpoint'. Backend persistence and generation internals are closed, so artifact and mutation rely on the public app contract.

ForgeAI moves prompt → structured blueprint → files with conversational refinement and bounded version restore: snapshots 'deep-copy both blueprint and files' and restore writes both back, giving real AI-driven mutation of a persistent project. Persistence is browser-local (localStorage with up to 25 versions), so durability and multi-device delivery are limited; export/deployment surfaces take copies of the selected project state.

Users define agents and wire retrieval/approval/evaluation/export nodes; the backend topologically orders the saved React Flow graph and real Anthropic calls execute configured agents, preserving run traces, citations and graph snapshots. The AI executes the workflow rather than mutating the design graph, and control-flow is capped ('branch-specific suspension and resume-from-node semantics are not established'). Delivery is a client-ready DOCX report.

Gemini produces a one-shot Mermaid explanation from retrieved document context, rendered in a modal; 'there is no implemented diagram record, source editor or version history' and closing the modal ends the artifact lifecycle. AI authorship of the diagram is real, but mutation is absent and the artifact is ephemeral — the dossier itself notes it represents a thin, weakest-persistence end of the batch.

Gemini authors source through conversational research/generation and an optional Google Stitch step can 'send the result through Stitch for refinement' — AI-authored components with a refinement branch. Project files, chat and activity hydrate via sessionStorage, so recovery is limited to the current browser session with no server-side version archive. Sandpack runtime previews current files and export packages the graph as a ZIP so delivery matches preview.

Clai runs a staged product-generation pipeline from brief and reference image to GLB model and packaging panels; 'a chat edit creates a later result without erasing the chosen earlier one', preserving per-version model outputs in a persisted project snapshot (Redis + file fallback). Human correction happens on the directly adjustable packaging dieline, and file_export materializes GLB/texture handoff files — early working design workspace, not yet parametric CAD.

The harness wraps installed Claude Code/Codex CLIs that 'edit the same project directory' containing the HTML working artifact, with prompt-builder feeding project structure, design-system files and pinned canvas comments back into each turn. Checkpoints snapshot the project tree before every turn and revert restores files rather than hiding a chat message — strong persistent mutation. Exporters (PDF/PPTX/handoff) consume the source; durability is local-first.

ÉTER's public contract is a six-step site lifecycle: guided brief → generated copy/content → user adjusts colors, typography and layout → preview → publish on a tenant-specific domain, so AI authors the site within 'a constrained design system' where visible parameters are the correction surface. Publishing to a tenant domain is first-class, a strong delivery loop. Application source and data model are private, so mutation depth and storage schema are unverifiable and penalized.

Architecture lives in repository-resident YAML (the durable working authority) while diagrams/docs are generated projections; the agent reads the contract and produces 'questions, analysis, and proposed updates', and drift checking reports divergence — but a developer must promote every change ('update the model, update the code, or explain the exception'). AI proposes rather than commits, so authority/mutation stay moderate.

Local Ollama generates website/React/MERN file graphs stored as MongoDB generation records ('prompts, generated content, type and ownership'); history opens records as distinct generations, 'not presented as an append-only version graph inside a single artifact', so AI iteration is regeneration rather than mutation of one artifact. Preview projects supported web output and download packages the selected generation for delivery.

Kintsugi compiles source annotations into a `kintsugi.json` contract that governs editable/locked/AI-only/human-only regions and validates agent procedures against declared surfaces — infrastructure that constrains editing rather than authoring designs. The core parser/validator/registry with per-annotation revision and rollback are working source, but the advertised CLI/runtime sidecar 'remain incomplete', so delivery of the CMS experience is partial; authority is correctly low for a bridge.

Gemini returns native Excalidraw data normalized into editable elements — 'the renderer is therefore also the editing surface' with no screenshot reconstruction — and the whiteboard editor debounce-saves to Firestore with preview thumbnails, making human post-edits part of the saved artifact. AI does not iterate on the existing board (mutation is human-side), and no export path beyond the saved board is evidenced.

The skill owns the complete deck loop: brainstorm the argument, generate a reviewable React/HTML deck, capture point comments and export editable PPTX, image PPTX, standalone HTML or PDF — a strong delivery surface. Layouts consume a theme contract so brand tokens survive across 34 layouts. Mutation evidence is moderate because the deck is generated and then copied out of the skill to evolve in the user's project; HTML/React remains the review authority.

Aria 'can create a whole site, page, section or custom element and configure business capabilities', continuously mutating the same managed Wix site graph that humans then edit with pixel-level drag-and-drop; the agent stays available across editor and dashboard rather than handing off a one-shot snapshot. Delivery is hosted publication with built-in commerce/bookings infrastructure. Implementation is closed, so internal patch planning and version restore are unproven but the product contract is clear.

vCAD unifies visual editor, MCP and in-product AI chat around one `.vcad` document whose mutations reach a Rust exact-geometry BRep kernel; the changelog records 'text-to-CAD and higher-level AI tools' as shipped, so AI both creates and edits the persistent model. The document 'survives every control surface' with versioned cloud persistence, history and sharing — a strong durable artifact — with export/share delivery and human oversight via the editor and chat.

Figma plugin where "AI UX Writer agent" produces suggested product copy that the designer reviews in Figma, so AI writes content but the design artifact stays human-owned. Dossier explicitly says implementation, prompt construction and persistence are closed and that "no direct node mutation" is documented, so mutation is penalized as no evidence. Suggestion-only output with no durable generated-copy history or shipped deliverable keeps artifact/delivery low.

Visual editor over a running front end where "inline text edits and element movement are translated into source changes" and connected coding agents produce the source patch, so AI and human co-edit the same authoritative source tree. "Source files remain canonical and Git provides review and recovery" gives a durable editable artifact, and the loop ends in "Git commit / branch / PR", so mutation and delivery score high. Human selects each element and expresses each correction, which keeps human_loop moderate.

Bridge/transport between Figma and self-hosted n8n/REST workflows: "MKitFlow supplies transport and native mutation capability; the user owns the n8n/REST workflow, model, prompts and credentials," so the product does not itself define the design AI (rule 6 bridge shape). Returned direct commands can mutate the native Figma canvas and reports return to the workflow, which justifies 4 on mutation/delivery. Heavy user setup (workflow, prompts, endpoint trust) and webhook-message persistence keep artifact/human_loop low.

AI creates only a raster decal from a text prompt via DALL-E while "the user applies that image to a fixed shirt scene", so AI authoring is limited to one texture component of a canned 3D scene. Generation is one-shot image creation with no AI iteration on the existing scene (mutation 2), and "the scene state is not persisted as an editable project" (artifact 3). It ends in a downloadable rendered canvas, delivering a preview image rather than an editable design.

Packaged ChatGPT workflow that turns paper facts into framework-figure candidate images, with "prompt packages, issue ledgers and checkpoints" carrying the decision trail, so AI authors visual candidates under staged human direction selection. "Generated images are review candidates, not an editable graph" and default output is not editable SVG/PPTX, penalizing artifact and delivery. The assistant "explicitly stops at S5; final selection and manual completion remain human work", keeping human_loop low.

Agent-operated production discipline where the calling agent authors medium-native artifacts (HTML prototypes, editable PPTX, motion) behind a shared workflow that "requires multiple directions before convergence" and refines the chosen direction, so AI is the primary author and iterates. "Sibling candidate files preserve alternatives; the selected editable source advances" under filesystem/Git persistence gives a durable editable artifact. Human selects directions and verifies before handoff, and verification scripts and exportable deliverables close the delivery loop.

Aida builds a small-business site conversationally from an example or description into a "managed site project" and "the user can ask for further changes or use manual tools at any time including after publishing", so AI and human co-edit the same managed project authority. Managed pages, responsive variants, forms, commerce and domain state constitute a durable editable artifact. Delivery is complete: "subdomain or connected-domain release" on one.com hosting; evidence ceiling on patch granularity and version recovery keeps authority/human_loop from reaching 9+.

Deterministic browser materializer plus agent skill: HTML is measured and "reconstructed as editable native PowerPoint text, shapes, vectors, images, transitions and animations", so conversion rather than design generation is the core (authority/mutation low per rule 6). The produced ".pptx becomes a distinct native editing authority" — a durable, structured, editable artifact — and validation + normalization give repeatable delivery. Human runs the skill and validates output, so human_loop is moderate.

The model plans a constrained UI graph from intent while "incremental intent mutates UIPlan" and the planner "distinguishes modify from regenerate", so AI authors and directly iterates the design representation. "versionStore retains version snapshots used for selection and replay" and "the plan remains the recoverable authority", a durable structured artifact. A deterministic generator renders React UI, giving a concrete deliverable, though deployment/publishing is not evidenced so delivery stays at 6.

OpenRouter-hosted model generates component source and "the accepted component stays in an editable workspace where source editing and property-level controls converge before preview and export", so AI does primary generation and human co-edits. AI regeneration is the mutation path but regeneration-from-scratch rather than direct repair of the existing artifact, and Session.js persists "conversation and current generated code" without a guaranteed immutable version. export.js packages the component for delivery.

Visual-judgment skill set that "reads screenshots or existing interfaces... then produces a review or ranking" and explicitly "does not own the implementation canvas", so AI evaluates rather than creates the design (authority low). There is no mutation path onto the artifact (mutation 2). Structured audit reports and rankings are evidence-bearing documents, and "human review is explicitly required", so artifact/delivery sit at 4.

AI-native EDA kernel that "accepts intent through SDK, CLI, REST or MCP, then carries a board through schematic construction, ERC, placement, routing, DRC and manufacturing export", so AI constructs the engineering design from intent. The normalized design model is the construction authority and native KiCad files become a downstream authority; proof packs and round-trip fixtures persist with the design. Automated stages and manufacturing export (Gerber/Excellon/BOM) deliver a finished output; explicit iteration on the model is not the documented loop, so mutation is moderate.

DeepPresenter makes "one HTML file per slide the working generative authority" and agents plan, author slides, then render and reflect: "Invalid HTML-to-PPTX conversion or visibly defective composition can therefore return to the file authority for another edit", an explicit AI repair loop over a persistent artifact. HTML workspace is the editable authority and the ".pptx" is materialized delivery. The loop is agent-driven with visual reflection as an execution gate, so authority/mutation/artifact/delivery are all high and human oversight is mostly review.

Gemini returns "one self-contained HTML document and the React client treats that exact document as both source and iframe input", so AI authors the full site in a single shot. There is no edit/iteration path on the generated document — generation is one-shot (mutation 2) — and "no persistent project graph is committed". The HTML file is a durable editable source previewed via srcDoc, but delivery is limited to previewing the document.

OpenRouter "sends a prompt through OpenRouter and expects a complete HTML response" and writes the accepted result to the data directory, so AI authors the entire site document. Iteration means replacing the whole document ("OpenRouter replaces the whole document") with no element-level mutation, and history is file-granular JSON without branching or semantic diffs. Preview and download HTTP paths use the same file for proof and delivery, giving a usable delivered HTML artifact.

MCP bridge that gives an external agent structured control of a live Grasshopper definition — component creation, wiring, movement, values, solve — so the agent performs real design mutations while "the external model never becomes the geometric kernel" and Rhino/Grasshopper stay authoritative (authority moderate as a bridge). The ".gh or .ghx remains the durable definition", a first-class editable artifact. Definitions can be saved through the live host but no finished shipped result or full version control is evidenced, keeping delivery at 5.

Gemini produces a structured strategy analysis and a landing-page prototype, and "both initial generation and AI refinement replace website_html and append the new document to website_history", so AI authors and can regenerate the site. Mutation is whole-document replacement with a retained history rather than element-level repair. Database persistence keeps strategy and website in inspectable versioned histories, and the UI previews, lists and downloads current or historical documents, closing a visible delivery path.

The named styles themselves are a curated human-maintained catalog; the agent skill selects and applies one, and export APIs "materialize the chosen direction as tokens, CSS variables, framework themes and AI rules", so AI applies a pre-defined style rather than inventing it (authority moderate). Exported tokens become "source-level constraints inside the target project", mutating that project's durable token/CSS state and delivering a concrete implementation contract; the catalog is not the decisive artifact.

Gemini is asked for tagged multi-file output and the server "materializes them under one generated-site directory", installs dependencies and launches Vite, so AI authors the whole site as a filesystem workspace. At the inspected commit this is "a single shared workspace with an in-memory prompt cache rather than isolated persisted projects", so there is no iteration path on existing output (mutation 2) and no reload-safe persistence. Execution via Vite and a download endpoint give a runnable, deliverable site.

Gemini generates HTML/CSS/JS/scripts as structured output and "element-targeted refinement accepts element context and requested changes", so AI authors the site and can mutate existing generated source by carrying a selected DOM target back to the generation path. Layers are inspectable before combination but "the inspected code does not establish durable server projects or historical snapshots", so persistence stops at the active browser workspace (artifact/delivery 5).

Agents move "from problem framing to visual alternatives, record decisions, and only then convert the agreed experience into production code", where wireframes and HTML prototypes are concrete visual artifacts the agents author and refine as a "living HTML specification". It is a delivery methodology (skill/command library) rather than a self-running tool, so the agent's authoring depends on the host agent, and decision logs provide a persistent trace. Production code downstream extends the loop to real delivery.

A coding agent writes parametric CAD source (part.py/params.json) and the desktop MCP server exposes rebuild as "the trusted verification entry" that regenerates geometry, populates caches and returns screenshots to the agent, so AI authors and iteratively repairs the persistent code-first artifact. The model package separates editable sources from preview styling, making the design durable and editable. Geometry (BREP/MJCF) and screenshots are delivered to the agent and viewer, closing a real CAD loop.

Agent-operable video editor where "the running Electron main process owns a mutable timeline graph" that the embedded terminal, CLI, HTTP bridge and MCP can mutate, so AI can directly create and edit timeline/Canvas content of real video projects. However "those surfaces do not converge on one authority": project state spans six kinds of truth with split-brain MCP writes, no project-wide undo and no versioning, penalizing artifact. FFmpeg export renders the timeline to a deliverable video, giving a real shipped result.

A design agent defines parts and bounding-box contracts, part agents implement them in Python, and "a vision judge can send failures back into the source", so AI authors the 3D model and iteratively repairs its own code artifact. "Code is the recoverable authority" — design.json, per-part builders and assembly code persist as editable files while renders/GLB/URDF are disposable projections. Blender headlessly measures and verifies and outputs previews/GLB/URDF, delivering tangible 3D assets.

Gemini reasons through a LangGraph ReAct loop over "bounded read write edit and list operations so the model mutates a named project graph", giving AI direct authorship and iterative mutation of persistent files. "SQL retains the project outside the model context" as durable project/file state, making the artifact recoverable. Sandpack provides runtime proof and github.py publishes the project to GitHub, closing a delivery loop to a deployed repository.

Multi-agent campaign coordination where the Designer "specifies composition, subjects, lighting, palette... and an image-generation prompt" but "the pinned system has no such rendering tool", so AI's qualifying output is a reviewed campaign specification rather than finished visual media (authority/delivery limited). Critique routes revision requests back to Copywriter and Designer with bounded revisions, giving an iteration loop over documents. Notion persistence is delivery coordination, not visual authority; no branchable campaign document or durable image lineage is established.

Phase-ordered agent method where content, structure and visual design are produced in order and "design tokens and approved style packs are applied only after the information architecture is settled", so the agent authors the office document under strong process control. The delivered office file is authoritative and editable (strongest for DOCX; richer PPTX/XLSX presets are roadmap, not implemented evidence). A final checklist separates content/structure/visual/technical defects as review evidence, so human QA remains part of the loop.

Method-and-template library whose structured deliverables (research plans, audit reports, journey maps, token architectures, component specs, handoff checklists) "coordinate decisions and reviews, but the host agent and the consuming repository still own any actual implementation or rendered artifact". Because "no independent renderer, persistence service or mutation runtime is present", mutation is 2 and artifact/delivery are limited to evidence-bearing documents. Authority stays moderate since skills shape AI output rather than directly producing finished design artifacts.

AI Build agent turns intent into complete project source, and Preview Toolbar selections/annotations flow into the main chat and durable code versions. Mutation is strong: Build edits existing project code with automatic versions, two-way Git sync and revert, while publishing deploys an explicit snapshot to a Lovable/custom domain. Human loop is lightly penalized because plan approval, explicit publishing and task-queue management remain human gates.

generate.ts makes Gemini return a complete HTML document with light/dark rules and primary color, so AI authors the full design artifact. Mutation is penalized: direct code edits 'bypass regeneration' and prompt history restores snapshots, but no evidence shows AI incrementally editing the existing document rather than regenerating it wholesale. Artifact is durable (self-contained HTML plus localStorage snapshot history) and delivery is closed via Copy/Download.

The skill maps workflows and writes a structured Markdown review, and 'deliberately does not silently rewrite the application', so AI critiques rather than authors the design (authority low) and cannot mutate the app (mutation 2). The review file is a durable decision artifact, but delivery stops at a coordination report rather than a shipped result; no evidence for iterative mutation.

AI generates editable vector illustrations from prompt/preset/reference and inserts native SVGs into Figma, so AI authors the artwork. Mutation is moderate: generation history reuses prompts and styles for batch re-insertion, but the dossier does not show AI editing inserted vectors in place after Figma owns them. Artifact is durable (generation history plus native Figma objects) and delivery includes insertion and ZIP export; no evidence for model, sanitization or node-decomposition internals.

This is an execution/rendering service for external agents: 'HTTP and MCP commands invoke a CAD/OpenSCAD engine', so the product is infrastructure and AI-vs-human design authority is low per rule 6. It can mutate the CAD model through executable modeling commands and exports STL/STEP/3MF plus dimensioned blueprints, giving solid artifact and delivery scores; the PNG render is explicitly feedback, not the model.

Gemini generates the full three-file website and follow-up chat 'includes current source so corrections replace rather than merely describe the project', showing AI iteration on the existing artifact. Artifact is the structured website with session-state versions (history lost on session loss, so artifact penalized) and delivery is real: deploy.py calls GitHub APIs to commit files and enable Pages plus ZIP export.

The skill turns a style description/screenshot/Figma reference into coordinated tokens, spec, preview and delivery package, so AI authors the design system; 'the user reviews the visual preview and specification before treating the token set as authority'. Mutation is moderate because later agents consume the local token files rather than a documented AI in-place edit loop over them.

Gemini extracts a room profile and Stability AI performs polygon-masked inpaint/restyle transforms, so AI executes the design transformation on the uploaded photo. Mutation is partial: every edit endpoint restarts from the original image_url, so history is sibling proposals, not 'an automatically chained edit graph'. Artifact is durable user-scoped room/edit records in Supabase but the visual artifact remains a raster lineage, and delivery is an edited JPEG download.

The agent declares logical topology and containment while the layout engine deterministically computes coordinates, so AI authors diagram structure with tool-assisted placement (authority mid). Mutation is solid: the CLI renders PNG so the agent can 'inspect and rectify visible defects' in the authoritative Draw.io XML. Editable XML persists as the artifact and PNG is disposable visual evidence; delivery is the renderable .drawio file.

The generation route asks the model for complete project files and the improve route 'supplies the current graph and applies file-level updates on later turns', so AI authors and iterates on a React file graph. Prisma persists the current workspace/conversation (artifact strong, though 'no independent version table' limits recovery) and Sandpack syncs source editing with ZIP export for delivery; no evidence of a full publish pipeline.

project_pipeline.py drives planning/design/development with typed intermediate decisions, and reviewer.py 'can send them through bounded revision loops', showing AI authoring plus AI mutation of generated pages. Files remain authoritative in the workspace while SQLite persists metadata/memory, and preview serving plus ZIP export close an exportable delivery loop.

Browser-side Gemini constructs the website prompt call and normalizes the response into complete HTML, so AI authors the whole document. Mutation is penalized: the Mongo model 'contains no immutable versions collection; saving a revision changes the project authority rather than creating a recoverable historical branch', and no AI in-place edit of saved docs is evidenced. Delivery is download/community sharing only, not real hosting.

The dedicated UI agent turns a brief or sketch into multi-screen prototypes and 'colors typography spacing components and interaction choices are remembered across sessions', so AI authors and continuously revises the prototype by conversation. Artifact is a hosted multi-screen prototype with persistent project memory (schema unknown, so not a 9-10), and delivery stops at visual prototyping and sharing with 'no code output'.

The design contract says the agent writes files under an output directory and renders HTML in a sandboxed iframe, positioning AI as the author of interactive charts/dashboards for non-technical teams. This is architecture-depth only: the repository 'contains documentation and screenshots but no application implementation', so mutation semantics, persistence internals and the claimed runtime are unproven and penalized per rules 4-5.

A five-stage pipeline forces vision output into a validated layout DSL before code generation, and validator 'can repair the DSL' while reflection can reject and trigger another pass, so AI authors React from screenshots and iterates within the pipeline. Artifact is penalized: the accepted code is inspectable in Monaco but 'the inspected source does not establish a durable project or version service'; delivery is copy/download.

OpenAI's Responses API returns a complete self-contained page that becomes the adopted generatedCode, so AI authors the entire artifact. Mutation is weak: 'Correction is a deliberate copy-back step' where the human edits editorCode and Apply replaces the adopted document; no evidence AI directly edits the persisted artifact. The HTML is previewable and downloadable (delivery 7) but refreshing loses it, penalizing artifact.

YouWare's agent generates a working React application and "Visual edits and AI edits ... converge on the same working code and runtime", so AI authors the app and iterates it in place (authority 7, mutation 7). DreamUI generates editable screens, multi-screen products and variants from prompts, screenshots or HTML, making AI the primary designer (authority 7). Output lands as an "editable Figma graph" in native canvas — durable and structured (artifact 8); the user drives prompts/selection while generation and edits apply automatically (human_loop 6), and delivery stays inside Figma with tokens/UI-kit/code output rather than a published surface (delivery 5).

AI generates the story, scene descriptions, per-scene images and ElevenLabs narration, i.e. the actual creative content (authority 8). The typed component object is structured but kept only in React state, not durable (artifact 4); generation is automatic once prompted (human_loop 5), and nothing is delivered beyond rendering in the workspace (delivery 3).

The open skill structures a figure and generates raster drafts, while the hosted platform offers multi-round editing with editable text layers and layered SVG/PPTX, so AI authors and iterates figures (authority 6, mutation 5). Gemini is asked separately for the master plan, design document, CSS and section templates, so AI authors the website from a brief (authority 7), but the pipeline is a single one-way run with no evidence of AI revising earlier output (mutation 2). FastBuild123d converts annotated build123d code into a live browser editor and is counted as visual-editor infrastructure, not a CAD agent — the AI's role is preparing parametric models via a skill (authority 2). Parameter/geometry updates are human-driven control manipulation rather than AI iteration (mutation 2). Bridge compiles a YAML CSpec through resolve+lint into a scene graph and then to Figma Plugin API operations, with compliance "guaranteed by deterministic resolution and lint rules before execution" — the model supplies the CSpec but the architecture is a deterministic compiler (authority 3). The versionable knowledge-base registry plus CSpec/history are durable structured state (artifact 6); manual correction is captured as learning with automatic execution (human_loop 5), and it delivers compiled, traceable native Figma graph changes (delivery 5).

Design Canvas explicitly "does not generate designs from prompts; another tool or coding agent does that" and renders live routes of an already-running app, so its own authority over the design is minimal (authority 2).
