Saved frame/section topology survives restart as a structured canvas artifact, with documents/images path-addressed (artifact 5); an external agent drives the canvas and the human reviews source edits (human_loop 5), and delivery is bounded visual-verification evidence rather than a shipped product (delivery 3).

Bunyan turns a plot and Arabic requirements into a proposed home, so AI generates the design from intent (authority 6), and conversational voice/chat revision "appears to update the same project and 3D result" — iteration on a persistent project (mutation 6). The auto-saving hosted home project is durable managed state, with no public version/diff detail (artifact 6); users revise and inspect in 3D while the tool drives generation (human_loop 5), and it advances toward cost estimate, CAD/PDF export and contractor handoff, though permit/CAD readiness is not proven (delivery 6).

AI generates the project from a prompt and "Failures can move through deterministic fixes, AI repair and per-file rollback before approval", so it authors and repairs the artifact (authority 7, mutation 7). Projects and file maps persist in IndexedDB while version snapshots are in-memory and lost on restart (artifact 6); acceptance checks and smoke gates run automatically but require human approval (human_loop 6), and delivery is a ZIP export of the project rather than a published result (delivery 5).

Specialized agents coordinate schematic/PCB/firmware/BOM/manufacturing work around KiCad and PlatformIO, with ERC/DRC checking and Gerber/BOM export, but "template-based schematic assembly ... still being developed" so full board generation is not proven (authority 4). Appy Pie's AI generates multiple interface directions from a description and continues the chosen result through conversational changes and a drag-and-drop editor, so AI is the primary designer (authority 7) and the artifact is iterated (mutation 6). Design tokens, wireframes and prototype views persist inside the managed Appy Pie project (artifact 7); the user refines via conversation and DnD editing (human_loop 5), and delivery ranges from PNG/SVG/HTML/CSS exports to a hosted domain or mobile application (delivery 7). Internal layout graph and round-trip fidelity are undisclosed.

The Gemini-backed route turns prompts into editable Mermaid source, so AI authors the diagram (authority 6), and chart revisions are persisted server-side with restore to saved state, while editor corrections are manual (mutation 5). Accounts, charts and historical versions in Express/MongoDB form durable structured product objects (artifact 7); the user prompts and manually corrects in the editor (human_loop 5), and delivery is a shareable managed diagram without code/diagram export beyond the app (delivery 5).

Language analyzers and dependency graphs build module context and then the documentation agent writes pages and Mermaid diagrams — AI authors the documentation model (authority 6). The str_replace editor tools can replace invalid or stale document fragments and generation is scoped over modules, so artifacts are repaired and maintained (mutation 6). The generated docs model with metadata and analysis JSON is durable and navigable (artifact 7); the workflow is run-then-review with MCP access for external agents (human_loop 5), and delivery is a maintainable documentation model rather than a deployed artifact (delivery 5).

AI generates a visual workflow graph, workflow.json and an Airflow DAG from a natural-language request, grounded in a retrieved API catalog (authority 6). MasterGo AI generates whole interfaces/components from intent, references or design.md and, in Agent mode, "directly calls canvas-editing capabilities" mutating the current file in place — AI is the author and iterates the native graph (authority 8, mutation 8). The MasterGo file with vector layers, components, styles, collaboration and history is a durable structured authoritative artifact (artifact 9); human and AI co-edit the same file with user-controlled tool-confirmation policy (human_loop 7), and it materializes React/Vue/mini-program code as a projection plus usable design-system content (delivery 7).

The Design Critique skill inspects an interface and "writes prioritized findings rather than offering unscoped aesthetic advice" — AI authors a review, not the design (authority 3), and target source/design files "retain mutation authority", so there is no mutation (mutation 1). The review artifact is a structured findings document that coordinates later work (artifact 4); the skill is invoked manually and follow-up work is manual (human_loop 4), and it delivers only a critique fragment with no renderer or canvas (delivery 2).

Claude can author a validated agent graph and lay it out on the canvas, so AI creates the designed workflow (authority 6), and the same React Flow objects drive editing and execution with results streamed into node state (mutation 5). The graph persists in browser local storage as the complete project — structured but browser-local with no shared access or revision history (artifact 5); users draw or prompt and the orchestrator runs connected agents automatically (human_loop 5), and execution produces real Claude results closing the run loop without external deployment (delivery 5).

The director and specialist skills author game source, assets and UI across gameplay/graphics/UI/VFX, with specialists able to "revise HUDs, materials, lighting, VFX, models and interaction" — AI creates and iterates the game (authority 7, mutation 7). Repository code and checked-in assets remain authoritative via the WebGL canvas projection with test baselines (artifact 7); a developer drives the skills through orchestrated rounds and QA gates (human_loop 5), and the QA/release skill checks static-host readiness to ship the browser game (delivery 6).

OpenDesign routes requests to wireframe, prototype, deck, frontend and tweakable-artifact specialists and commissions a separate verifier against the brief, so AI authors the designs inside local coding agents (authority 7) and iterates through specialist rounds plus verification (mutation 6). Project-local design systems and HTML artifacts are durable, editable media with a local preview server (artifact 6); the agent-driven loop needs human steering and briefs (human_loop 5), and an explicit handoff skill translates accepted artifacts into implementation work (delivery 5).

AI rebuilds flat/semi-flat images into semantic SVG objects and 'repairs the largest mismatch regions' of the persistent semantic SVG, which remains 'the editable authority' (authority 8, mutation 7, artifact 8). Correction is explicitly bounded, so mutation is restricted rather than open-ended. Deliverable is Illustrator-ready SVG ('Illustrator-ready' means no major object needs rebuilding), a complete exportable result.

This is a bridge: 'Modeling operations work on the staged copy' and 'atomically replaces the durable .c4d target', so AI agents can create and mutate native documents, but the product itself supplies no design authorship (authority 3, mutation 4 per bridge rule). It renders previews and 'can export C4D, OBJ, FBX, glTF, STL, Alembic or Collada', a real exportable delivery; the artifact is the host-owned native document.

Devin is an autonomous agent that 'edits and runs the repository' and 'creates a branch and PR as the reviewable implementation result', with Computer Use validation and recording attachments; AI authors and persistently mutates Git-backed artifacts (authority 9, mutation 9, artifact 8). Human reviews the PR and recording, an approval-only loop. Delivery reaches reviewable/deployable PR state, though the video is positioned as a 'quick sanity check' rather than full acceptance evidence.

AI generates candidates from prompts/media and the chosen direction becomes 'a user-owned/editable Canva resource'; MCP exposes 'start-editing-transaction / perform-editing-operations / commit-editing-transaction' so AI directly mutates the native layered design (authority 9, mutation 9, artifact 9). Human selects candidates and reviews; delivery spans 'export, publish, print or platform handoff'. Still a candidate-promotion and brand-review surface, so not a perfect 10.

SlideX 'turns a sentence or pasted outline into a deck using built-in layout patterns', so AI creates the draft (authority 7). PPTX/HD PDF export and fullscreen presentation close the loop to delivery.

The website-builder contract lets a user 'describe a site... inspect the live result select elements for visual edits continue through chat and publish', so AI generates and iterates a managed app project with 'full-project snapshots covering code files and database' (authority 8, mutation 7, artifact 8). The skill 'reviews and rewrites labels, actions, errors and flows against measurable standards', so AI produces proposed interface copy (authority 6), but 'the product or Figma document still owns durable copy' — the skill owns audit and proposed language only, with no evidence it writes back (mutation 3, artifact 4). Human must apply the proposals, and delivery covers review/audit fragments rather than a shipped design.

Team approval, measurements and notes add heavy human involvement (human_loop 5), and delivery is handoff to manufacturing partners via collection links/print-ready PDFs.

Sandpack preview supports review (human_loop 6) and promotion into a shared registry delivers (delivery 7).

No evidence of AI mutating existing artifacts (mutation 4); persistent Spaces are claimed but the artifact model is unknown (artifact 5). The workspace loop with async jobs is documented (human_loop 5) and generated Office previews/deliverables are the output (delivery 6).

DCC-MCP OpenSCAD is a deterministic adapter: 'Its Design loop begins with an existing .scad authority and safely explores or materializes parameter choices' without writing arbitrary source, so it does not author design (authority 3, mutation 3). Parameterized renders and exports carry SHA-256 provenance linking to source and parameters (artifact 5), the pipeline runs on agent invocation (human_loop 5), and it exports STL/3MF/DXF/SVG/PDF deliverable formats (delivery 6).

Gemini 'returns a single self-contained HTML file' and its improvement route returns a complete replacement, so AI authors the site; the same document is re-authored only via whole-document regeneration rather than patch-level mutation, and no persistence exists (mutation 4, artifact 3 per 'no database, project reload path or version graph'). Authoring power is real (authority 8), one client state drives generation and re-improvement (human_loop 6), and copy/download/new-tab preview deliver the HTML (delivery 6).

Ghosted embeds an agent workflow as a `.canvas` file, where the human designs the node graph and the Pi agent executes the compiled run, so AI executes rather than authors the design (authority 5). The canvas serializes/reloads on file changes with undo and dirty state, and runs compile the upstream subgraph (mutation 6). A durable JSON Canvas 1.0 file beside workspace sources is a strong artifact (artifact 8). Runs are triggered and reviewed in the IDE (human_loop 6) and deliver executed agent outcomes and run logs (delivery 6).

Local Llama models decide component selection and composition while deterministic code assembles the site from a foundation library, so AI authors the plan and visual system within constraints (authority 7). Visual studio controls can change tokens and current files on the filesystem, giving direct edits (mutation 6). Project directories and generated site files persist (artifact 7), preview/update/upload routes support the workflow (human_loop 6), and ZIP delivery of the same workspace closes the loop (delivery 7).

The plugin manages workflow/model/image/batch artifacts around the existing ComfyUI canvas, with local models that summarize, tag, translate and improve prompts but 'not silently rewriting every graph', so AI assists rather than authors the visual design (authority 4, mutation 4). Stored workflow JSON and PNG metadata provenance are durable structured artifacts (artifact 6). Users operate the ComfyUI canvas with tool assistance (human_loop 5), and it augments the existing canvas rather than delivering its own product (delivery 5).

Gamma turns topic/text/file/URL into a structured card graph and lets Agent rewrite content, generate cards and bulk-edit with review before 'Accept all', so AI authors and directly mutates the persistent card artifact (authority 9, mutation 9, artifact 9). Human review, hidden cards and version restore remain in the loop but are reviews/steers (human_loop 8). Delivery spans presentation, published site/document and PowerPoint/PDF/image export from one card model (delivery 9); closed-source internals keep it below the fully-AI-native tier.

AI reduces an app brief to a product schema (appName, entities, roles, features) that drives a form mockup, so AI authors the app definition (authority 7). Correction is narrow — a second model call may return only four style keys that the server sanitizes, and style overrides stay client-session state (mutation 5). The MongoDB product schema persists while visual overrides do not (artifact 6); the user supplies briefs and visual changes (human_loop 6), but output is a structured mockup rather than a shipped app (delivery 5).

This is a visual no-code editor where humans design agent pipelines from eight node types; AI agents run inside the executed graph rather than authoring the design (authority 4). The canvas graph is directly editable and recompiled to LangGraph (mutation 6), Convex persists workflows and executions durably (artifact 7), approval nodes expose human pauses (human_loop 6), and the compiler executes the saved design to real runs (delivery 7).

The service is a Cloudflare diagram storage/rendering layer whose MCP API lets external agents create/update/delete persistent diagrams, so the product provides the tool surface rather than the AI that authors diagrams (authority 4). `update_diagram` mutates durable records directly (mutation 6), persistent Mermaid source records are durable artifacts (artifact 7), shared web editor and agent hit the same backend (human_loop 5), and nine diagram families render/export derived forms (delivery 6).

SimCorrect autonomously detects mismatches, 'identifies a responsible geometric or dynamic parameter, rebuilds the model and accepts the change only after the task succeeds', which is automated engineering correction rather than intent-driven AI authorship (authority 5). It writes MJCF changes and emits structured JSON patches against the CAID contract that OpenCAD applies to the model — direct, validated mutation (mutation 8). The corrected MuJoCo model and versioned CAID artifact persist (artifact 7); validation is programmatic with little human input (human_loop 6), and the deliverable is a corrected simulation model rather than a shipped product (delivery 6).

ALICE-SDF has an LLM-facing text-to-3D server where 'the model composes mathematical geometry' and the server translates requests into scene operations, so AI authors the SDF program (authority 8). Agent loops iterate through visual feedback against the same field (mutation 7). Compiled instructions and constraints remain the geometry authority across render/mesh/bindings (artifact 7), the loop runs from text intent with visual feedback (human_loop 7), and mesh export plus DCC/game/Web/mobile/XR bindings deliver (delivery 7).

TypeUI's decisive artifact is the editable, publishable design-system package (SKILL.md, brand.md, colors.md) that governs AI coding agents generating UI, so the human authors the system while agents apply it (authority 5). Draft/publish cycles, numbered versions, restore and a selected current package give real mutation of the governed artifact (mutation 6). The versioned markdown package is a strong durable artifact (artifact 8); users review/edit markdown and name the direction in the agent loop (human_loop 6), and delivery is indirect — the agent's generated UI lives in the user's repository, which TypeUI does not own (delivery 6).

Drawtir attaches AI at generation points — storyboard/wall modals generate scenes and Supabase functions generate merch designs or import Figma structure — and humans continue with layout/keyframe tools, so AI generates material on a human-led canvas (authority 7). Generated elements land on the editable canvas and timeline for direct correction (mutation 6); the canvas, timeline and Supabase-hosted state persist (artifact 7, though no portable file/version contract is documented). The movie/static renderer exports time-based or static deliverables (delivery 7), with human selection after generation (human_loop 6).

a0 grounds component generation in scraped documentation that 'enters the model context before React is produced', so AI authors React components from the API/library source (authority 8). Chat coordinates code, preview and documentation state for iteration (mutation 6). Public source does not establish a durable multi-project version graph, so artifact 5; the user drives the generation conversation (human_loop 6) and sandboxed preview projects the generated runnable component (delivery 6).

The workbench lets an agent operate at the intent layer — synthesize a filter, place a transmission zero — while real simulator runs supply evidence, so AI proposes and optimizes circuit designs (authority 7). Durable job artifacts and the design–simulate–revise chain support iteration on circuits through the IR (mutation 6); circuit IR, job artifacts and Touchstone interchange persist (artifact 7). Independent-simulator verification reduces human intervention (human_loop 7), though delivery stops at the antenna and schematic-to-layout boundary rather than full physical closure (delivery 6).

DCC-MCP Core 'is not an AI agent' and 'does not define a universal scene model'; it is a control plane routing operations to separately owned DCC sessions and Skills, so design authority stays outside it (authority 2). It owns workflow checkpoints, artifacts and audit but cannot mutate creative truth (mutation 4). Control-plane state, artifacts and audit records are durable (artifact 5), agent-invoked operation via a bounded contract automates much of the flow (human_loop 5), and it makes DCC sessions discoverable/operable — infrastructure delivery (delivery 5).

Conductor dispatches CLI agents that turn goals into files, diagrams and executable work; 'agents change the project-management state used by the UI' and canvas tools apply atomic operations to Obsidian Canvas files. Mutation is strong ('canvas_write' batched operations applied atomically, format-specific round-trip code writes back to Markdown/Mermaid/Excalidraw). Artifact is durable and structured (SQLite goals/evidence state plus project files). Human supervision flags, dependency blocking and evidence judging mean the human still steers and approves, so human_loop is mid-range; delivery covers goal achievement with verified evidence gates rather than a deployed product.

Claude Code drives Figma and Webflow MCP so the agent 'creates Webflow variables, fonts, pages, assets and sections before comparing each rendered section with Figma and correcting discrepancies' — AI authors and corrects the delivery artifact. Webflow is called 'the mutable delivery authority', a durable, user-editable artifact. Human picks the class convention and approves publication, while the agent owns visual QA, responsive rules, accessibility and SEO; delivery ends at a published Webflow site. Slight deduction because publication is a separately approved transition.

The framework is governance infrastructure: AI proposes phase artifacts but 'policy.py enforces governance rather than allowing model output to advance state by assertion'. Proposals only pass schema+policy validation into a persisted PostgreSQL session/audit, so it coordinates and verifies rather than authoring design. Mutation is limited to revision-or-refusal cycling through validation; artifact is the persisted session/audit record. No evidence of end-to-end delivery beyond the session runtime; appropriate low authority/mutation for a contract/verifier layer.

A multi-DCC agent layer where the shared bridge core and MCP server standardize agent transport while 'each DCC's native scene or node graph remains authoritative'. Artists can discover, generate, version, publish and share tools/skills from an in-editor conversation surface, so AI can generate and agents can execute against DCC scenes. Native scene mutation is possible but the product is a bridge, not an author; in-editor sessions persist and resume (artifact), and tool lifecycle gives partial delivery. No strong evidence of AI authoring finished design artifacts.

The saved .pen JSON document is the native design program and agents mutate it directly through MCP or the CLI 'execute' operation with editId/edits patching — a compositional, direct mutation surface over a durable structured graph (components, refs, variables, Script nodes, imports). AI generates framework code and the product documents design-to-code/code-to-design agent loops. Human still must save explicitly, verify visually and commit Git revisions (no autosave, limited undo), so human_loop is mid; delivery is strong via export_html, media export and agent-authored application code, though round-trip semantics are unproven.

A verification workspace, not an authoring loop: canonical authority is the React Native source and 'Chromatic... does not give Chromatic authority to edit the component'. Coding agents consume dual-purpose example files as usage contracts, but the studio only detects rendered drift against locked baselines. Mutation is explicitly absent (1); the durable outputs are stories, baselines and source (artifact 4); CI compares deterministic web renders, giving a narrow verification delivery rather than a shipped design.

Fudge captures live sites, compares them with precedents and 'turn[s] that analysis into concrete implementation guidance' — ordered fixes, tokens, CSS variables, Tailwind themes, structured JSON or DESIGN.md, so AI produces design decisions and durable tokens/guidance artifacts. It 'does not directly become the application's source authority' — a separate coding agent applies accepted guidance, so mutation of the target is indirect (3) and the loop still needs human search/selection and agent application. Delivery is guidance/evidence artifacts rather than the shipped app.

A coding agent creates the full playable 2D game project (HTML+JS+JSON+assets) from a brief, and the visual scene editor mutates the same SceneModel via SceneOps, so AI authors the game and both paths converge on the persistent project. Conventions constrain the agent so project layout stays editable and reopenable; framework-free output deploys as a static site. Human corrects positions/scale through the editor after generation, giving partial hands-on loop; Godot/Unity remain roadmap and are not counted.

FIGS is a pre-alpha schema laboratory: users model a governed knowledge schema from source material, inspect it as a graph, and test it via retrieval and Cypher queries. Provenance is tracked before entities become graph material, but AI (OpenAI AI SDK) assists retrieval rather than authoring the schema; users alter schema structure. No evidence AI mutates or persists design, MCP is only a future direction, so delivery is confined to in-app graph exploration; no evidence for end-to-end design delivery.

The AI-authored Python module becomes a first-class ComfyUI workflow node inside the native graph, and the chatbot/OpenAI-facing node 'generate or revise module code' with dirty-state tracking — direct, inspectable creation and correction of the node within the canvas. The workflow JSON is the operational artifact and export materializes standalone Python. Human still wires, edits and runs the graph, and the product 'spans native graph authoring and code materialization rather than promising an autonomous end-to-end design service', so it is high AI-enhanced rather than AI-first.

Etlaq's agent workspace turns an Arabic/English brief into a provider-managed project spanning pages, logic, database, authentication and design, then supports conversational revision and one-click hosted publication with domain, SSL, CDN and analytics. AI authors the draft and revises it; the managed application project is the durable artifact and chat is the control surface. Mutation/version semantics (named versions, rollback, migrations) are undisclosed, so mutation and artifact are capped at 7; delivery is full (published product journey) as claimed by the first-party surface.

RAGFlow's decisive design object is the persisted agent DSL that the canvas edits, backend services version and the Python canvas runtime interprets — a durable, structured artifact with explicit replica and user-canvas-version services. The canvas is a typed DSL editor where users compose workflow logic and AI contributes retrieval/agent execution within nodes, so authority over the workflow design is mostly human with AI as a component. Execution follows the authored topology, tying the running agent to the graph; no evidence the system generates whole designs from intent.

Claude is asked for structured intent then a typed blueprint grounded in retrieved component names before generating React/TypeScript, and the six-stage pipeline exposes each transformation — AI genuinely generates the frontend from intent. However 'there is no durable project store', outputs are in-memory and validation is partly simulated with fixed pass messages, so mutation of a persistent artifact is absent and artifact is weak (3). The live preview and downloadable code give a partial delivery; the loop is a one-shot generation rather than iteration.

A visual workflow canvas for composing agents from models, tools, knowledge, logic and guardrails, with drag-and-drop construction, preview runs, inline evaluation and 'full versioning'. Users arrange workflow logic and promote versions to publish — the design object is the executable agent configuration, so AI does not generate the design itself; authority is user-driven. Architecture-level evidence only (closed internal schema/runtime), so mutation and artifact get moderate scores from the described version/publish loop; delivery is publishing agents for the platform.

Dosmos is a runtime-to-source feedback bridge: clicking an element reduces the selection to a Markdown annotation typed into an external CLI PTY, and 'the default prompt contains no source file, line, selector or page URL' — the product routes to a separately installed agent rather than authoring. Project source and Git remain the durable authority while Dosmos' own state (sessions, queues, screenshots, presets) is volatile or short-lived. The Edit code resolver opens realpathed project files for the built-in editor, and delivery depends on the external agent's diffs and the project's own release path; the page-message bridge admits forged annotations.

The backend turns prompts into structured cloud components/relationships for AWS/Azure/GCP materialized as editable React Flow nodes, and 'the first model response is not the final artifact' — dragging/changing the graph remains possible and suggestions propose improvements. FastAPI/SQLAlchemy/PostgreSQL persist durable user diagrams. AI analysis suggestions 'remain hypotheses that the user must assess', so the loop is human-led; exported diagrams are the delivery and 'persistence is not deployment', capping delivery at 5.

graph.json is the explicit design authority edited visually and materialized into an executable main.py, so regeneration starts from the graph and both the AI Editor and the Node Editor 'write the same system'. AI generates nodes, HTML, CSS and logic into the graph-to-code pipeline, and users can switch back to direct node editing. SQLite stores projects and transcripts, and transcripts reconstruct a damaged canvas — a durable, recoverable artifact. Generated Python remains a projection to be reviewed before deployment, capping delivery.

Browser audio is uploaded and sent as voice_prompt to a Relevance AI studio endpoint whose output.answer is treated as HTML — the AI genuinely generates the whole page from a voice brief. But the HTML is installed via dangerouslySetInnerHTML and replaces the recording interface, with 'no code editor, correction request, export or project persistence' in public source, so mutation of a persistent artifact is absent (1) and the artifact is disposable display output (2). Historical (repository ends 2024) and the studio hides model behavior; delivery stops at a rendered page.

Users prompt a printable part and the browser editor exposes an editable scene tree with native objects, sketch/extrude/revolve/fillet/mirror tools, so AI generates the CAD part and object-level tools refine it directly. Artifact is editable native objects plus exported STL with print-readiness checks, but 'persistence versions boolean kernel model-generation implementation' are not disclosed, capping artifact; delivery produces STL with manufacturability evidence but 'does not prove a physical print will succeed'.

A React Flow canvas autosaved to Supabase with undo snapshots, model-generated graph insertion and an agent run route that invokes OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini and writes the final response into the output node — AI can generate graph content and results flow through the persisted canvas. 'Most executors choose find(edge => edge.source === currentNode.id), so only the first outgoing edge controls continuation' and placeholders mix with real calls, limiting the run route's fidelity. Authority is split between human canvas authorship and AI model nodes; no deployment evidence.

A planning model decomposes campaign intent and an execution agent streams state changes into a shared Fabric.js JSON graph that the human can edit directly, with human edits 'become context for the next agent action' — real-time co-editing of one authority and intervention is part of the control model. Artifact is the JSON object graph but persistence, undo, versioning and export are not evidenced, capping artifact; delivery stops at the canvas output with no collaboration/export contract. The account is architecture-level from a live product blog.

A local browser notebook where users compose prompt/AI/Markdown/annotation nodes and compute.ts runs typed work with reactive dirty-parent resolution — the AI executes nodes rather than authoring the design, so authority is low. Workflows persist as named graphs in localStorage with JSON import (artifact 5) but 'no durable run log, collaboration, hosted deployment, or source-generation boundary' — delivery is the local browser graph itself, and clearing site storage removes it.

Deterministic Playwright extraction of live sites into normalized tokens and findings, timestamped snapshots, pinned baselines and drift scores, exposed to agents via MCP — a design-system evidence and verification tool rather than a design author. It saves durable versioned evidence (artifact 6: JSON, DTCG tokens, DESIGN.md, audit reports) but never edits the design itself; the CI drift-gate example shows delivery as verification in the release pipeline. Low authority/mutation are correct for this verification/bridge shape.

OpenAI vision receives an uploaded image and must return one TSX component, exposed as both MCP tools and REST endpoints with code-refinement functions — AI generates and can refine the code. Monaco edits mutate the same in-memory TSX state and copy/.tsx download deliver the current source, but 'there is no project store or version graph', capping artifact; the PreviewPane iframe exists in source but is never mounted in the product route, so the visual feedback loop is not shipped. No persistent mutation target.

A build agent turns a prompt, design reference or Figma input into a code-backed web/mobile project, and Visual Edit 'saving writes those pending edits to source' — direct manipulation AI changes and manual Code View edits are views over one continuing project the user owns and can export. Delivery covers hosted or app-store publication and GitHub/ZIP export. Hosted project format, patch protocol and model orchestration are closed, capping artifact; Figma screen updates are not yet fully supported, and the loop still needs user visual checks.

The .excalidraw file in the user's repository is the shared state: the Claude skill drafts a Mermaid recipe, the browser resolves it into an Excalidraw scene and saves it back to the same path, and later agent turns read a compact scene summary and 'perform minimal edits' — direct bidirectional mutation of a durable, Git-versionable, portable file. Human manual placement is sacred unless movement was requested, so the loop is deliberately hands-on for placement. The model/conversation stays in Claude Code while the local server is a filesystem/editor bridge; delivery is the resolved portable .excalidraw documents.

The skill reconstructs a 2D photonics schematic as a physically auditable Blender optical table with mesh, ray, BVH and load-path checks whose results are PASS/BLOCKED/UNVERIFIED — AI produces the 3D artifact and the workflow reopens the scene to run checks, so artifact is rich and durable (3D model plus manifests, hashes, annotated renders). Reconstruction is capped at auditing, 'not mechanical, spectral or laser-safety certification'; published forward tests include failures and replay drift, so authority/mutation/delivery are moderate.

Prompts, media, generation settings and outputs stay connected as an editable Vue Flow graph with visible media lineage, and model output 'enters a user-controlled node rather than replacing the project' — AI generates images/videos while the user keeps manual rewiring and parameter changes available, so generation and correction happen within a persistent canvas. Projects, settings, undo and redo are browser-local (recovery is deliberately local), giving a durable local artifact; delivery is exported media and locally saved graphs with no server-side collaboration or history.

A runtime overlay bridge: a reviewer clicks an element, leaves a note or captures a region, and the agent receives structured context via clipboard or MCP 'before resolving the annotation' — the designed app remains canonical and Instruckt only carries runtime visual intent into the repair loop. It persists JSON annotations and PNG screenshots (artifact 4) and its MCP tools enumerate and resolve pending findings; no evidence Instruckt authors or mutates design itself, so authority 2, mutation 3.

A plugin/sidecar/Skill platform giving agents MCP access to Unreal actors, assets, Blueprints, materials, cinematics, Niagara and packaging, composing with Epic's own MCP Toolsets on 5.8+. It is infrastructure that lets AI agents act inside Unreal rather than authoring design itself (authority 3); skills declare mutability/destructiveness/idempotency and the build-package skill 'advances a saved project toward delivery', so agents can mutate and partially drive the Unreal project to delivery. Unreal project files remain the durable authority; the platform's own persistence is the skill/capability catalog.

Infrastructure/bridge: 'Python/CLI foundation for agents to parse, analyze and mutate KiCad schematics' — the tool does not author designs itself (authority 2). It does enable 'programmatic repair' and 'apply geometric operations and save a new native file', so mutation of persistent .kicad_sch/.kicad_pcb is genuine (mutation 4). Artifacts are native editable KiCad files plus renders/fabrication exports (4), but an external agent + human must drive the whole loop (human_loop 3) and the package is a component/library rather than a self-contained shipped result despite exporting fabrication packages (delivery 3).

AI planner+generator produce React source under a known-component schema and 'retries invalid source instead of silently accepting arbitrary output' (authority 8). VersionStore lets generated revisions and direct editor changes be 'selected or rolled back' in-session, so AI iterates on existing source (mutation 7). Artifact is editable React source but persistence is in-memory only — 'do not survive a restart' (artifact 6). Pipeline with validation runs largely automatically but human edits/reviews (human_loop 6); preview is 'a simplified projector... not a general React runtime', so delivery to working result is partial (delivery 6).

A coding agent 'can propose pipeline structure' into the same .pipe file and visual graph the user edits — AI co-authors the pipeline (authority 7, mutation 7). The '.pipe JSON' is a version-controllable, portable artifact executed by one C++ engine locally/on-prem/cloud (artifact 8); Python/TS SDKs invoke the same format. Human reviews and edits proposed changes (human_loop 6). Deployment is 'a target choice over that artifact' with real local/hosted execution, giving a working deliverable (delivery 7).

Gemini-backed agent features 'can propose HDL and diagram changes' entering a real syntax/simulation environment (authority 6, mutation 6); Verilog source is the durable editable authority with schematic projection (artifact 8). Compile/sim gives feedback but agents are semi-automated and the human drives design (human_loop 5). Delivery stops at browser simulation — 'falling short of synthesis, timing closure, or silicon correctness' (delivery 5).

Gemini 'converts a brief into three conventional web files' directly, so AI creates the complete artifact (authority 7). But 'Delivery is implemented; correction is not' — preview/revision remain roadmap items, so no iteration on existing output (mutation 2). The HTML/CSS/JS files are the durable authority after generation but with no versioning (artifact 5). One-shot pipeline with manual download, no runtime correction (human_loop 4); 'website.zip' and a download button deliver the site files (delivery 6).

Human authors the workflow topology; AI task nodes only execute individual tasks via OpenAI (authority 4). The graph serializes into Appwrite documents and runs create durable per-node evidence (artifact 6, mutation 3 — AI nodes do not edit the workflow artifact itself). Runs are inspectable but 'no server worker, scheduler, or shared edit protocol' and execution depends on a live browser session (human_loop 4, delivery 4).

The AI Architect 'can reason about and mutate that topology' with explicit apply-canvas-mutations.ts tooling applied as data to the persistent typed node/edge canvas — direct mutation of the shared artifact (authority 7, mutation 8). Canvas autosave, Liveblocks collaboration and collaborative undo make a durable editable graph (artifact 8). Human drag/drop, labels and review remain in the loop (human_loop 6); a generated spec becomes a versionable preview/download delivery artifact (delivery 7).

Lovable-style builder where 'tool writes, not prose, mutate the project' — Spring AI tools perform explicit file reads/writes on the server-owned project file set, so AI authoring and iteration are direct (authority 8, mutation 8). The project file set in object storage is persistent and streamed to the frontend (artifact 7); the CodeMirror pane is read-only so normal mutation flows through agent tools rather than human typing (human_loop 6). Delivery is a temporary Kubernetes preview ('temporary runtime evidence, not a durable release record') plus ZIP download (delivery 6).

The typed graph is human-authored on the canvas; AI appears only as node executors (OpenAI/Anthropic/Ollama calls), not as the design author (authority 3, mutation 3 — AI does not edit the graph). Persistence is unusually strong: immutable WorkflowVersion snapshots and PostgreSQL per-node execution records (artifact 8). Human builds and runs workflows with human-approval nodes (human_loop 4); delivery is real via web chat, Telegram, email, schedules and signed webhooks over the same versioned artifact (delivery 7).

Import recovers product behavior from live code and 'a person can... ask an agent to change the flow and see the canvas update', with a real pull request carrying implementation — AI co-edits flows grounded in source (authority 5, mutation 5). The canvas is a structured projection over real components/routes with clickable shared flows and snapshot versions (artifact 7). Snapshot of the canvas 'is not necessarily a branch snapshot' and comments need human/agent application (human_loop 5); issue documentation or PR carries decisions outward (delivery 6). Closed parser/PR internals limit evidence.

A Pydantic agent converts text/image intent into a typed family specification and a cloud AppBundle 'materializes and flex-tests the Revit family' — AI creates the native .rfa artifact (authority 7). No iteration/repair loop is evidenced — one generation job (mutation 3). The .rfa is the durable native artifact with request logs/previews as supporting evidence (artifact 6). Requires Autodesk credentials, AppBundle registration and a Revit runtime, so setup and review are human (human_loop 5); FlexTester-validated .rfa delivery is a real export (delivery 6).

Natural-language requests become proposed entity-level operations on the active AutoCAD DWG; the AI proposes and the human approves — AI drafts, human owns the design (authority 4). 'An accepted mutation lands in the live host drawing' with snapshot and one-click rollback, so AI directly mutates the persistent artifact under a gate (mutation 5). DWG stays the authoritative artifact with cross-session project memory (artifact 5). 'The user approves or rejects it' before every execution (human_loop 4); scope is repetitive drafting ops inside the host, not a full design-to-ship loop (delivery 4).

This is an adapter/bridge: 'the AEP project remains the durable authority; DCC-MCP supplies discovery, validated calls and delivery jobs around it' — the creative authorship belongs to the external agent (authority 3). Mutation is concrete and typed: layer tools cover text, transforms, masks, effects, ordering and keyframes and create_motion_intro.py shows real authoring (mutation 5). The persistent AEP artifact is external and the adapter adds session-scoped references over it (artifact 5). Agent must re-inspect after host restarts and the human/agent drives every call (human_loop 4); render-queue control delivers exports but remains a bridge fragment (delivery 4).

Staged agent interface around native KiCad: the agent drives design while the product gates phases — read-only review, 'controlled build, human-gated release' (authority 3). Write/manufacturing modes do mutate .kicad_sch/.kicad_pcb via PCB-design skills, with ERC/DRC as gates (mutation 5). Native KiCad files remain authoritative and exports invoke KiCad engines (artifact 5). Explicit elevation and permissioned progression keep humans in the approval loop (human_loop 4); fabrication output/export reaches a manufacturing handoff (delivery 5).

Groq 'constrains a model to return HTML, CSS, and JavaScript', so AI creates the complete source from a prompt (authority 7). There is 'no server project model, version branching, or direct editor' — one-shot output only (mutation 2). Persistence is localStorage chat history feeding iframe.srcdoc (artifact 3). Minimal prompt→preview loop with no editing surface (human_loop 3); results are executable source shown in a sandboxed iframe but not a deployable project (delivery 4).

Figma plugin that 'streams frames, Auto Layout, text, icons and images directly into the native canvas' from a prompt reference — AI authors native Figma content (authority 7). 'Selected-node patching' makes in-place changes to existing elements, a stronger intent boundary than regenerating a screen (mutation 7). Output lives as native Figma graph nodes bound to variables/styles with style memory (artifact 8). User selects and steers per request while AI generates/patches in the real canvas (human_loop 6); React/Tailwind export is one-way delivery with no verified round trip (delivery 6). Closed plugin source limits verification of variant/combo validation.

AI Layout 'produces multiple furniture layouts' from room constraints and AI rendering/style transfer project the design — AI creates design candidates (authority 7). 'The chosen option returns to the ordinary 3D design environment for manual customization', so mutation of the spatial graph is largely human while AI outputs feed it (mutation 6). The cloud design project holds room/wall/opening/furniture/material state as native authority (artifact 8). Human selects and customizes between AI steps (human_loop 6); delivery spans CAD drawings, cut lists, BOMs, quotations and JEGA manufacturing data — a design-to-manufacture lineage (delivery 8). Internal solver/schema closed.

The Rosie chat agent 'changes the game's code' from prompt/image/template and corrections are 'validated by playing the current state' — AI authors and iterates the executable project (authority 8, mutation 8). The saved Rosebud project containing code and assets is the durable authority with publish and remix semantics (artifact 8). Chat correction + real-time preview keeps the user steering but the AI does the coding (human_loop 7); a published playable URL is real runtime delivery with remix spawning new projects (delivery 8). Platform implementation closed; schema/sandbox/merge undisclosed.

Two authorities: the Figma visual object and the JMPY.me managed link/QR record. MCP integrations 'create and update links or QR codes and query analytics', so agents manage the delivery record, not the canvas design (authority 4). Managed records are mutable but no canvas refresh/rollback identity is proven (mutation 4). Figma nodes plus managed records/analytics form dual persistent artifacts (artifact 5). User inserts objects and agents update records with human review (human_loop 5); the product delivers operational links/QRs with analytics (delivery 5). Public MCP repo is packaging only, 'no server implementation' — penalized evidence.
