The React Flow graph preserves generative composition across 25+ providers, but humans connect the nodes; AI provides generation, not authorship of the composition, so authority is moderate. Mutation is limited because changes are made by rewiring/rerunning nodes rather than AI editing the canvas. Artifact is persistent local browser state; delivery ceiling is 'an executable local playground' with no multi-user or server-side semantics.

The explicit protobuf operation model makes the MCP server 'another synchronized client': an agent 'can submit the same operation family and subscribe to live document updates', i.e. direct mutation of the persistent document. Artifact is strong (invariant-checking core, snapshot + oplog persistence). Human_loop and delivery are capped by the 'milestone-driven vertical slice' status with only SVG/PNG exports.

Plain-language instructions invoke edits that land on a real timeline with keyframes and manual control, so agents perform production edits that remain inspectable. Artifact is a persistent project timeline referencing managed or S3 media. Human_loop drops because users retain manual timeline control; delivery includes local render/share plus an editable pro-tool timeline handoff, though no public contract shows changes synchronizing back.

This is a bridge/infrastructure project: the server embeds in TouchDesigner so an agent can 'read and write parameters, load or save .toe/.tox state', so AI authorship of design is not the product itself (authority low per rule 6). Mutation is real — direct writes to persistent host state with capture_viewport as post-mutation evidence. Artifact/delivery are capped because the durable artifact and renderer belong to the host DCC; the adapter is a component, not a closed design loop.

The builder reconstructs flat slide images into layered PowerPoint by combining visual-layer manifest with an editable text-layer model, so AI performs the conversion/reconstruction. Mutation is moderate — regeneration and text-layer edits rather than deep iteration on rendered output. Artifact is durable (manifest.json, text-layer.json, PPTX with backend record); processing is mostly automatic after input; delivery is a real PowerPoint file with optional runtime previews.

MCP capabilities become editor commands: the agent invokes a capability that 'mutates site state/source' inside the same GrapesJS editor a human uses, so AI and human co-edit one authoritative local website project. Artifact is the editable web source/state plus clean static HTML/CSS output. Human_loop remains hands-on (refine by hand, publish); delivery is publishable static sites, though alpha/transition lifecycle is acknowledged.

Natural language is compiled by the model into workflow JSON validated by Zod, so AI authors the automation graph. Mutation is moderate because versions are immutable and revision means a new compiled version ('every run points to the exact version it executed'). Artifact is strong (SQLite immutable versions, React Flow projection, step traces). Delivery is capped: action nodes only simulate and no production deployment is established.

The inherited Studio runtime gives agents tools and workspace context over MBSE objects, so AI assists within a constraint domain rather than a general chat IDE. Mutation is evidenced by agents editing engineering objects behind coverage/traceability/FMEA views. Artifact is strong: 'structured source and its cross-links' with DSL and diagram projections. Execution quality and certification remain project-specific validation claims, capping delivery.

A generator service turns prompts into typed diagram data that is independent of any provider, so AI authors the specification. Mutation is limited: 'the current evidence does not establish bidirectional synchronization from draw.io back into the stored specification', so downstream manual edits do not flow back. Artifact is durable (DB records, MinIO storage, Celery-separated generation); delivery is Mermaid/draw.io renderers through web and Tauri desktop shells.

Three Gemini calls create a plan, component source and explanation, so AI authors the component. Mutation is partial: the page treats 'complete source strings as editable versions' but 'no persistence layer outlives the page session'. Artifact is therefore in-memory versioned source rather than durable state. Delivery is capped at a React Live preview with export/deploy outside the product.

An ordinary user describes an app and the open-agent-kernel drives sessions, workspace snapshots and applied changes with 'source-level receipts' (file diff viewer, file editor), so AI authors the app in a persistent workspace. Human_loop is high: user reviews diffs, edits files, opens live preview and deploys. Delivery is closed: web and mini-program deployment to CloudBase is implemented with separate completion events.

This is a verification/benchmark product: the runner executes generated Blender programs and records scores rather than authoring a design work, so authority is low per rule 6. Mutation is minimal — candidate scripts are evaluated one-shot, not iterated against a persistent artifact. Artifact is generated Blender Python/renders as evaluation candidates plus score records; human_loop is strong via automated scoring and LLM judges; delivery is the benchmark harness and agent adapters, not a design product.

The AI assistant derives project name/package/screen prompts and 'subsequent tool calls update application state screens data types resources', i.e. direct mutation of a structured project graph. Artifact is the durable YAML 'Project' serialized by ProjectRepository, with code generation as a materialization via CodeGenerator. Users may rename/rewrite prompts and drag-and-drop edit before generation, keeping human_loop hands-on; delivery covers export and generated Compose code.

The skill defines reconstruction as the design task: the agent measures the reference, records layout fingerprint and generates native mxCell geometry; the loop diagram shows 'Visible mismatch → A' iterating the editable geometry. Artifact is the uncompressed editable .drawio XML with PNG evidence and SVG assets; editability is an explicit invariant. Human_loop is strong because the agent executes the protocol with render-and-compare feedback; delivery is a complete package (.drawio + PNG + SVG + provenance note).

The canvas records heterogeneous creative nodes and preserves provenance via trinity-store.json and provider job records, so AI generates media inside a spatially arranged graph. Mutation is limited: 'revision normally means changing an upstream prompt mapping or node and running again' with no semantic direct editing of raster/video output. human_loop is under construction ('an approval boundary under construction rather than a general autonomous creative executor'); delivery retains generated assets and the graph that produced them.

CraftEditor's 'iterative fixer revises the SVG' with a VLM judge scoring reconstruction, so AI directly mutates the durable editable-SVG artifact until it matches the input. Artifact is the geometry-bearing SVG schema ('a visually similar PNG does not preserve selectable text, shapes or coordinates'). Human_loop benefits from automated judging; delivery is a complete raster-to-editable-SVG pipeline, with external endpoints as runtime dependencies noted.

Multi-agent generation builds the site and pipeline_followup 'turns feedback into a structured change request and asks another agent to revise the full existing code', i.e. AI authorship with direct mutation of the persistent file set. Artifact is the parsed website files exposed for preview and code inspection. Delivery is closed: deploy.js creates a repo, pushes files and enables GitHub Pages, so publication is implemented rather than claimed (with noted credential-hardening caveats).

An external agent builds a screen in Figma from real design-system components; the plugin 'creates native nodes and returns binding feedback', so AI authors and mutates the live Figma graph. Artifact is the native Figma document (components, instances, variables, styles, auto-layout) plus cached local policy — the strongest durable artifact in this batch. Corrections become later rules and gap reports improve future mutation; delivery depends on the installed Figma host and model client.

The MCP server 'list, read and launch workflows' and automate visible controls, so an agent edits or invokes 'the same files a human sees rendered' — direct mutation of authoritative TSX/Python source via esbuild compilation. Artifact is the workflow folder as source-authority live projection. Human_loop is moderate because humans author the workflows and install is a code-trust decision; delivery covers running local interactive apps and exchange publishing, not collaborative hosted versions.

Historical but complete prompt-to-page loop: request.php sends the prompt to GPT-4 and the generated page is stored under the application. AI authorship is high for its era. Mutation is moderate — the CodeMirror source surface allows manual editing and refresh, but no AI-driven regeneration of stored pages is evidenced. Artifact is a durable stored page file shown simultaneously as code and iframe; delivery is a downloadable page rather than deployment.

Gemini generates raw single-root JSX previewed in a sandboxed iframe, so AI authors the component draft. Mutation is weak: generation is transient ('not durable until the user presses Save') and there is no evidence of iterative editing of the generated component. Artifact is the Firebase gallery of saved component records that render their own previews; delivery is a recoverable component collection rather than a deployed app.

Seven agents and skills route analysis/construction/optimization across Blender, Unity, Omniverse and VRoid, so AI performs design work, but the dossier is architecture-level with only team/skill contracts visible. Host-native files retain authority and there is no independent scene runtime, so AI mutation of existing persistent artifacts is unproven (penalized); exported meshes/animations are the delivery objects.

Generative nodes produce images/video/audio/3D inside a visible node workflow where 'the workflow is the creative process' and results can branch, remix and feed later nodes, giving AI direct creation and iteration on a persistent graph. Humans still run nodes and adjust parameters, and closed implementation leaves schemas unverified; publishing to Community/Tool mode and exports close the delivery loop.

Ask AI lands real page variations in the native graph and MCP edit_page/edit_component mutate nodes by data-node-id, so AI authors and iterates the hosted design graph; theme tokens and version history are durable. Human review/commit and explicit Apply/export steps remain, and page/prototype code intentionally forks from the graph, so the loop is strong but not fully automatic.

Agent skills guide an external coding agent that edits React composition source and Studio writes position/size/rotation/keyframe changes back into source ('agent edits React → Studio evaluates → renderer executes the same composition'). React source plus assets is the durable editable artifact with no separate canvas translation layer, and rendering to video/stills is a closed downstream step.

The studio is a visual composer where humans assemble components into an executable agent record; no AI generation of the design itself is evidenced, and AI does not mutate the agent graph (authority/mutation penalized). The agent record is durable and reusable across test and deployment, giving artifact and delivery moderate strength.

The AI generator selects components and creates a page in a configured Builder.io space, so AI authors the initial page into a durable content graph. Correction/authoring is then handed to Builder.io and Kadnya's AI has no mutation loop on existing pages (penalized); fallback IDs are not persisted pages, and real editing is external.

Brand extraction creates governing studio state and AI generates posts, ads, carousels, images and videos as managed brand assets, so AI is the primary author. No object-level edit schema, version history or generation/iteration semantics are evidenced, so AI mutation of existing assets is unproven (penalized); brand library persistence and publication support delivery.

The model output is written back into the LLM node, giving a minimal AI-writes-to-graph loop, but the graph lives only in React state with no persistence, no chaining and no retained runs. The ordinary loop is closed only as an experiment; there is no delivery to a working product.

The model composes bounded interactive UI as OpenUI Lang within a registered component vocabulary, and incremental editing changes parts of that program while the runtime executes queries/mutations without regenerating, giving AI real authoring and iteration power. Persistence is supplied by the embedding application and the developer controls prompts/tools, so the loop is strong but infrastructure-bound.

The model fills a validated landing-page template schema and the renderer interprets that graph, so AI authors the page structure; editor mutators and autosave let direct edits return to the structured authority. AI mutation of existing pages is only implicit (penalized slightly); publish snapshots, versioning and public-URL export close the delivery loop.

AI generates structured WebsiteOutput content projected into editor, preview and export routes, so AI authors the site. The active endpoint stores websites in module-level dictionaries instead of the modeled relational tables, so durability and AI-iteration semantics are penalized; preview/export exist but production delivery is not evidenced.

A routed skill stack has the host agent produce decks, landing pages and videos under a shared brand authority, with projects persisting under a filesystem root and versioned renders never overwritten, so AI performs the creative production. Iteration is skill-driven file editing mediated by the host agent, and delivery is rendered/published media.

The durable design is the human-built React Flow graph persisted in PostgreSQL and executed topologically via Inngest; AI only generates text inside LLM nodes during execution and does not design or modify the graph. The durable graph, credentials and run records give solid artifact and delivery, but AI authority and mutation are low.

This is a verification/bridge adapter that controls Tracy capture and CSV export binaries, writing .tracy files and bounded summaries; it does not create or design anything. Durable trace artifacts exist but there is no design-authoring loop, so authority, mutation and delivery are correctly low.

Four agents transform a PRD into structured requirements, journeys, wireframes and a high-fidelity UI specification, so AI is the author of the design stages. Stage JSON accumulates but there is no evidenced iteration loop that mutates a persistent artifact (penalized); exporters produce Figma-like and Design Tokens JSON, an exchange format rather than a working UI.

Generation jobs produce candidate variants, the service inspects quality, and project-edit operations apply bounded source changes to real workspace files with snapshot history, so AI generates and directly edits the persistent project. A human selects the promoted variant and reviews, and export/deploy routes close the delivery loop.

Chat AI actions convert requests into node and connection changes that mutate graph objects directly, giving real AI mutation of the durable diagram database with WebSocket collaboration. The diagram is mostly human-constructed and the educational scope leaves scale/conflict behavior unproven; delivery is a working deployed editor without export/publish.

Edgeless Copilot stages AI output as proposed mutations with insert/discard/retry, and insertion mutates the persistent BlockSuite store, so AI creates slides, mind maps, images and prototypes directly in the durable document. AI output requires staged human acceptance, and delivery is in-workspace generation rather than a publish/export pipeline.

D2 text is the interchange authority and the agent bridge accepts replacement code over POST /api/code, so an external agent can write and mutate the diagram source that the editor parses and re-renders. Persistence depends on importing/exporting .d2 since bridge state is process memory (no version graph), and SVG preview/export are the delivery surfaces.

Gemini regenerates complete Draw.io XML or Mermaid source from prompt, references, screenshots or selected regions, making the model the author of the diagram text that rendering and delivery both use. The mutation is whole-document replacement without a structural patch boundary and persistence is browser-local history snapshots, so iteration and cross-device durability are limited.

The agent inspects references and produces a structured Design DNA JSON that is the long-lived authority, with generated HTML as a replaceable projection, so AI defines the portable design spec. There is no hosted project database or direct editor (filesystem/Git mediation), and refinement is agent-mediated, so mutation and delivery are moderate.

Typed agent stages plan and execute images, variants and restyling while a critic-agent evaluates output and repair targets specific assets, so AI authors and iterates the visual work within a durable project JSON that records lineage. A handoff agent packages the selected context into ZIPs for coding agents, closing the delivery loop.

The AI assistant proposes and explains SQL while write execution is gated by tests and confirmation, and accepted SQL changes the live database that ERD surfaces render, so AI edits the authoritative schema only with human confirmation. The durable artifact is the real database, giving moderate artifact and delivery strength.

The versioned React Flow graph is durable and executed topologically by a queued backend with real LLM adapters, but the workflow design is human-built and the 'AI assistant' is rule-based, so AI does not author or mutate the graph. Execution writes to run records, and triggers/logs provide delivery.

Users compose ordered steps that persist in Hasura and run real Groq/HTTP calls with approval gates, but AI only produces content inside executed steps and does not design or mutate the workflow. The persisted workflow is a solid artifact; some steps record synthetic success and deployment relies on an admin secret, limiting delivery.

A repository-local agent can inspect and mutate the shared diagram JSON through server operations while the browser refreshes via SSE, so AI directly edits the durable diagram model that human direct manipulation also targets. Persistence is save-oriented file storage with operation logs, and SVG exports are the delivery snapshots.

Model responses are parsed into files in a real Vite project directory and the refine controller carries the existing project through correction, so AI both creates and iterates the persistent source-file artifact. The builder joins explorer/editor/chat/preview and history snapshots are reopenable; storage is filesystem-heavy and includes committed examples, keeping it transitional.

The promoted authority is a governed YAML agent configuration built by a human in a web editor and launched into isolated container sessions where the contained agent works and its files are viewable. The contained agent does generative work, but configuration design is human-led and active session state is memory-resident; files can be downloaded but deployment trust depends on the provider.

AI design steps route standard/creative/refinement paths and results become panes in the same typed node store humans edit, with reversible undo patches and explicit save, so AI creates into and iterates the persistent authoring graph. Rendered HTML is the delivery surface of the published Astro site, with contextual belief matching at runtime.

Generated component definitions are the durable design unit composed into routes with Firestore overrides, and free-form feedback routes to either a concrete component mutation or a persistent user preference, so AI both authors and repairs the living page. A Playwright benchmark drives and scores the live URL, confirming real delivery.

AI writes the implementation for requested captions/transitions/motion graphics and changes the video timeline, judged in a live preview ('write the implementation for requested captions... compositing effects'). Artifact and export semantics penalized: 'The public material does not disclose its project file format execution sandbox supported effect APIs save/version implementation or export interchange', so durability/versioning evidence is missing.

Gemini authors a serializable UI schema constrained by a prompt vocabulary ('enumerates the allowed node and property vocabulary... sends that contract to Gemini'), and saved schemas reopen as addressable artifacts. Mutation of existing schemas by the model is only weakly evidenced (schemas route lists/creates), and delivery stops at a React render without a deploy/export path; no evidence for AI-driven iteration on saved artifacts.

Qwen generates a whole file set from one response and the app renders/downloads it ('parses named code fences... drives code, preview and download panels'). There is no durable repository or version model: 'Its artifact is the current extracted file bundle in the Gradio session', so mutation and persistence score low; delivery via download panel is real but shallow.

Neo Studio is a control/replay layer over separately installed runtimes ('makes ComfyUI Forge Neo KoboldCPP... behave like one recoverable creative workspace'); it routes and records rather than authoring the design, so authority is low. It does persist outputs with prompts/lineage and supports replay ('reusable action state'), but the creative work is done by human-driven backends.

The presentation agent 'can search, regenerate and edit an existing presentation' and generated XML is parsed into the same editable slide structures as direct editing, giving strong authority and mutation on the managed slide graph. Durable Prisma state plus up to fifty undo snapshots ('holds up to fifty snapshots for undo/redo') evidence the artifact; PPTX export is best-effort and lossy, capping delivery.

The model returns the full HTML/CSS/JS bundle ('expects another complete bundle, making replacement explicit rather than pretending to apply an AST patch'), so AI authors the site but mutation is replace-whole-bundle only. Persistence is weak: 'A five-entry history lives only in React state and is not a durable project or version store'; ZIP export preserves the document for delivery.

A local CodeGen model generates HTML/CSS/JS from a brief ('wraps the brief in a frontend format contract'), so AI is the author. Iteration is human-driven: 'Users can correct all three parts' in editable panes and the download materializes files, but there is no AI mutation of the artifact and no version/project database; the parser's textual delimiters also cap robustness.

The workflow graph is human-authored in a visual DAG editor; AI appears only as an LLM handler node executing inside it ('The runtime calls a local Qwen model through Ollama'), so authority over the designed artifact is low. The PostgreSQL-persisted graph is durable and the runtime genuinely executes it ('creates durable run records and dispatches that order'), but branch/loop/parallel semantics are absent.

A two-pass builder 'first creates a draft then asks a critic to identify defects before rewriting', with quality/repair retries operating on the candidate payload — clear AI-authored generation and AI mutation of the artifact. Typed artifacts are versioned in PostgreSQL ('artifact_version records') and can be previewed or ZIP-exported, though production-safety and semantic round-tripping are unproven.

The agent 'authors an element recipe after visually separating semantic regions' and deterministic scripts turn it into transparent assets plus manifest.json — real AI design decomposition feeding a persistent, editable-ready intermediate authority. It is pipeline infrastructure: mutation of the recipe by AI is not evidenced, and the output is an intermediate asset set for downstream renderers rather than a shipped product.

Gemini proposes a six-line plan from prose and the client renders it as editable nodes ('parses numbered lines into trigger action and output nodes'). Changes live only in client state: 'no durable serialization boundary is implemented', and 'there is no save load version history or export path' — so mutation, artifact and delivery are minimal; human correction happens on a non-persistent projection.

Agent-authored virtual files and direct edits on the running page join into one loop: 'The selected runtime element is mapped back into source rather than retained as a detached annotation', with editor transformers patching the corresponding files. A VFS working file set plus Prisma users/chats/sites and a deploy route that 'materializes the accepted project into delivery state' cover artifact and delivery.

AI dispatches one designer agent per design/edit and authors runnable React/TypeScript/Tailwind programs; visual DOM edits return to source via source-marked mutation manifests that create new Design revisions ('the save path tries to reconcile recorded DOM mutations back into those source files and builds a new Design revision'). Versioned revisions, canvas, exports (code, clone, Figma, image, deploy) are all evidenced; closed compiler/conflict semantics and human Done/AI-edit steps keep it just below the fully AI-native bucket.

OpenRouter creates the site HTML and 'sends the current document back for sequential revisions', giving AI authoring and genuine iteration on the same artifact. The Mongo document persists `latestCode` and supports publication to a stable slug, but there is no version/project graph, and the editor is a source/iframe projection of a single current document.

Three model stages (content, visual design, code) converge on one Manim Python program and rendering is an executable acceptance boundary ('the program must render to an MP4 that the browser can preview and download'). Corrective passes rerun stages and a small deterministic repair set patches code, but there is no source editor or AI-driven edit of the persistent artifact, and session metadata is in-memory.

Gemini proposes elements in the canvas's native vocabulary and app code normalizes/lays them out ('requests JSON in Synthezy’s element vocabulary... applies application-owned layout rules'), so AI authors diagram content. Generated elements join the editable array but AI does not mutate existing elements; persistence spans localStorage, Mongo current-data and `.flowstate`, yet the metadata version number 'is not durable version history'.

A provider-backed chat turn produces structured source files streamed against a codeGenerationSchema and run in an E2B sandbox ('writes every generated file into an E2B sandbox'), so AI is the author. There is no durable project tree or promotion model — 'Persistence stops at conversations' — so mutation and artifact are weak; the README itself calls the product early-stage.

Humans author agent workflows on a Vue Flow canvas; AI is the executed runtime (agent nodes call models) rather than the author of the designed artifact, so authority/mutation are low. The graph is a durable, versioned, governed artifact: migrations 'retain workflows, versions, executions and stage results', with dry runs and real execution following the saved canvas_data.

The agent scaffolds a connected visual editor and can prefill product name, copy, locales and visual direction, but the continuing design work happens in the user-owned editor ('The user receives a connected visual canvas... for continuing work'), so authority is partial and mutation by AI is absent. The project JSON plus hashed assets on disk are authoritative with concrete cache/disk reconciliation; export produces exact PNG bundles at required store sizes.

The model proposes PageBuilder-compatible native markup from a prompt and reference ('returns PageBuilder-compatible content'), which humans then edit, duplicate or remove through normal Magento operations — generation is a proposal into an existing platform graph. Magento PageBuilder owns the published page artifact; durable governance (prompt templates, budgets, request logging, draft queues) is strong and pages reach the storefront.

Skill-gated agents build a design system across Figma and code with real in-place mutation ('preserves variable IDs by renaming and realigning in place' and token sync 'regenerates outputs, detects probable renames and lands changes as a pull request'). Human confirmation gates stop pipelines between stages, so the loop is heavily manual; delivery is reviewable PRs of tokens/components/docs.

The model authors a constrained dashboard component graph ('restricts output to headers, text, metrics, tables, bar or line charts...') that a fixed renderer interprets, so AI authority is real but bounded by the schema. There is 'no direct component editing, persistent project store or revision graph' — JSON lives in session state and downloads raw, capping mutation, artifact and delivery.

An external coding agent creates and edits native Figma nodes — frames, text, vectors, components, variables, auto-layout — through an authenticated bridge ('The returned IDs let later turns inspect or revise the same layer rather than regenerate a replacement image'). Figma's document graph remains the durable authoritative artifact with its native versioning; Figsor is the mutation/inspection surface.

Generation is staged (interview → plan → diagrams → files) and 'a later request includes the existing project so the model returns full updated files', giving real AI authoring and replacement-style iteration. Persistence and release mechanics are weaker than the generation kernel ('persistence and release mechanics are weaker'), so artifact/delivery are penalized and lifecycle is active-transition.

A four-role Mastra workflow (Audit/Architect/Fabricator/Stylist) transforms a typed resume and 'produces a schema-valid candidate', so AI performs the design work on a persistent Zod-typed JSON store. Apply/Discard makes promotion explicit and reversible; PDF output is downstream of structured state ('PDF output is not round-tripped as the editing model'), keeping content revisable.

The AI generator 'requests bounded UI component trees, 3D scenes or CAD feature lists' and validates them into domain schemas serialized into a `.EoStudio` JSON project, giving AI authoring of the unifying artifact. Whole-spec refinement and domain editors modify the saved project; geometric/code exporters (SVG/OBJ/STL/glTF/DXF/React) provide delivery, though many advanced README claims are thinner than the shared core.

Gemini Flash generates the site and the app 'parses the response into the three web-file channels' presented as one preview with separate source views and per-file downloads — real AI authorship and exportable delivery. There is 'no durable revision or correction protocol... another prompt creates another session result', so mutation and artifact are minimal (session-only retention).

AI generates framework-dialect component code directly from a prompt ('asks Gemini for output in one of many named framework dialects'), so authority is high; but correction is entirely manual via Monaco ('Manual changes replace that state'), with no AI re-edit of the artifact, so mutation is low. Artifact is an editable code string with browser-local history; delivery is copy/download of corrected code. Human does the design fixes manually in the editor.

The skill resolves platform/brand direction and writes a complete multi-file HTML/CSS/JS bundle ('writes a CJX-ready multi-file HTML/CSS/JS bundle'), giving AI strong authorship of the designed artifact. Later changes pass through a dedicated expansion path instead of regenerating unrelated platforms, evidencing mutation of the existing bundle. foundation.css is the token authority and generated source is authoritative; delivery is a handoff bundle adapted to a host stack. Some human steering of the skill remains.

The plugin reviews designs through five lenses and outputs recommendations; it 'does not say that the model rewrites nodes, applies fixes or owns a parallel design graph', so it does not author the design nor mutate it. Figma remains the working design authority and the output is decision evidence for a human correction loop. No source/acceptance run found; artifact is recommendations rather than a persistent designed artifact.

DStoAI materializes Figma system context into a portable Build Task Markdown snapshot; the downstream coding agent 'owns code changes' while DStoAI owns the extraction/materialization boundary, so it is a one-way design-code bridge rather than a design author. It cannot touch the design after export ('one-way materialization'), and delivery stops at a downloadable document. Implementation/export grammar are closed, penalizing evidence for artifact semantics.

AI converts code↔UML↔image through a structured JSON intermediate ('.RohanUML format preserves that structured model'), giving it conversion-authorship of the model artifact. The visual editor supports 'relationship correction and dynamic layout', but no evidence that AI itself iterates on the existing model, so mutation is moderate. Generated code and reverse-engineered UML need compilation and domain review; delivery is exportable diagrams/code.

claude-eda is scaffolding/infrastructure: it 'assembles constraints skills agents and MCP servers' so an external agent can work in a KiCad workspace; the product itself does not create the design. KiCad files and constraint documents remain source and ERC/DRC results are evidence, so the durable artifact is real but AI mutation happens through the external agent bridge. Delivery reaches manufacturing handoff. As a bridge/orchestration project authority and mutation stay low per the rating rules.

FanBox is a coordination cockpit: 'files remain authoritative while a desktop shell brings previews diffs terminals snapshots and resumable... sessions into one visual cockpit'. It does not author or directly mutate the design (agents do, through scoped file ops and embedded sessions), so authority/mutation are low. The durable artifact is the local workspace and Git state; user resumes agent sessions and previews/rolls back changes, a semi-automatic loop ending in a working workspace rather than a published result.

The model writes project files from chat tool calls into a Supabase schema separating projects/files/messages/versions; restore 'resolves the chosen version and writes its snapshot back into the current project', and Monaco and the agent operate on the same file model — AI and human co-edit one durable artifact. WebContainer runs and ZIP export deliver the work. Transactional recovery across running runtime/chat/deployment is unproven, slightly capping delivery.

Natural language goes through a Spring service to an anonymous JSX component rendered live by react-live ('user can correct source and see the same state projected without another model call'). AI authors the component but mutation is manual only — no AI iteration; there is no project store, dependency graph or deployment protocol, so the artifact and delivery are bounded to a single component session.

Gemini is constrained to return a named component plus render call and react-live renders the cleaned string with error reporting; the page owns 'prompt, source, copy operation and code/preview mode' with no persistent projects or historical variants. AI authors the component source; mutation and persistence are absent beyond the current editor state, so artifact/delivery stay at component-session level.

The model returns Matplotlib-oriented Python that the server executes to produce a plotted visual whose element geometry becomes editable Fabric.js objects — AI authors the drawing. Human manipulation updates the same in-process canvas record, but there is no evidence the AI can re-edit the existing canvas after generation. Canvas and chat state live in a Python dictionary and 'restarting the server clears both', so there is no durable artifact and no publish/delivery layer.

A visual React Flow graph persists ReactFlowData and NodeConfigurations in PostgreSQL as a capability-attachment contract that is hydrated into an execution contract for Orleans actors to run model conversations. The design (agent composition) is human-built in the canvas, but the platform persists it durably and executes it across providers. The graph is not the whole platform state (credentials/MCP/history live outside it), so design is a governed persisted composition rather than a portable artifact.

Gemini is asked for HTML/CSS/JS and each response is written into a generated workspace, creating an inspectable multi-file artifact. There are 'no durable database versions or conversational modification', so the AI cannot modify the existing generated work and the current directory is authority. The browser previews and the backend packages the three files as a ZIP — a portable delivery endpoint but a thin correction/persistence model.

Core is 'prompt-to-interface generation semantic HTML visual refinement persistent private canvas' with local agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity) connecting to the workspace — AI authors interfaces and the product describes a continuous 'prompt inspect refine connect ship' loop on a persistent canvas. Web delivery is current while native iOS/Android and parts of Figma are staged early-access/roadmap. The implementation data model is not public, capping mutation/delivery evidence.

The Figma plugin drafts usage guidance from the selected component's native metadata (description, properties, variants, styles) into editable documentation on the canvas, and the maker frames output as a starting point — AI authors guidance text, not the design itself. Public evidence shows no automatic dependency tracking after component changes, no diff between regenerated drafts, and no stable export format, so AI mutation and delivery are unproven; human correction is part of the loop.

The scene graph is the canonical model: 'AI generation, screenshot reverse-engineering, manual property changes, responsive variants and React/Tailwind export all pass through a structured visual model', and AI/reverse-UI routes 'must return data that can enter the same model rather than bypassing it'. Nodes carry identity, props, styles, tokens and interactions, giving AI and human a shared durable structured artifact. Export and responsive preview deliver results; no server-backed version ledger is evidenced, capping recovery.

Retains Bolt's generated-file protocol (structured artifact/file actions) but manages a real project: users build web or React Native artifacts, inspect/edit files, run WebContainer/Expo projections, reopen saved projects, and deploy. Project code/file maps/chat history persist in PostgreSQL and the Vercel deploy route converts the accepted file map into a deployment and persists the release URL — generation, correction, recovery and delivery share one project authority. No immutable version graph is evidenced.

A direct client-to-model request returns a JSON file map stored on-device (AsyncStorage/Expo document directory); the editor 'reads and displays files but does not write manual edits back, so the generated map... is authoritative'. AI authors a real local artifact but neither the AI nor the user can modify the persisted map through the app, and the sandbox/deploy paths are fabricated stubs ('builds a successful-looking URL... without making a provider request'). Delivery is inspection/export scaffolding plus a separately hosted URL.

The built-in BYOK agent reads the current file and selection and 'runs the same create property layout component search and export commands available to the application', producing native frames/text/vectors/components/styles on a plain-text YAML .design artifact that autosaves to disk; per-canvas undo includes AI operations and Git supplies durable versions and branches. Human and AI co-edit the same authoritative file with a design-system source/generated layer. Delivery spans SVG/PDF/HTML/React/video exports plus Figma round-trip; desktop implementation is closed, so command/validation internals are architecture-level.

A single-file product where an AutoGPT-style assistant 'turns intent into a plan and editor actions' against a layer model with undo/redo; JSON is the recoverable project representation while PNG/JPG/SVG are delivery projections. The assistant mutates the canvas layer model through editor actions (AI mutation exists), but the loop is a small local canvas with no server-side account or collaboration; delivery is image/JSON export only.

Claude drafts and extracts from source material in Content Studio while automated tags/knowledge signals 'can be reviewed, approved, or overridden instead of silently becoming curriculum truth' — AI authors instructional content but humans gate it through version/approval workflows. The React Flow graph models learning behavior and PostgreSQL persists projects and xAPI events, with publishing and analytics in one loop. Pedagogical quality/compliance remain human judgment.

A one-line SaaS/site request is routed through brief, research, architecture, build, design system, motion, media, quality and deployment, where 'parallel build and verify agents operate the consuming repository' and Playwright screenshots, vision review, Lighthouse, axe, SEO and console checks form release evidence before deploying to Cloudflare and verifying the live result. This is an end-to-end automated delivery loop on a persisted repository, with gates standing in for human review.

A planner turns the request into pages/data models/auth/integrations, a deterministic scaffolder creates the file graph, and 'the coder asks routed models to rewrite files one at a time' while persisting spec and per-file rows after every stage with checkpoint restore APIs. AI authors and mutates the durable PostgreSQL-backed project, but the preview is a static-analysis stub and GitHub/Railway publication return 501 stubs; delivery is a ZIP of database-authoritative files. Monaco edits are ephemeral local-only, so manual edits do not share authority.

TemPad Dev is a read-only bridge: it 'turns a selected Figma node into implementation-grade semantic context' (semantic tree, screenshots, assets, variables, tokens under a context-budget preflight) and 'the reviewed toolset is read-only with respect to the Figma document'. It does not write the design and cannot mutate Figma; the intermediate representation only grounds code that an external agent writes, so it is design-to-code infrastructure rather than a design author. No delivery beyond grounding downstream coding.

Natural-language prompts, uploaded diagrams/images, PDFs and documents 'can become editable draw.io content' through more than a dozen provider integrations, giving AI conversion-authorship of a normal inspectable canvas. Yjs-backed shared state and team spaces make the content collaboratively editable, but no evidence shows the AI itself iterating on existing drawings after generation; recognition of images/PDFs carries provenance risk. Exported draw.io documents are the portable recovery boundary.

A generative model writes NPC dialogue while 'deterministic rules validate those proposals and choose transitions', so AI authors visible narrative content inside a governed state machine; the visual editor and MCP server 'mutate the same content graph through preconditioned transactions'. The project graph (settings.json with characters, scenes, roles, etc.) is durable and portable via .monogatari import/export with SHA-256 manifests, and executable quality suites make routes replayable. Authority is deliberately partial (route/ending withheld from the model).

ComfyUI is the workflow host: its design artifact is a directed node graph that 'remains visible and rewritable instead of collapsing into a single generation request', with blueprint JSON and subgraphs preserving reusable wiring. Authority over the design rests with the workflow author (human builds the graph; models run inside it), and AI-generated outputs are run results rather than graph mutations. The graph and referenced environment are the durable, editable, reusable authority, delivering images/video/audio/3D outputs.

An agent server for 'creating and changing hierarchical schematics and PCB layouts' with native schematic/PCB writers, where the PCB workflow creates a preview and layout_id the user reviews 'before the stored proposal may be applied' — AI authors and directly mutates saved KiCad files (the authoritative artifact) with recoverable checkpoints. Final ERC/DRC is delegated to kicad-cli, delivering validated, exportable boards. Human review gates placement proposals.

An installable correction layer that lets an agent click matched widgets, trigger QActions, set values and process host event loops in legacy PySide/PyQt tools, with a screenshot of the exact widget after a change as visual return evidence. It does not author design and holds no persistent design artifact (screenshots are evidence only); it is a bridge enabling an ordinary UI-correction loop in tools that otherwise lack an agent-friendly API. Authority/artifact stay low per the bridge rule.

MCP surface can 'get the current source, set revised source, and request a render', so an external agent addresses the live editor and directly mutates the open diagram source; AI syntax fixes repair malformed Mermaid. Mermaid text remains the authoritative, portable artifact with file/local-storage persistence, but 'repair is bounded by review' and the setter lacks evidence of conflict control or semantic validation, so human_loop/authority are capped.

The skill directs the agent to 'creating, revising, auditing and exporting' figures with one authoritative plotting backend, so AI authors and iterates the figure from source data; 'the plotting script and source data are the reproducible authority' with editable-text SVG/PDF and raster TIFF/PNG delivery. Execution quality depends on external libraries/fonts and data, so authority is constrained; revision is replot-based rather than element-level mutation.

Generation feeds a 'layered shared canvas' where users arrange layers and continue with 'generative edits such as expansion, removal or restyling', i.e. AI directly mutates existing canvas content. 'Canvas layers are the editable authority before export' with account workspace, reusable layouts and video timeline state; delivery is downloaded images and rendered video. Human still drives composition/layer control, capping authority and human_loop.

Claude streams a tagged artifact under a 'full-content replacement contract' and the streamed content is promoted into the workspace, so AI authors and can replace the component; React source in editor state is 'the live authority' and both AI content and human edits compile into the preview. But the artifact is session-scoped ('no database, file export, version graph or reopen path') and delivery is preview-only, so artifact/delivery are penalized.

KiClaw is a file-first MCP server for safe KiCad iteration: it 'permits constrained edits, invokes KiCad's own checks and returns a post-mutation diff and evidence', so AI mutates the persistent KiCad project with snapshots and evidence. As infrastructure it does not author the design itself (authority capped), the guarded loop leaves 'electrical intent and final fabrication approval outside the server' (delivery capped), and the companion skill decides when to inspect/mutate/verify/stop.

Anthropic generates archived HTML artifacts, but a human-authored taxonomy constrains recommendation and the user assembles/alters the recipe before generation, keeping an 'explicit decision boundary'; iteration 'creates lineage rather than overwrite' and derives subpages from a design contract. Archived artifacts, site/page rows and retained artifact lineage give durable persistence, though the human decision boundary keeps human_loop involvement relatively high.

The workspace persists agent graphs in SQLite ('database.py enforces project-scoped foreign keys') with version restoration, a genuinely durable structured artifact. But the dossier shows no AI authoring or AI mutation of the graph - the user manually composes nodes/edges in Streamlit - and the generic graph-to-runtime path is unevenly implemented ('runtime breadth is uneven'), so authority, mutation, human_loop and delivery are low.

GPT-4o is prompted for 'HTML CSS JavaScript and metadata' and parsed into a combined document, so AI authors the whole site in one pass. There is no post-generation edit path (one-shot: 'no saved project authority is established', projects page is a hard-coded array), and the result lives in session state until exported via Blob/ZIP download; artifact and mutation are therefore low.

The archived workspace stores a planning graph in SQLite ('node and edge tables'), a durable structured artifact, but the canvas 'change handlers do not POST those direct edits back' and the graph is 'not traversed to run an agent'; planning edges never compile into an execution schedule. AI coding happens via separate OpenCode sessions, while the visual design canvas is user-driven with an unfinished edit-save loop, so authority/mutation/human_loop/delivery are all weak.

A local Llama 3 model 'asks for a JSON object containing HTML, CSS and JavaScript', so AI authors the site; but the raw message is parsed into a sandbox iframe with 'no export, correction or recovery path' and the result 'exists only for the page session'. Mutation is one-shot, artifact is transient session state, and delivery is preview-only.

The ten-skill suite routes schematic/PCB/library/repair/release work so the agent iterates on real KiCad projects, and the PowerShell wrapper runs official ERC/DRC, parity and zone checks and exports manufacturing files with a machine-readable manifest. Release readiness is an evidence gate ('NOT_READY_FOR_PCBA_UPLOAD' until verified), so delivery to fabrication is strong; as a skill/CLI tooling line the AI's design authority is bounded by external board-house specs.

Gemini is instructed to return body-suitable Tailwind/Flowbite HTML that the workspace displays and packages as a downloadable HTML file, so AI authors the page from the sidebar conversation. Follow-up changes come through new prompts and replace the current HTML rather than editing a structured graph ('does not establish a versioned source tree'), and prompt history is not shown to be a revision lineage, capping mutation/artifact.

Shape's design source map 'records exact character spans for scrubbable CSS and Tailwind values and rewrites only the selected span', and the design agent writes files to the filesystem with Keep/Undo decisions against a session baseline, so AI directly mutates the authoritative repository source. AI Visual previews are sandboxed and reviewed before mutation ('reviewing agent edits'), Git remains durable history, and the visual tools never introduce a second design document.

The hosted service generates the deck from notebook sources with user-chosen format/length/audience; per-slide instructions group into 'Pending Changes' and 'generating the revision creates an entirely new deck' with previously generated decks loadable, so the hosted deck is a durable working authority the AI revises. PDF/PowerPoint are explicit delivery copies, and the user stages/reviews revisions, keeping human_loop moderate.

The kx engine 'reads, edits, renders, verifies and fabricates schematics and boards through a session state machine' with byte-stable source handling, so AI performs direct edits on authoritative KiCad files and nothing saves before geometric review. Fabrication produces grouped BOM/placement/Gerber only after review; as a skills/engine tooling line the design authority is bounded by pinned tooling and external optional services.

Specula BOS is an open product/governance architecture ('seven system layers, five-domain memory architecture, workshop protocols') with the Brand Governance Playbook template as the durable handoff, so it is documented/artifactual but not a design runtime; the repository 'explicitly withholds' AI configurations, prompt libraries and implemented JSON memory schemas. AI onboarding exists but 'without granting it final authority', and there is no implementation or mutation loop - no evidence of AI creating design work.

Google GenAI 'streams generation and follow-up changes' into a separated virtual file set in browser state, and imported files 'enter the same graph as generated ones', so AI authors and revises the artifact. There is no backend persistence layer ('does not claim a backend persistence layer'), durable versions and hosted deployment are absent, and copy/export act on the in-memory graph, capping artifact and delivery.

OpenAI/Anthropic generation creates a component plus its initial revision, and later changes are 'anchored to the existing code instead of asking for an unrelated replacement', with revisions persisted and forkable into new identities - a genuine branch choice. Prisma schema persists components and revisions, and preview is 'compiled from stored source' downstream of the DB; the code tab is read-only so correction returns through chat, and no export path is evidenced (delivery capped).

This adapter embeds an MCP server in Substance 3D Designer so an agent can 'create a rendered procedural PBR material package' through the real Designer session and render path - genuine native-material creation and delivery. It is a bridge/adapter with a 'narrow but complete' surface (inspect + create one material pass), so it does not author broad design nor iterate over multiple edits, keeping authority/mutation and delivery modest.

HyCanvas is a full visual platform where 'AI output enters the same document system rather than becoming the only source', the native HYC graph is directly editable, and persistence includes 'repository writes, CRDT branches, history updates' plus a portable .hyc export for cross-instance recovery. AI is a workspace-scoped BYOK layer over a human-driven document engine, so authority is moderate; the render/export pipeline (PNG/PDF/video/document projections and export API) gives strong delivery.

The builder stores agents/topic edges as portable JSON in localStorage edited via React Flow, so the design is a durable-but-client-side artifact, but the user manually draws the mesh and AI does not generate or mutate it. Deployment is a demonstration handoff that 'does not establish a general importer' for arbitrary builder JSON, so the canvas is a coordination artifact rather than cluster authority.

A UX architect agent converts the brief into a plan and 'a bounded group of wireframers produces screens' written as committed spec.md and HTML under an artifact contract, so AI authors the design deliverables; the 'review step cannot be skipped', keeping human review authoritative. Iteration is workflow re-runs rather than direct AI edits of one artifact, and DesignSync is one-way, capping mutation.

Model output is 'parsed into the same element graph used by direct canvas controls', so AI-generated frames/text/images become natively selectable/editable objects in the Redux canvas graph with a shared undo/redo stack - real AI-to-canvas mutation. Undo/redo is in-memory with 'no durable project database', HandoffPanel exports React TSX/CSS from the graph, and security/robustness are prototype-grade, capping artifact and delivery.

Gemini returns a path-keyed files map that Convex persists alongside messages so the workspace can be reopened, and the result is projected in Sandpack with JSZip export - a real generated-file artifact with recovery. Every user message triggers 'whole-bundle regeneration rather than target-level DOM correction', manual Sandpack edits stay local, and there is no element-to-source mapping or commit graph, capping mutation.

The FastAPI endpoint asks GPT for HTML/CSS-only output and the client shows the returned string as code and an iframe, so AI authors the page in one pass. There is 'no intermediary component graph, model-driven patch protocol or server-side project record' - a new prompt replaces the result and copy-to-clipboard is the only delivery path - so mutation, artifact and delivery are minimal.

PX-bench is an evaluation product: it places a customer's coding agent in held-out host apps and 'run[s] and score[s]' product experience, producing run evidence and a scored report tied to the modified app - an evidence-producing verification operation, not a design author (low authority per bridge/verification rule). The benchmark run evidence and scored report are durable artifacts with automated rubrics and explicit versioning, but private scenario corpus and scorer implementation are not exposed (architecture-level evidence only).

The skill instructs the agent to build a single offline HTML board with durable frame IDs, permanently identified phone/tablet/desktop frames, flow connectors and annotations - AI authors the specification artifact and the HTML board 'and its implementation contract are the source authority'. Output hooks check offline rendering and pairing, but iteration/mutation beyond initial creation is not evidenced, and delivery is handoff/specification rather than a deployed product.

The React Flow graph is durable product data persisted via Convex ('stores the graph alongside generated tool configuration'), and Gemini acts as a graph-to-config compiler whose structured output is persisted - so the AI materializes a runnable config from the visual design. Hosted execution is narrower than the palette ('explicit weather-tool calling path... do not interpret arbitrary control-flow edges'), and publication exposes preview/integration code without provisioning infrastructure, capping delivery.

LLM proposals are constrained changes that a deterministic pipeline re-resolves and gates before persistence: 'The pipeline re-resolves pointers against current evidence and applies trust and substance gates'. Draft prompts are not final truth, so authority is shared with deterministic governance; persistent schema-governed YAML records are a strong artifact. Diagrams are governed projections, so delivery covers published topology and visual output. No evidence of autonomous design creation, so authority/mutation stay moderate.

The model has broad HTML authority inside the client sandbox: 'a prompt becomes HTML and Tailwind source' with the whole authoring loop in one page. There is no iteration on existing work ('no file tree, revision history, visual element mutation'), so mutation is one-shot at 2. The sandbox document is transient and the only delivery mechanism is copying source, so artifact and delivery are limited.

Recraft Studio generates and refines typed visual objects on an infinite canvas: 'Prompts adapt to the selected object and edits produce a new image version while preserving the original', and the vector editor lets users select shapes, drag anchors and recolor paths. Mutation and artifact are strong (raster versions, editable SVG structure). Human still drives refinement and selection, and delivery is full export to SVG/PDF/Lottie/PNG/JPG/TIFF.

Claude generates a path-keyed React project or plain web bundle ('asks Claude for a path-keyed React project or a plain web bundle') persisted under a MongoDB project identity with its conversation and copy/vote reuse state. Artifact is strong (file graph + Sandpack preview) but iterative mutation of the existing artifact is not evidenced beyond conversation-driven regeneration, and delivery stops at live preview and copying rather than deployment.

The App Prototyping agent produces a real Next.js codebase and 'each of its responses commits changes to local Git', with Code OSS files, terminal, and deployment to App Hosting/Hosting/Cloud Run behind it. Mutation is direct workspace/file/commit-level editing and repair; artifact is durable files plus Git and deploy receipts. Human approval gates (blueprint approval, diff review, validation) keep human_loop at 7; sunset lifecycle does not change the score as last evidenced.

buildWithAI() drafts a model-backed pipeline from a brief but 'the documented workflow requires reviewing the returned configuration... AI proposes the artifact while the user retains authority over it'. Pipelined configs are structured and API-visible with CRUD, execution, traces and schedules, so delivery reaches runtime execution. The visual graph/persistence internals are closed (no evidence for them), so mutation and artifact are capped at contract level.

External agents create/perceive/mutate the same hosted versioned Composition graph the human edits live, headlessly: 'one clearly_canvas_act batch... then read the result through clearly_canvas_perceive'. Scene nodes, components, tokens and prototypes are durable structured graph semantics. Human audit/refine and verification steps (batch partial-durability, export projection caveats) keep human_loop and delivery at 7; code delivery is a separate Git clock.

A syntax-aware repair loop: 'the agent can call Mermaid validation/rendering tools, observe an error, and revise the source until it reaches an acceptable state' — direct iterative mutation of the diagram source. Generated Mermaid is shown to the user before application, and the resulting Mermaid source remains editable outside the app. Authority is real generation but review-gated; validation cannot prove design correctness, capping delivery to rendered diagrams.

A Claude Code skill pipeline whose output is 'a controlled mutation of an existing or newly created frontend codebase'; design-to-code discovers framework/conventions before generation and maps approved values into project components and tokens. Mutation targets real repository files. A required CSS-value comparison table confirmed by the user is the write gate, so human_loop is heavy; the destination repository owns the durable artifacts and delivery.

A server embedded in Nuke dispatches typed compositing operations scoped to graph and material identity; corrections leave pixels outside the selection unchanged and the .nk script/native node graph remain authoritative. This is agent-controlled mutation of a durable native graph artifact, but authority is constrained (typed ops, not free design) and delivery is graph results plus sampled renders as evidence. Node-asset skills add a reuse-governance loop.

The agent proposes several style vectors, the user selects or rejects them, and '/apply converts the accepted direction into DTCG-compatible tokens and implementation guidance'; the accepted-store persists choices. This is human-selected AI proposals that constrain real code implementation and review, not full AI authorship. The accepted store is a constraint record, not a drawable canvas, so artifact is a durable record and delivery is the constrained build.

A Claude Code skill that chooses and operates 3D production routes with a shared loop 'generate or model, render, inspect the image, critique the worst defect and correct it'. It operates real Blender/Fusion/Three.js source, so authority and mutation are genuine but tool-grounded. It supplies guidance and code patterns with 'no independent modeling runtime or persistence service', so artifact and delivery rely on the external tools; human steering is expected.

The agent can modify the selected page or objects in the Draw.io graph rather than reissuing the whole document, while 'the editable Draw.io graph remains the working artifact' with content version management. Selection narrows agent context and versions bound mutation. Human selects context and reviews, and delivery is the editable editor plus MCP exposure rather than a separate publishing path.

AI builds model context from the current character card and can request 3/5/8 front-end directions, previewed and then deliberately chosen; agent patches are constrained json:patch proposals with a pre-apply snapshot the user accepts or rejects. The coupled character card plus embedded HTML/CSS is a durable structured artifact in IndexedDB, but variant selection and accept/reject steps make the loop human-intensive; delivery is JSON/card PNG export.

An agent-native PPTX editor whose declarative patch language 'inspects stable shape IDs, pre-validates every requested operation, applies the patch atomically' — direct mutation of the existing .pptx, which remains the native authority. HTML creation compiles into the same patch IR, keeping one writer for creation, edit, lint, diff and render verify. Review of patches/measurements keeps human_loop at 6; delivery is verified renderable decks.

Gemini writes the HTML document and 'visual moves rewrite source': DOM drag reordering moves the source DOM node and serializes the full document back into the same HTML string. That is real source mutation, though limited to reordering elements with IDs. Artifact is a single HTML doc plus localStorage project autosave; delivery reaches ZIP and Netlify deploy API, but arbitrary property editing and server recovery are not established.

The builder 'derives candidate agents from local file metadata and lets the user accept, rearrange or simulate the suggested graph', so the graph suggestion is data-derived and the user arranges it; the engine topologically executes nodes as dataflow. The workflow graph and logs persist in local SQLite ('single-machine authority with no collaborative version graph'). It executes workflows locally but does not author a persistent design artifact itself.

Gemini streams component source into an isolated renderer and completed generations become selectable browser-local versions; generation is one-shot per prompt with no mutation of an existing artifact. Persistence is localStorage prompt/code history, and delivery is previewed/copyable component source. No iteration or deployment path is evidenced, so mutation, artifact and delivery are low.

A four-Skill delivery/verification product that 'starts after a DCC or engine has produced an export' and makes the handoff verifiable; it creates publish manifests, packaging and acceptance evidence rather than authoring design or mutating creative work. Hash manifests are durable records consumed by OpenUSD/farm/Flow systems, and delivery is a verifiable release handoff, but authority and mutation correctly stay low as a bridge.

The AI assistant edits the same React Flow graph as the user through a constrained tool vocabulary ('adding, updating, deleting, and connecting nodes'), so mutation is direct and in-session, and generated structure stays negotiable by hand. The strained edge is durable ownership: 'not a substantial server-side project/version subsystem', so artifact and delivery are capped at the canvas/in-session level.

A project-local CAD workbench where 'STEP-first authority is explicit' and a geometry-authority module prevents the derived mesh projection from becoming canonical; agents and humans share the CLI workbench and review bundles. This is structured tooling around authoritative CAD source rather than AI-authored design, so authority is moderate. Persistent STEP/parametric source plus reviewable export bundles give solid artifact and delivery.

The generator enhances the brief and has Groq/HF/OpenRouter produce the final single HTML document; a MERN mode emits one file at a time. The project is 'one current snapshot rather than a version graph' in MongoDB, so iterative mutation of an existing artifact is not evidenced. Delivery is real: GitHub/Netlify/Vercel API routes execute provider deploy calls and report failures.

Groq returns a JSON object with a full HTML document; corrections 'include latestCode in a later correction prompt and replace it after a valid response' — regeneration anchored to current source rather than fine-grained editing. MongoDB owns the current document, conversation and publication fields, and the backend deploy action serves that same document publicly, giving real delivery; no immutable snapshots exist, limiting artifact and mutation.

A forensic decision workspace with four predefined specialist agents run individually or in order on case geometry and evidence; 'users... cannot add or reconnect agents', so topology is fixed. Model output is grounded in case state via per-stage JSON contracts and stored as reviewable case records with a PDF report. This is a visual AI decision/coordination loop, not autonomous design, so authority and mutation are moderate and human drives each run.

The agent separates video understanding from editorial decisions: evidence is recorded in checkpoints.jsonl, 'the editing loop writes decisions to sequences.jsonl and derives EDL, FCPXML or OTIO only from supported records', with corrections re-derived upstream. Durable JSONL ledgers are a strong artifact and revision-pinned multi-cut export delivers. Authority is editorial suggestion grounded in evidence rather than full autonomous authorship, with a human loop for guidance and correction.

Architecture-level claims show agent-created screens/flows/variants in a multiplayer studio grounded in real components/tokens, with 'MCP can give a coding agent the design output and a pull request can enter normal repository review'. Human review/decision is explicit between variants and production source. Closed internals mean no proof of bidirectional round-tripping, so mutation is capped; delivery via MCP handoff/PR to real production source is strong.

AI architects operate on the persisted React Flow node/edge graph while humans co-edit the same authority; the presentation agent reads all project surfaces into an append-only blackboard, creates an exact slide skeleton and checkpoints slide JSON. Mutation is direct on a structured graph and delivery reaches PDF/JSON/Markdown. The presentation is a projection of project evidence rather than autonomous design authorship, keeping authority at 7.

Prompts/text/documents become a deck graph that is the authority, and natural-language remix at element or slide scope coexists with direct drag/resize/rotate on the same element model — 'direct manipulation to the same element model that generation creates'. Undoable history and IndexedDB persistence support iteration. Delivery materializes HTML/PDF/PNG/PPTX from the stored deck graph; it is local-first with no hosted collaboration.

The model generates a complete HTML document with optional pattern/palette, and the refinement operation 'accepts the current HTML and a refinement instruction and requires a complete updated document', anchoring correction to the existing artifact. But the HTML is an in-memory value with no durable project store ('transient until downloaded'), so artifact and delivery are limited to preview, copy and index.html download.

Each model response becomes a versioned file inside a branching version graph, and 'direct Monaco edits go through the same graph as draft user files before later model corrections' — both AI and human mutations are recorded as versions in IndexedDB. Files are projected through sandboxed srcdoc and React/Vue/Svelte/Lit exports are derived from the HTML file. Mutation and artifact are strong; delivery is framework export rather than deployment.

The product packages Draw.io/Excalidraw MCP skills so an AI harness turns intent into architecture documents and editable diagrams, which are the durable results ('Architecture documents and editable diagrams are the durable results'). Mutation is delivered through skill instructions for XML authoring, icon catalogs and layout antipatterns rather than an implemented repair loop. The external MCP servers own the live canvas, so the product itself is a workflow pack; human drive and review remain.

The product is explicitly 'not an autonomous agent; it is the structured, owned artifact' — a canonical design-system Markdown with approved assets that keeps human/AI marketing work in one visual language. There is no AI mutation: 'the system does not automatically lint or write generated artifacts', enforcement depends on the consuming agent and reviewers. It is a usable, versioned contract for agent-fed generation, so artifact is strong but authority and mutation are AI-adjacent.

'The agent owns much of the HTML generation' — the coding agent produces a self-contained HTML deck, and the workflow gates on three first-slide previews the user selects or mixes before expansion. The durable artifact is an inspectable, editable single HTML file ('the saved or downloaded HTML file remains the portable authority'); correction workflow and inline editing allow revision. Delivery materializes HTML plus Playwright PDF, but PowerPoint output is one-way extraction only, so export scope is partial.

AI composes image/video/3D generation, inserts reconstructed assets into Blender scenes, and a VLM critique drives iterative repair of lighting, pose, environment and materials within a bounded action space ('feedback_apply.py applies them with anti-oscillation controls'). The render–review–repair loop is largely automatic, mutating Blender scenes directly. Blender scenes plus RGB/masks/depth/normals and split manifests form a durable, training-ready dataset authority; humans mainly configure and consume the dataset.

A marketplace of 25 skills and 33 agents lets AI harnesses perform Canvas component development and Drupal-to-Canvas migration as a phased artifact protocol: 'Specialists analyze the source, extract CSS, build and audit components, test in Storybook... visually verify the result'. Files and checklists carry state across agent turns, so agents iteratively mutate migration artifacts, and Drupal Canvas is the destination authority. The product remains a distributed skill pack; humans visually verify, and delivery reaches full-site migration.

Three model roles (planner, generator, reviewer) turn intent into a governed structured-JSON plan and then JSX constrained to the repo's component set; the reviewer pass 'can resubmit a render error for a model-authored repair'. Artifact is penalized: 'the inspected code keeps the current plan and source in client state rather than a persisted project model'. Delivery is visual preview via react-live plus source, with no export or durable project record.

Two orchestration skills drive a cross-stack creative-coding agent that 'builds a visual universe and persistent stack-aware MASTER.md', with gates at thesis, variant and identity where the user requests live motion/contrast artifacts. The repository source and generated design-system files become authoritative while previews are disposable, so AI iterates on a persistent code artifact. Human gates creative direction at each milestone; delivery reaches live preview routes in the target stack.

The model is 'deliberately denied final-pixel authority': it routes intent, plans JSON and emits constrained Mermaid, while deterministic parsers/layout code materialize an editable React Flow graph ('React Flow becomes authority after compilation'). This bounds authority since deterministic code owns final geometry. Mutation is one-shot snapshot application with one undo checkpoint; users then edit native nodes. The graph, autosave snapshots and ZIP export with project.json preserve a durable editable artifact, with no cloud required.

An OpenAI route converts a natural-language request into 'allowed node and edge structures' on an editable React Flow canvas, and users inspect and change parameters before execution; generation does not bypass the workflow schema. Artifact is strong: PostgreSQL persists workflows and execution records, and the same graph materializes as TypeScript and runs through Workflow DevKit. A local-first home-automation platform where a typed Workflow graph in MongoDB is edited in Studio and a bounded NL path normalizes requests into supported trigger/action types and saves the workflow ('It does not pass arbitrary generated code to devices'), so AI authoring is bounded and safety-governed. An OpenAI call generates React/Tailwind JSX shown in an isolated srcDoc preview; 'generated React source is transient until the user saves it into the gallery', with Firebase persisting a small promoted-variant collection rather than a project graph. Relai lets a user's external MCP agent mutate the native Figma graph while file-carried rules (conventions, precedents, no-go zones, confirmation dial, selection lock) govern what may change — 'the model proposes work, while the active design artifact sets the authority envelope'. The durable artifact is the Figma file with policy persisted as plugin data; the designer controls the confirmation dial.

OpenRouter returns one complete HTML document with embedded style and behavior, written into a SQLite project for the authenticated user; the preview iframe closes a visual loop. Delivery stops at preview, code view and clipboard copy rather than a hosted or packaged deploy.

Delivery is runtime execution plus code download from that same session artifact.

The model produces a project-oriented file map that is persisted behind project routes and 'updated through follow-up prompts', with the client builder projecting files against the same workspace — a real model-to-project-to-preview loop.
