An agent skill/CLI/MCP that reverse-engineers starter tokens from public websites into normalized.json, tokens.json and tokens.css — a deterministic extraction bridge ('It defines Design as evidence-backed system extraction'), not AI-authored design. Mutation is one-shot emission with no iteration, and provenance is explicitly evidence-based ('Generated tokens therefore require review before governance use'). Artifact is durable; the audit/token matchers report confidence rather than claiming intentionality.

Caliper renders a real application, lets a person visually edit, and 'asks an agent to rewrite the owning source using repository selectors, tokens, conventions and accumulated design history' — source stays authoritative and a preview mutation counts only when the agent materializes a file change and the app rerenders. Design history feeds back into later agent actions, with branching/step-back/recovery advertised. Implementation is closed and early-access, so framework coverage and merge semantics are unproven but the authority arrangement is clear.

Model output is restricted to a fixed component schema — 'The schema—not emitted JSX—is the canonical UI artifact', with the renderer mapping validated nodes to the component library and Supabase persisting sessions, messages and versions. Authority is bounded by the whitelist and mutation is versioned recovery rather than demonstrated deep iteration on existing UI. Artifact is durable and versioned; delivery is runtime preview plus session/version recovery, with no export evidence.

AI Studio routes prompts through Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini/DeepSeek and 'model output participates in real file and site operations', generating PHP/HTML/CSS/JS pages that stay deployable files. Structural operations and visual edits 'converge on that managed workspace' with SQLite durable state, snapshot/undo, and a preview-then-publish lifecycle, so the canonical artifact is broader than chat. Human reviews the working site before publication, keeping the loop review-oriented rather than fully automatic.

The Agent 'writes the application' and the critical transition is 'external design or running DOM -> bounded conversation context -> Agent search and reasoning -> project-file mutation -> refreshed runtime and diff -> human verification', so AI is the author of implementation. Agent directly edits local project files with automatic checkpoints for revert, and Figma/Preview/Miora inputs are materialized into file changes. Delivery exits through EdgeOne Pages, CloudBase, Cloud Studio or Lighthouse, but the DOM-to-source grounding and reverse-sync semantics are undocumented and human diff/plan review is expected at each verification step.

Installable Claude skills make AI produce standards-bound engineering artifacts ('Each builder emits a structured XLSX or related artifact') with traceability IDs and schemas as operational interfaces, so AI is the artifact author. Matching confirmation skills 'reopen the artifact, check required structure and domain rules' and produce findings plus dashboards, enabling review-driven iteration on the structured workbooks. The skills require an external agent and human orchestration per artifact, and delivery is reviewable workbooks rather than a shipped product.

Three model roles turn an objective into a runnable filesystem project: 'an orchestrator decomposes work, a sub-agent produces code, and a refiner consolidates the final file set', so AI authors the complete project. Maestro 'repeats until the orchestrator declares the task complete' and files.py creates the project under results/, giving a durable file artifact, but iteration happens inside one generation run rather than editing an existing persistent artifact afterwards. The result is served in a Streamlit iframe with no later persistence, recovery or deployment, and the last pinned activity is 2025.

Discovery 'normally creates twenty concepts across five territories' from numbered icon territories, and refinement 'keeps parents and controls visible, never recycles IDs and archives rejected rounds', so AI generates and iteratively mutates a persistent icon graph. A numbered human choice is mandatory before refinement, making human selection a hard loop step. Finalization checks the selected SVG across favicon sizes and backgrounds and renders canonical currentColor/black-white SVGs plus PNG/ICO/zip, delivering a production asset suite.

The React Flow canvas lets users author nodes/edges, but the backend 'locates nodes by the labels User Query and KnowledgeBase' and sends only query plus document text to Gemini, so the AI executes a fixed recipe rather than designing the workflow. Workflow durability is file export/import; the result is a prototype query-answer loop, not a general or shipped workflow engine.

Adeu projects Word content into Markdown and 'writes accepted changes back as native Track Changes while preserving the underlying OOXML layout', so AI edits the authoritative DOCX document in place through a Word virtual DOM. Read/search/batch-edit operations 'address document structure without exposing the model to raw XML' and ambiguous or invalid changes are blocked before mutation, with a visual diff for review. It is a focused redlining loop rather than a general document-layout generator, and human acceptance of tracked changes is part of the workflow.

All execution events are 'deterministic browser scenarios; no model or external ERP is called', so the AI does not create or change any design work in this product. Nodes cannot be reconnected and state is not persisted across reload, giving a static inspection study of operator states rather than an editable artifact. It is explicitly a visual decision/verification workspace for designing agent-control UX, not deployed automation, so authority, mutation and delivery are at the floor.

A versioned JSON op-list 'can create or edit hierarchical .kicad_sch files through atomic writes, whole-tree net-diff safety, deterministic UUIDs, backups and undo', so AI-generated operations directly mutate the persistent schematic document. KiCad and read-only Altium inputs project into one JSON model consumed by authoring, ERC-lite, intent contracts, simulation, rendering and release preflight, and dry runs/strict-net gates reveal mutation before it touches source. The native KiCad document remains the delivery authority and human engineering checks are not replaced, capping delivery and loop automation.

Generation 'advances a named project through generation while validating planned files', and distinct modify and repair routes 'apply requested changes to existing authority' and handle invalid artifacts, so AI both generates and directly mutates the persistent project file graph. Saved versions can be 'promoted back to current' via restore, and preview/export consume the promoted files rather than an unrelated caching layer. The loop is request-driven with explicit user-triggered operations and preview/export delivery rather than one-click publishing.

The skill turns 'briefs, screenshots, documents and design-system context into HTML prototypes' through a contract lifecycle of intake, plan, build, preview, 'verification and fix', so AI authors the design artifacts and iterates on them. 'Editable HTML and related source files remain authority' with a machine-readable contract and handoff manifest recording what was delivered, and validation scripts check the contract before a package is called complete. Desktop/mobile screenshots are correction evidence and delivery is export packages plus implementation handoffs.

The skill guides an external agent to 'design a constitution and operational state machine for an AI system' as separate JSON artifacts, so AI produces the governance design. 'Separate JSON schemas validate each artifact and validate_specula.py checks cross-artifact consistency', making the JSON the editable authority with validation as evidence. It is a bounded skill workflow without the broader orchestration/memory roadmap implemented, and delivery is validated JSON artifacts rather than a shipped system.

The baseline loop is deterministic: it 'scans design tokens and modes, presents a visual diff, serializes W3C Design Tokens, Style Dictionary or CSS Variables, then creates or updates a pull request' — 'the public contract does not establish that AI is needed' for it, so authority is near the bridge floor. AI participates only in the paid code-generation surface, while the ordinary governance loop is extraction plus human-reviewed merge. It delivers durable token/PR artifacts to a repository, but synchronization semantics (identity across renames, deletions, conflicts) are undocumented.

The public contract is prompt-to-component: 'the user describes a UI component and the model constructs a professional, visually consistent component inside Figma', so AI is the author of the component. 'The public page does not state how descriptions become properties, variants... whether generation modifies an existing component; how errors roll back; or whether prompts and revisions persist' — mutation and persistence semantics are unevidenced and penalized. The editable Figma component is a durable artifact the designer then edits or reuses.

Users can bring Claude or OpenAI keys into in-app panels and connect Cursor via MCP, and 'MCP operations can get state, apply operations, and save, allowing external agents to change the visible diagram', so AI can create and modify diagram content. The canvas is a projection over that file, and humans remain the primary authors of most diagrams.

The pipeline 'generates structurally different HTML wireframe candidates, renders evidence for each, rejects failures, compares survivors' with a repair pass, so AI is the author of the candidate designs from a brief. Each run directory 'retains the diagnosis, gate result, per-strategy specification, HTML wireframe, viewport screenshots, check JSON, verdicts, tournaments and final ranking', a durable decision record, with deterministic checks and model scoring automating most of the loop. Mutation is per-run candidate generation rather than editing one persistent artifact, and the winning HTML is explicitly 'not production frontend code'.

This is review governance: skills 'read schematics, PCB layouts and fabrication outputs... and decide whether a board is ready to release', so AI reviews evidence rather than authoring the board. 'KiCad files remain authoritative; reports and machine-readable findings are evidence artifacts', and diff_analysis limits re-review to changed design facts while fab_release_gate turns them into a production decision. Recurring semantic problems can be promoted to deterministic assertions, but AI does not mutate the board itself, keeping authority and mutation at the bridge/verifier level.

The Power BI report skill 'directs an external agent through discovery mutation validation and handoff while the CLI performs deterministic changes', so AI proposes the report design while the CLI executes typed operations on PBIR/TMDL source. pbir_models.py 'gives agents structured contracts instead of asking them to patch arbitrary JSON' and snapshots/restore make the source package recoverable, with versionable project files authoritative over rendered .pbix output. Full visual acceptance still depends on Microsoft Power BI Desktop, and the design flow is agent-proposal plus deterministic execution.

The design surface is 'an ordered agent roster plus a coordination strategy' that the human authors; the workflow API 'creates an execution record, hands saved agents and coordination to the orchestrator, then persists status, context and results', so AI executes as the team rather than designing the workflow. There is no visual edge editor or source export, and the creation UI exposes a smaller subset than the backend step model.

Preview compiles the selected TSX in a sandbox and 'does not become the durable source itself'; delivery stops at the iframe preview with no deployment path.

Slate makes 'generator prompts' native filmmaking artifacts in a project graph, and humans can 'lock lines against transformation' while director notes, variants and alt takes append history, so AI transforms prompt material within a human-authored project. A circled take can feed reality back, so the governed shot history is the authority, but the delivered result is prompts for a target model rather than a shipped design.

The five-agent pipeline 'synchronizes variables into design/tokens.json and tokens.css' and extracts the selected design into design.md, then layout/style agents 'build semantic HTML rather than repeatedly querying Figma', so AI produces the implementation from the Figma design.
